# Ballpark

A multi-tenant SaaS operating system for youth sports performance facility franchises, starting with an athlete-facing mobile app for kids and parents.

## Run & Operate

```bash
npm run dev          # expo start --tunnel (test on phone via Expo Go)
npm run typecheck    # tsc --noEmit
npm run lint         # eslint
```

`npm install` requires `--legacy-peer-deps`. Real testing is on a physical phone via Expo Go. Replit Deployments are not used; production ships through Expo EAS.

**Portal demo data:**

```bash
node scripts/seed-portal-demo-data.mjs    # seed 4 coaches, 15 families/kids, 15 memberships,
                                           # 12-month payment history, 20 today's bookings,
                                           # 60 historical bookings, 5 products, points & orders.
                                           # Idempotent — safe to re-run.

node scripts/delete-portal-seed-data.mjs  # remove every seeded record by its deterministic UUID
                                           # (5eed… namespace). Deletes in reverse FK order:
                                           # orders → points_ledger → bookings → payment_events →
                                           # memberships → kids → family/coach auth users (which
                                           # cascade-delete the families/coaches rows) → products.
                                           # Run before going to production.
```

**CEO demo scenario (Marcus Rivera end-to-end story):**

Full demo script and leave-behind doc: `docs/DEMO_SCRIPT.md` · `docs/DEMO_LEAVE_BEHIND.md`

```bash
node scripts/seed-demo-scenario.mjs       # Seed a scripted hero story: Marcus Rivera (14U, 847 pts,
                                           # rank #3), Coach Mike message, pending + reviewed drills,
                                           # upcoming Friday lesson, today's HitTrax session (88.4 mph),
                                           # personal best, 2 achievements, 8-kid leaderboard, 3 store
                                           # products, 1 past order, 12 dashboard bookings across 3
                                           # coaches. Requires provision-coach-mike.mjs for coach-specific
                                           # rows. Uses de00… UUID namespace — safe to combine with
                                           # seed-portal-demo-data.mjs (5eed… namespace). Idempotent.

node scripts/delete-demo-scenario.mjs     # Remove every record seeded by seed-demo-scenario.mjs.
                                           # Deletes in reverse FK order: orders → kid_achievements →
                                           # points_ledger → assignments → coach_messages → bookings →
                                           # sessions → personal_bests → memberships → kids → products →
                                           # family/peer auth users → demo coach auth users.
                                           # Coach Mike is NOT deleted (provisioned separately).
```

**Coach Mike sessions (for Sessions tab testing):**

```bash
node scripts/seed-coach-mike-sessions.mjs   # Insert 6 confirmed upcoming bookings for Coach Mike
                                             # spread across the next 15 days (days +1, +3, +5, +8,
                                             # +11, +14), across Marcus Rivera, Jaylen Carter, and
                                             # Sofia Martinez. Times rotate 9 AM / 11 AM / 2 PM / 4 PM.
                                             # Requires provision-coach-mike.mjs + seed-demo-scenario.mjs.
                                             # Uses c0ac… UUID namespace. Idempotent — safe to re-run.

node scripts/delete-coach-mike-sessions.mjs # Remove the 6 bookings inserted by seed-coach-mike-sessions.mjs
                                             # (c0ac0006-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 … 000000000006).
```

**Environment Variables:**

- `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`, `EXPO_PUBLIC_TENANT_SLUG=infinitehitting`
- `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (server-side only)
- `EXPO_PUBLIC_AUTH_REDIRECT_HOST` (optional; when set, signup confirmations redirect to `https://{host}/auth/callback` and `app.config.js` registers iOS/Android associated domains. Unset → falls back to `ballpark://` scheme.)
- Edge Function secrets (set via `npx supabase secrets set`): `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM_EMAIL`, `MUX_TOKEN_ID`, `MUX_TOKEN_SECRET`, `MUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `HITTRAX_BASE_URL`, `HITTRAX_PARTNER_ID`, `HITTRAX_API_KEY`, `HITTRAX_CONTENT_TYPE`.
- Stripe Connect (portal env vars): `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, `STRIPE_CONNECT_CLIENT_ID`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. Also set `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` and `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` as Supabase Edge Function secrets via `npx supabase secrets set`. See `docs/STRIPE_SETUP.md` for the full runbook.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_PORTAL_URL` — **required for Stripe Connect** (production Replit env var, e.g. `https://ballpark-app.replit.app`). The three Stripe Connect routes (`/api/stripe/connect/start`, `/api/stripe/connect/callback`, `/api/stripe/connect/refresh`) use this as the explicit public origin for building `return_url` and `refresh_url` values sent to Stripe. When unset, the routes fall back to `REPLIT_DEV_DOMAIN` then x-forwarded-host headers — set this in production so the origin is always deterministic regardless of proxy headers.

## Stack

React Native / Expo SDK 54 / React 19 / TypeScript (strict) on mobile. Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage + Realtime + Edge Functions) on the backend. Stripe Connect for payments, Mux for video, Resend for email. Zustand (client state) + TanStack Query (server state). React Hook Form + Zod. StyleSheet + design tokens. Built with Expo EAS.

## Where things live

- `/src` — `screens/{Name}/` (Name.tsx + styles.ts + types.ts + components/), `components/{ui,layout,feature}/`, `api/` (one file per resource), `store/`, `theme/`, `lib/supabase.ts`, `types/database.ts` (generated)
- `/supabase` — `migrations/`, `functions/`, `seed/`
- Path aliases (`@/*` → `src/*`) in `tsconfig.json` and `babel.config.js`.
- `/portal` — Next.js admin portal.
- `/docs` — PRD, DESIGN, ARCHITECTURE, ROADMAP, PROMPTS, HITTRAX_INTEGRATION, TENANT_ISOLATION_AUDIT. **Authoritative architecture: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md §9`.**

## Architecture decisions

- **Tenancy:** UUID `tenant_id` everywhere; `slug` is routing-only. Infinite Hitting = `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`. JWT custom claim is `app_role` (not the reserved `role`), injected via Supabase's Custom Access Token Hook. UI enforces one kid per family for v0.5; schema supports many.
- **Coach provisioning:** admin-created via Supabase Admin API with `raw_user_meta_data.app_role='coach'`; `handle_new_user` trigger branches on `app_role`. No in-app coach signup. Reference: `scripts/provision-coach-mike.mjs`.
- **Stripe Connect:** onboarding handled out-of-band via Stripe-hosted dashboards; the app only consumes `stripe_account_id`.
- **Mux Webhook (`mux-webhook`):** deployed `--no-verify-jwt`; auth is `Mux-Signature` HMAC vs `MUX_WEBHOOK_SECRET` (300s replay window). Idempotent on `videos.mux_asset_id` UNIQUE — UPDATE only, never INSERT. Unknown asset/upload ids → 503 to force Mux retry.
- **Coach video notifications:** push (Expo) + email (Resend) fire from `mux-webhook` on `video.asset.ready` for `purpose='coach_message'`, best-effort via `Promise.allSettled`. Replay path intentionally does NOT fan out — only the first ready-update sends. Never fired from `mux-create-upload` or the client.
- **`device_tokens`:** UNIQUE on `(user_id, expo_push_token)` — never global. Same physical device can switch accounts (sibling on Expo Go) without 409. `src/services/notifications.ts:upsertDeviceToken` also DELETEs other rows for that token belonging to a different user.
- **HitTrax pipeline (v0.7):** five Edge Functions split by trust boundary — `hittrax-associate`/`hittrax-disconnect` (parent JWT), `hittrax-poll` (service-role, pg_cron every 2 min), `hittrax-registration-complete`/`hittrax-forget` (`--no-verify-jwt`, constant-time PartnerID+APIKey check). Per-user HitTrax password lives in `kid_capture_links.third_party_user_password` and is NEVER returned to the client. Polling cursor `last_polled_through` only advances on successful UPSERT batch (30s safety slack on `EndDate`). Full runbook: `docs/HITTRAX_INTEGRATION.md`.

## Product

- Auth (signup, sign-in, sign-out from parent Me + coach home), kid registration, Home dashboard
- Booking system (private / group / cage), upcoming + past
- Coach ↔ family video messaging (Mux pipeline both directions, full-screen playback marks viewed)
- Earn (Rewards / Store / Ranks / Rules) with 8-char redemption codes + QR + live leaderboard
- Drill assignments (coach assigns, parent submits, coach reviews 1–5★ + feedback)
- Achievements catalog with auto-grants + bonus points + push fan-out
- Profile screen with PRs grid, achievements grid, settings
- Train library (HQ-curated training videos)
- HitTrax integration (auto-imported sessions/swings/PRs)

### v0.7 #122 — Profile / Achievements / Leaderboard polish / QR codes (2026-05-09)
Migration `20260511000000_v07_achievements_and_fulfillment.sql`: `achievements` catalog (12 seeded) + `kid_achievements` log + `_grant_achievement(kid, key)` SECURITY DEFINER fn that writes a `points_ledger reason='achievement_bonus'` bonus and pings `notify-achievement` via pg_net. Per-source-table grant triggers on `points_ledger` / `swings` / `personal_bests` / `orders` / `coach_messages` / `assignments`. `mark_redemption_fulfilled(p_code)` admin-gated RPC (FOR UPDATE-locks the order, gates on `payment_method='points'` AND `status='ordered'`). New mobile `ProfileScreen` (`src/screens/Me/ProfileScreen.tsx`) replaces `MeScreen`; rebuilt `RanksScreen` with podium + `get_kid_weekly_rank_delta` RPC; `react-native-qrcode-svg` on `RewardRedeemScreen`. Three new Edge Functions (`notify-achievement`, `notify-assignment-reviewed`, `notify-leaderboard-weekly`) with durable idempotency via `notification_log`. Portal `/admin/redemptions` with `<QRScanner />` (html5-qrcode). **Operator note:** for trigger pg_net push to fire, set `app.settings.supabase_url` + `app.settings.service_role_key` GUCs once per env, then `SELECT pg_reload_conf()`. Migration tolerates them being absent.

### v0.7 #121 — Train library + Video Player (2026-05-09)
Migrations `20260510000000` + `20260510000001`: `training_videos` catalog + `training_video_views` log + `record_training_view(video_id, kid_id)` RPC with **server-side per-session dedupe** (≤1 view-count increment per kid/video per 30 min). RLS: tenant members SELECT published; admins SELECT drafts + own all writes. `videos.purpose` extended with `'training'`. Mobile `TrainStackNavigator` (TrainHome + TrainingVideoPlayer): filter chips, featured hero, Continue Watching from AsyncStorage (`ballpark.trainingProgress.v1.{kidId}`), 2-col grid. Player throttles position writes ~3s, fires `record_training_view` once per mount. Portal `/admin/training-videos` with category+status filters and Mux Direct Upload via `/api/admin/training-uploads` proxy.

### v0.7 #120 — Share Card + Send Video to Coach (2026-05-09)
Migration `20260509000000_v07_parent_to_coach_messages.sql`: `videos.purpose` += `'parent_to_coach'`; `coach_messages.{label, sender_display}`; six new RLS policies for bidirectional thread. `mux-create-upload` branches on `purpose` (coach/drill require `app_role='coach'`, parent_to_coach requires `app_role='parent'`). Share Card: dual-render pattern in `ShareCardScreen` (220px on-screen preview + off-screen 1080×1920 view that `react-native-view-shot` captures). Send-to-coach: 4-step composer in `SendVideoToCoachScreen`. Bidirectional thread in `MessageThreadScreen` (parent gold-on-dark right, coach dark-on-gold left). Coach push fired SERVER-SIDE from `mux-webhook` `fanOutParentToCoachNotifications` for `purpose='parent_to_coach'`.

### v0.7 #119 — Videos surface + favorites (2026-05-08)
Migration `20260508080000_v07_kid_swing_favorites.sql`: `kid_swing_favorites UNIQUE(kid_id, swing_id)` + `toggle_swing_favorite(p_swing_id)` SECURITY DEFINER RPC (derives `kid_id`+`tenant_id` from the swing row; never trusts client params). Optimistic `useToggleFavorite`. Originally introduced a 7-tab nav with dedicated Videos/Train/Rewards/Ranks tabs — rolled back in #135 but the underlying screens (`SwingDetail`, `SessionDetail`) are reused under WorkStack. Coach assigns drill (title, notes, optional Mux drill video, duration, due date, point reward default 25). Parent sees pending on Home + Work, taps "Mark as done" → +25 pts via SECURITY DEFINER RPC. Run `node scripts/audit-tenant-isolation.mjs 'AuditFixtures2026!'` (exit 0 = PASS). One-time setup per env: `node scripts/provision-audit-fixtures.mjs 'AuditFixtures2026!'` then `node scripts/seed-audit-rows.mjs`. Full results, methodology, migration SQL, defence-in-depth notes: **`docs/TENANT_ISOLATION_AUDIT.md`**.

## v0.5 Deferred (intentional, still relevant)

- **Stripe Connect card checkout** for purchase-only / dual-priced store items. Schema supports it (`orders.payment_method='card'`, `amount_paid_cents`, `stripe_payment_intent_id`); UI today points the parent at the front desk.
- **Nightly leaderboard snapshot** — Ranks queries `kids` live (top 50 by `points_balance`); fine for one tenant, will need a snapshot table at scale.

## Generated types caveat (recurring)

`src/types/database.ts` is regenerated by `scripts/post-merge.sh` after each migration runs in CI. New tables/RPCs introduced in v0.7 (`training_videos`, `record_training_view`, `achievements`, `kid_achievements`, `mark_redemption_fulfilled`, `_grant_achievement`, `coach_messages.{label,sender_display}`) are accessed via `SupabaseClient` cast (the un-typed client, **not `any`**) until the next regen. Source of truth remains the migrations + RPC SQL signatures.

## Gotchas

- `npm install` requires `--legacy-peer-deps` (also `npx expo install <pkg> -- --legacy-peer-deps`).
- The Replit preview pane is not for mobile testing — use Expo Go on a physical device.
- Supabase email confirmation: signups pass `emailRedirectTo = ballpark:///auth/callback` (PKCE). Add that URL to Supabase Auth → URL Configuration → Redirect URLs allow-list per env.
- Stale JWTs after schema changes: sign out + back in to refresh tokens.
- Tables created via raw SQL may lack default GRANTs; explicit `GRANT` required.
- `err instanceof Error` is wrong for `PostgrestError`/`AuthError`; use `errorMessage(err)` from `src/utils/error.ts`.
- Metro must NOT watch `.local/` — Replit churns dirs there constantly. Exclusions in `metro.config.js` `resolver.blockList`. Never put platform-managed dirs under `src/`.
- `Expo dev (proxy)` workflow MUST be `outputType: "console"` (not `webview`). Metro is a packager — a bare `GET /` from a browser yields `CommandError: Must specify "expo-platform" header` (502 in canvas iframe). Test only via Expo Go QR in console.
- **Expo Go physical device (Replit sandbox architecture):** `ngrok` and LAN tunnels are blocked in Replit. The durable fix: `portal/next.config.ts` rewrites any request carrying `expo-platform` header to `http://localhost:8080` (Metro). `portal/middleware.ts` short-circuits Supabase auth for `expo-platform` requests so they reach the rewrite layer. Expo dev (proxy) workflow uses `EXPO_MANIFEST_PROXY_URL="https://$REPLIT_DEV_DOMAIN"` (no port) so the QR code is `exp://[dev-domain]` (→ portal → Metro). **Use `REPLIT_DEV_DOMAIN`, NOT `REPLIT_EXPO_DEV_DOMAIN`** — the `expo.riker.replit.dev` subdomain does not reliably route to the portal. Do NOT add a port number. Do NOT use `--clear` on `expo start` (clears cache = slow cold start on every restart). Always re-scan the QR after restarting the workflow. **Portal dev workflow must run on port 5000** (`cd portal && npm run dev -- -p 5000`) as the webview entry point — do not revert to port 3000 or the preview pane and Expo Go routing both break.
- Editing `supabase/functions/<name>/` does NOT change what Supabase serves until `npx supabase functions deploy <name>` runs. The three webhook-style fns (`mux-webhook`, `hittrax-registration-complete`, `hittrax-forget`) need `--no-verify-jwt`. `scripts/post-merge.sh` re-deploys all of them automatically after every task merge.
- HitTrax keys (`HITTRAX_PARTNER_ID`, `HITTRAX_API_KEY`, `HITTRAX_BASE_URL`) — until set, every HitTrax fn returns `503 hittrax_not_configured`. Local exercise: `node scripts/replay-hittrax-fixture.mjs <kid_uuid>` against `_shared/fixtures/hittrax-sample.json`.

# CLAUDE.md

This file is automatically read by AI assistants (Replit Agent, Claude Code) on every session. It provides essential context. **Read this first, then refer to `/docs` for deeper information.**

---

## What This Project Is

**Ballpark** is a multi-tenant SaaS operating system for youth sports performance facility franchises. The anchor customer is **Infinite Hitting**, a 17-location youth baseball franchise migrating off MindBody.

**The mission:** Replace MindBody as the operating system for youth sports facilities. Win on five wedges: kid-facing engagement, HitTrax integration, franchise-native architecture, gamification, and unified lead-to-member CRM.

**What we are building first (v0.1 - v0.5):** The athlete-facing mobile app for kids and parents. NOT the operations portal. NOT the AI layer. NOT the franchisor dashboard. Those come after the athlete app ships.

---

## Development Environment

This project lives on **Replit** as a shared multi-developer workspace.

- Multiple developers may be active at the same time
- Code, environment variables, and dev server are shared
- All work pushed to GitHub for backup, branching, and code review
- Expo dev server runs in Replit's container, exposed via tunnel mode for phone testing

---

## Tech Stack (LOCKED — do not deviate)

- **Mobile app:** React Native via Expo (TypeScript, strict mode)
- **Backend:** Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Storage + Edge Functions)
- **Payments:** Stripe Connect (Express accounts per location)
- **Video:** Mux (uploads, playback, analytics)
- **SMS:** Twilio
- **Email:** Resend
- **LLM:** Anthropic Claude API (Sonnet for most, Opus for parent reports)
- **State management:** Zustand for client state, TanStack Query for server state
- **Styling:** StyleSheet + design tokens from `/src/theme/tokens.ts` (do not introduce styled-components, Tailwind RN, or NativeWind)
- **Forms:** React Hook Form + Zod validation
- **Testing:** Jest for unit, Detox for E2E (deferred to v0.4+)
- **Builds:** Expo EAS for production builds (Replit can't build native binaries)

## Code Conventions

### TypeScript
- Strict mode always on. No `any` unless absolutely necessary, and document why.
- All component props are typed as interfaces, not types (easier to extend).
- Prefer named exports over default exports for components.

### Naming
- Files: kebab-case for utility files, PascalCase for component files (`UserCard.tsx`)
- Components: PascalCase (`UserCard`, not `userCard`)
- Functions: camelCase (`getUserById`)
- Constants: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE (`API_BASE_URL`)
- Database tables: snake_case (`session_swings`)
- API endpoints: kebab-case (`/api/session-swings`)

### Imports
- Absolute imports via path aliases (`@/components/Button`, not `../../components/Button`)
- Group order: React → third-party → internal absolute → relative → types → styles

### Components
- Functional components with hooks, never class components
- One component per file
- Co-locate styles in `styles.ts` next to the component
- Co-locate types in `types.ts` next to the component (or inline if small)

### Database
- Every table has `id` (uuid), `created_at`, `updated_at`
- Every record is scoped to `tenant_id` (franchise) where applicable
- Use Row Level Security (RLS) for all tables — no exceptions
- Use Supabase migrations for ALL schema changes — never modify live DB directly

---

## Key Commands (Replit-specific)

### In the Replit Shell

```bash
# Development — uses tunnel mode so phones can connect via Expo Go
npm run dev                 # Configured to run `npx expo start --tunnel`

# Or directly:
npx expo start --tunnel     # Tunnel mode (works for phones outside Replit's network)
npx expo start --lan        # LAN mode (only works if phone is on same network as Replit, usually doesn't)

# Database
npx supabase migration new <name>
npx supabase db push        # Push migrations to remote Supabase
npx supabase gen types typescript --linked > src/types/database.ts

# Testing
npm test                    # Unit tests
npm run typecheck           # TypeScript check (must pass before commit)
npm run lint                # ESLint check (must pass before commit)
```

### Environment Variables

In Replit, environment variables are set via **Tools → Secrets**, not `.env` files. The `.env.example` shows what keys to add.

To access in code:
```typescript
process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL  // Bundled into app, can be public
process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_KEY      // Server-side only, never bundled
```

Note: Expo only bundles env vars prefixed with `EXPO_PUBLIC_` into the app. Anything else is server-side (used by Edge Functions).

## ALWAYS Do This

1. **Read `/docs/PRD.md`** before working on any feature for the first time
2. **Read `/docs/DESIGN.md`** before building any UI component
3. **Reference `/design/InfiniteHittingApp.jsx`** for visual specs of the athlete app
4. **Use planning mode first** — show plan, wait for approval, then execute
5. **Write the database migration BEFORE the API endpoint BEFORE the UI**
6. **Match the prototype design EXACTLY** unless explicitly told to deviate
7. **Use design tokens from `/src/theme/tokens.ts`** — never hardcode colors, fonts, or spacing
8. **Run `npm run typecheck` before suggesting code is complete**
9. **Commit incrementally** with conventional commit messages (`feat:`, `fix:`, `chore:`)
10. **Verify Supabase RLS policies are in place** for any new table
11. **Check git branch before committing** — main branch should require PRs

---

## NEVER Do This

1. **NEVER hardcode credentials, API keys, or secrets** in code — use Replit Secrets
2. **NEVER skip TypeScript types** with `any` without explicit justification
3. **NEVER bypass RLS policies** by using the service role key in client code
4. **NEVER use AsyncStorage for sensitive data** — use Expo SecureStore
5. **NEVER make architectural decisions on the fly** — they belong in `/docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
6. **NEVER introduce a new dependency** without checking if existing tools cover the need
7. **NEVER mix the operations portal code into the mobile app** — they're separate apps
8. **NEVER modify production database directly** — always use migrations
9. **NEVER deploy without running typecheck and lint locally first**
10. **NEVER guess at the design** — refer to the prototype files in `/design`
11. **NEVER force-push to shared branches** — coordinate with team

## Replit-Specific Workflow Notes

### Running the Expo dev server in shared workspace

Only ONE developer should run `npm run dev` at a time. If multiple people start it, you'll get port conflicts.

Convention: announce in team chat when starting/stopping dev server.

### Working with Replit Agent vs Claude Code

This project uses BOTH AI tools intentionally. Use them for different things:

**Replit Agent** (fast, integrated, good at scaffolding):
- "Set up a new Expo project with TypeScript"
- "Create a Supabase migration with these tables"
- "Add a new screen file with placeholder content"
- "Install these dependencies"
- "Run this command and tell me what happens"

**Claude Code in terminal** (precise, careful, follows conventions):
- "Refactor this component to match the prototype exactly"
- "Implement this feature according to /docs/PRD.md section X"
- "This code violates a convention from CLAUDE.md — fix it"
- "Read these files and propose a careful plan before writing code"

The pattern: Agent for skeleton → Claude Code for refinement. Don't have them edit the same file at the same time.

### Git workflow in shared Replit

- All real work happens in feature branches
- Push to GitHub frequently (every working state)
- Use PRs for code review before merging to main
- Replit's auto-save can create merge conflicts — discipline matters
- Pull from GitHub at the start of each work session

/**
 * Dynamic Expo config.
 *
 * Wraps the static `app.json` so we can wire up universal links / Android
 * App Links for the Supabase email-confirmation flow without hard-coding the
 * production domain. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_AUTH_REDIRECT_HOST` in EAS / Replit
 * Secrets to e.g. `app.ballpark.com`. When unset (local dev / Expo Go) the
 * app falls back to the `ballpark://` custom scheme registered in app.json,
 * which is enough for round-tripping confirmation emails on a personal
 * device but won't work for users who don't yet have the app installed.
 */

const base = require("./app.json");

module.exports = () => {
  const config = JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(base));
  const expo = config.expo;
  const authHost = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_AUTH_REDIRECT_HOST;

  // EAS config
  expo.owner = "harjinderharry";
  expo.extra = expo.extra ?? {};
  expo.extra.eas = expo.extra.eas ?? {};
  expo.extra.eas.projectId = "4ce07796-bc3a-4c22-b3a1-502a1d5d6dfc";

  // Universal links / deep links
  if (authHost) {
    expo.ios = expo.ios ?? {};
    expo.ios.associatedDomains = Array.from(
      new Set([...(expo.ios.associatedDomains ?? []), `applinks:${authHost}`]),
    );

    expo.android = expo.android ?? {};
    expo.android.intentFilters = [
      ...(expo.android.intentFilters ?? []),
      {
        action: "VIEW",
        autoVerify: true,
        category: ["DEFAULT", "BROWSABLE"],
        data: [
          {
            scheme: "https",
            host: authHost,
            pathPrefix: "/auth/callback",
          },
        ],
      },
    ];
  }

  return config;
};

FILE: metro.config.js
=================================================================================
const { getDefaultConfig } = require('expo/metro-config');
const path = require('path');

const escape = (str) => str.replace(/[.*+?^${}()|[\]\\]/g, '\\$&');

const projectRoot = __dirname;
const config = getDefaultConfig(projectRoot);

const blockedDirs = [
  '.local',
  '.git',
  '.cache',
  '.upm',
  '.config',
  'attached_assets',
  path.join('supabase', '.branches'),
  path.join('supabase', '.temp'),
  path.join('node_modules', '.cache'),
  // Exclude pnpm's content-addressable store from Metro's file map.
  // Top-level node_modules/<pkg> symlinks are still visible; Metro
  // follows them via unstable_enableSymlinks (direct fs reads), so
  // module resolution is unaffected. Excluding this prevents Watchman
  // from inotify-watching the 941-package .pnpm tree and hitting the
  // container's watch-fd limit (ENOSPC).
  path.join('node_modules', '.pnpm'),
];

const blockListPatterns = [
  ...blockedDirs.map(
    (dir) =>
      new RegExp(`^${escape(path.join(projectRoot, dir))}(?:[\\/].*)?$`),
  ),
  new RegExp(`^${escape(projectRoot)}[\\/].*[\\/]\\.old-[^\\/]+(?:[\\/].*)?$`),
];

// watchFolders: explicitly list every source root so Watchman's active
// subscription covers only real source trees.  node_modules itself is
// still reachable for resolution via nodeModulesPaths below.
config.watchFolders = [
  projectRoot,
  path.join(projectRoot, 'src'),
  path.join(projectRoot, 'supabase', 'functions'),
];

config.resolver = config.resolver || {};
config.resolver.blockList = blockListPatterns;

// Follow pnpm symlinks (node_modules/<pkg> → .pnpm/…) via direct fs
// reads rather than requiring Watchman to have crawled the target.
config.resolver.unstable_enableSymlinks = true;

// Explicit module roots so the resolver never needs to walk upward
// through directories that Watchman hasn't indexed.
config.resolver.nodeModulesPaths = [path.join(projectRoot, 'node_modules')];

config.watcher = config.watcher || {};
config.watcher.healthCheck = {
  ...(config.watcher.healthCheck || {}),
  enabled: false,
};

module.exports = config;

# Architecture & Technical Decisions

> Authoritative technical reference. Every decision documented here is binding for v0.1-v0.5 unless explicitly revisited.

---

## 1. Stack Overview

```
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│       React Native + Expo App (mobile)      │
│  Development: Replit (shared workspace)     │
│  Testing: Expo Go on phones via tunnel      │
│  Production builds: Expo EAS (cloud)        │
└─────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                  │
                  ▼
┌────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              Supabase                        │
│  • Postgres (data)                           │
│  • Auth (JWT, email/password)                │
│  • Storage (avatars, message attachments)    │
│  • Realtime (messages, leaderboards)         │
│  • Edge Functions (custom server logic)      │
└─────────────────┬──────────────────────────┘
                  │
   ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
   ▼              ▼              ▼
┌────────┐  ┌──────────┐  ┌──────────┐
│ Stripe │  │   Mux    │  │  Twilio  │
│Connect │  │ (videos) │  │  (SMS)   │
└────────┘  └──────────┘  └──────────┘
            ▼
       ┌──────────┐
       │  Resend  │
       │ (email)  │
       └──────────┘
```

---

## 2. Replit-Specific Architecture Notes

### Why Replit doesn't host the app itself

Replit hosts the **development environment** — the code, the build tools, the dev server. But the actual production app isn't deployed from Replit.

- **Mobile app:** Production builds via Expo EAS Build (cloud builds), distributed via TestFlight (iOS) and Play Store (Android)
- **Edge Functions:** Deployed to Supabase, not Replit
- **Database:** Hosted on Supabase, not Replit

Replit is the editor + dev environment. Everything else lives elsewhere.

### Why this matters
- Replit Deployments are not used for this project
- Production environment variables live in Supabase (Edge Functions) and EAS (mobile)
- Replit Secrets are for development only

---

## 3. Multi-Tenant Architecture

### The model

Every meaningful record is tenant-scoped via a `tenant_id` column. **`tenant_id` is always a UUID** — never a slug. Infinite Hitting's tenant UUID is hardcoded for predictable local dev: `00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001`. The human-readable slug (`'infinitehitting'`) lives in `tenants.slug` as a separate column for URL routing only. JWT custom claims always carry the UUID.

### Tenant resolution

For v0.x: tenant is determined by app build (each franchise gets a branded build with `EXPO_PUBLIC_TENANT_SLUG` baked in).

For v1.x: support runtime tenant detection from subdomain or magic link.

### Data isolation

**Row-Level Security (RLS) is mandatory on every table.** Standard policy template:

```sql
-- Example RLS policy on `bookings` table
CREATE POLICY "tenant_isolation" ON bookings
  FOR ALL
  USING (tenant_id = (auth.jwt() ->> 'tenant_id')::uuid);

-- Family members can only see their own kids' bookings
CREATE POLICY "family_can_see_own_bookings" ON bookings
  FOR SELECT
  USING (kid_id IN (
    SELECT id FROM kids WHERE family_id IN (
      SELECT id FROM families WHERE parent_user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  ));
```

### Service role usage

The service role key bypasses RLS. **Use ONLY in:**
- Edge functions (server-side)
- Admin scripts
- Migrations and seeds

**NEVER use the service role key in the mobile app.** The mobile app uses the anon key + JWT.

---

## 4. Authentication Architecture

### Flow

```
1. Parent signs up (email + password) via Supabase Auth
2. A trigger on auth.users INSERT calls handle_new_user() which:
   - Creates a row in `families` with parent_user_id = NEW.id
   - Sets tenant_id from EXPO_PUBLIC_TENANT_SLUG → tenant lookup
3. A Supabase Auth Hook (Custom Access Token Hook) injects JWT
   custom claims (tenant_id, family_id, role) on every token issuance
4. Parent adds a kid → creates row in `kids` table
5. App switches to "kid mode" via in-app toggle (no separate auth)
6. JWT refreshed every hour automatically by Supabase client
```

### Custom JWT claims

After signup, the JWT includes:

```json
{
  "sub": "auth-user-uuid",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-uuid",
  "family_id": "family-uuid",
  "role": "parent",
  "exp": 1234567890
}
```

**Implementation:** Use Supabase's Custom Access Token Hook (a Postgres function registered under Auth → Hooks in the Supabase dashboard). A plain trigger on `auth.users` cannot inject claims into the JWT — it can only modify table data. The Custom Access Token Hook receives the default claims and returns the augmented set. The hook function looks up `family_id` and `tenant_id` from the `families` table by `auth.uid()` and merges them into the claims payload.

### Session storage

- Use `expo-secure-store` (NOT AsyncStorage) for any secret-grade data
- Supabase session auto-refresh enabled
- On app launch: check session, restore if valid, redirect to login if not

### Kid mode (no separate auth)

In v0.x, kids do NOT have their own login. The parent's account hosts kid profiles. The app UI switches to "kid mode" via an in-app profile selector. All data ownership stays with the parent for COPPA compliance.

---

## 5. Payments Architecture (Stripe Connect)

### Account model

- **Platform account:** Ballpark (us). Receives application fees from every transaction.
- **Connected accounts:** Each franchise location has a Stripe Connect Express account.
- **Customers:** Each family is a Stripe Customer object on the location's connected account.

### Why Stripe Connect Express

- Fastest to onboard (Stripe handles KYC)
- We control the customer experience
- Application fees automate franchise royalty collection at the transaction level

### Transaction flow (recurring membership example)

```
1. Parent enters card details in app
2. Card tokenized via Stripe.js, sent to backend
3. Backend creates PaymentIntent on the LOCATION's connected account:
   - amount: $280.00
   - application_fee_amount: $16.80 (6% royalty)
   - on_behalf_of: location_stripe_account_id
4. Money flows: parent → location's connected account
5. Royalty automatically split: $263.20 to location, $16.80 to platform
6. Platform routes royalty to franchisor's account (configurable)
```

### Royalty collection models

**Per-transaction (default):** As above. Instant split.

**Monthly aggregate (alternative):** Some franchise agreements don't support per-transaction royalties. In this case:
- Location keeps 100% of transaction
- Backend calculates monthly royalty from prior-month gross
- Auto-debits the location's account on configured day
- Generates statement for franchisor visibility

Configurable per tenant in `tenants.royalty_config` JSONB column.

### Stripe webhooks

Critical webhooks to handle:

- `payment_intent.succeeded` → mark booking/order as paid
- `payment_intent.payment_failed` → mark for AI layer retry (when AI layer ships)
- `charge.refunded` → update order status
- `account.updated` → update connected account onboarding status
- `customer.subscription.created/updated/deleted` → recurring membership state

Handled via Supabase Edge Function endpoint `/api/stripe-webhook` with Stripe signature verification.

**Important for Replit dev:** Webhooks need a public URL. In dev, configure Stripe to point to your Supabase Edge Function URL (which is always public), NOT to your Replit URL. Edge Functions handle webhooks for both dev and prod.

---

## 6. Video Architecture (Mux)

### Why Mux

- Direct uploads from mobile via Mux upload SDK (chunked, resumable)
- HLS playback URLs ready instantly after upload
- Per-second pricing (no minimum durations)
- Analytics and engagement metrics built-in
- Supports auto-thumbnail generation

### Upload flow

```
1. App requests upload URL: POST /functions/get-mux-upload-url
   Edge function creates Mux Direct Upload, returns upload URL + asset ID
2. App uploads video file directly to Mux (chunked)
3. Mux processes asynchronously
4. App stores `asset_id` in DB record (assignments, messages, swings)
5. Mux webhook fires `video.asset.ready`:
   - Updates DB record with `playback_id` and `duration_seconds`
   - Notifies coach if it's a homework submission (via Supabase realtime)
```

### Playback

```typescript
// In React Native, use react-native-video with HLS URL
const hlsUrl = `https://stream.mux.com/${playbackId}.m3u8`;

<Video
  source={{ uri: hlsUrl }}
  style={styles.video}
  controls
  resizeMode="contain"
/>
```

### Storage redundancy

Mux is the source of truth for video. We do NOT store video files in Supabase Storage. Supabase Storage is only for:
- User avatars
- Brand assets (tenant logos)
- Static images

---

## 7. Messaging Architecture

### Real-time messages

Uses Supabase Realtime on the `messages` table. The mobile app subscribes to:

```typescript
const channel = supabase
  .channel(`thread:${threadId}`)
  .on('postgres_changes', {
    event: 'INSERT',
    schema: 'public',
    table: 'messages',
    filter: `thread_id=eq.${threadId}`,
  }, handleNewMessage)
  .subscribe();
```

Cleanup on unmount: `supabase.removeChannel(channel)`.

### Send flow (text)

```
1. Optimistically render message in UI
2. Insert into `messages` table via Supabase client
3. Trigger updates `message_threads.last_message_at`
4. Realtime fires for coach's app/portal
5. If insert fails, mark message as "failed" in UI, allow retry
```

### Send flow (video)

```
1. User taps camera → records or picks video
2. App requests Mux upload URL (Edge Function)
3. App uploads to Mux (show progress UI)
4. On Mux upload complete → insert message with asset_id, status='processing'
5. UI shows message with "Processing..." overlay
6. Mux webhook → update message with playback_id, status='ready'
7. Realtime fires → recipient's UI updates
```

### Read receipts

Deferred to v1.0. For v0.x, just track `unread_count` on the thread for badge display.

---

## 8. State Management

### Layers

- **Server state:** TanStack Query (React Query) — handles caching, refetching, optimistic updates for ALL Supabase data
- **Client state:** Zustand — for UI state that doesn't belong on the server (modals, current view, form drafts)
- **Form state:** React Hook Form + Zod — for ALL form inputs

### Patterns

**Don't use Redux.** Don't use Context for global state. Don't use prop drilling for shared state.

**Server state goes in TanStack Query:**

```typescript
// /src/api/bookings.ts
export const useUpcomingBookings = (kidId: string) => {
  return useQuery({
    queryKey: ['bookings', 'upcoming', kidId],
    queryFn: () => api.bookings.getUpcoming(kidId),
    staleTime: 30 * 1000,
  });
};
```

**Client state goes in Zustand:**

```typescript
// /src/store/uiStore.ts
import { create } from 'zustand';

interface UIState {
  isFilterModalOpen: boolean;
  setFilterModalOpen: (open: boolean) => void;
}

export const useUIStore = create<UIState>((set) => ({
  isFilterModalOpen: false,
  setFilterModalOpen: (open) => set({ isFilterModalOpen: open }),
}));
```

## 11. RLS Policy Patterns

Every table needs RLS. Here are the standard policies:

### Tenant-scoped tables

```sql
ALTER TABLE bookings ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;

-- Tenant isolation (read)
CREATE POLICY "users_see_own_tenant_bookings" ON bookings
  FOR SELECT
  USING (tenant_id = (auth.jwt() ->> 'tenant_id')::uuid);

-- Family members can only see their own kids' data
CREATE POLICY "family_sees_own_bookings" ON bookings
  FOR SELECT
  USING (
    kid_id IN (
      SELECT k.id FROM kids k
      JOIN families f ON k.family_id = f.id
      WHERE f.parent_user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- Coaches can see bookings at their location
CREATE POLICY "coach_sees_location_bookings" ON bookings
  FOR SELECT
  USING (
    coach_id IN (
      SELECT id FROM coaches WHERE user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );

-- Family can create bookings for their own kids
CREATE POLICY "family_can_create_bookings" ON bookings
  FOR INSERT
  WITH CHECK (
    kid_id IN (
      SELECT k.id FROM kids k
      JOIN families f ON k.family_id = f.id
      WHERE f.parent_user_id = auth.uid()
    )
  );
```

---

## 12. Edge Functions Architecture

Edge functions handle:
- Stripe webhook verification
- Mux upload URL generation (signed)
- Sensitive operations requiring service role
- Multi-step transactional logic
- Future: AI layer SMS handling

Pattern:

```typescript
// /supabase/functions/get-mux-upload-url/index.ts
import { serve } from 'https://deno.land/std/http/server.ts';

serve(async (req) => {
  // 1. Verify JWT
  const authHeader = req.headers.get('Authorization');
  if (!authHeader) return new Response('Unauthorized', { status: 401 });

  // 2. Parse and validate request
  const { kidId, purpose } = await req.json();

  // 3. Call Mux API
  const muxResponse = await createMuxUpload({ ... });

  // 4. Return upload URL
  return new Response(JSON.stringify(muxResponse), {
    headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
  });
});
```

Edge functions are deployed to Supabase (not Replit) using:
```bash
npx supabase functions deploy get-mux-upload-url
```

---

## 13. Error Handling

### App-level

- All API errors caught at TanStack Query level
- User-facing errors translated via error message dictionary (`/src/utils/errors.ts`)
- Crash reporting via Sentry (deferred to v0.5+)

### Server-level

- Edge functions return structured error objects: `{ error: { code, message, details } }`
- Stripe errors translated to user-friendly messages
- Database errors NEVER exposed to client (sanitized)

### Network resilience

- Retry failed requests automatically (TanStack Query retries 3x by default)
- Offline mode: deferred to v1.0
- Loading skeletons for all data-fetching screens

**v1.0:** Full test pyramid: unit (60%), integration (30%), E2E (10%).

# Ballpark — Client Preview via Expo Go

This document explains how to share the Ballpark app with clients using Expo Go (no TestFlight, no dev server, no same-network requirement).

## Stable Expo Go link

```
exp://u.expo.dev/4ce07796-bc3a-4c22-b3a1-502a1d5d6dfc?channel-name=preview
```

Clients scan the QR code below with the **Expo Go** app (iOS or Android) to open the latest published preview build.

### QR code

![Ballpark preview QR code](./client-preview-qr.png)

Point the **Expo Go** app's scanner (or your phone's camera on iOS) at the image above. The link is permanent — this QR code never changes. After each update is published, Expo Go fetches the new JS bundle automatically the next time the app is opened.

To regenerate the PNG locally:

```bash
node -e "
const https = require('https');
const fs = require('fs');
const url = 'https://api.qrserver.com/v1/create-qr-code/?size=400x400&margin=2&data=' + encodeURIComponent('exp://u.expo.dev/4ce07796-bc3a-4c22-b3a1-502a1d5d6dfc?channel-name=preview');
https.get(url, res => res.pipe(fs.createWriteStream('docs/client-preview-qr.png')));
"
```

## Prerequisites for the client

1. Install **Expo Go** from the App Store or Google Play.
2. Open the camera app (iOS) or Expo Go's QR scanner (Android) and point it at the QR code.
3. The app opens and authenticates against the live Supabase project.

## Publishing an update

After any feature ships, publish a new update to the preview channel:

```bash
eas update --channel preview --message "Brief description of what changed"
```

Required environment variables must be set before publishing (they are embedded in the JS bundle):

```bash
export EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL="<your-supabase-url>"
export EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY="<your-supabase-anon-key>"
export EXPO_PUBLIC_TENANT_SLUG="infinitehitting"
```

EAS CLI reads these from the shell environment at publish time and bakes them into the over-the-air bundle.

## How it works

- `app.json` points `expo.updates.url` at `https://u.expo.dev/4ce07796-bc3a-4c22-b3a1-502a1d5d6dfc`.
- `expo.runtimeVersion.policy` is `sdkVersion` — a bundle is compatible with any Expo Go build on the same Expo SDK version.
- `eas.json` sets `channel: "preview"` on the `preview` build profile so EAS knows which update channel to target.
- EAS Update hosts the JS bundle; Expo Go fetches it over HTTPS when the app starts.

## Useful commands

| Command | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `eas update --channel preview --message "..."` | Publish a new JS bundle to the preview channel |
| `eas update:list` | See all published updates and their channels |
| `eas update:view <update-id>` | Inspect a specific update |

## Notes

- This is **JS-only** (OTA update). If native code changes (new Expo SDK, new native module), a full EAS Build + new Expo Go-compatible binary is needed.
- The client must have internet access — Expo Go fetches the bundle from EAS servers on launch.
- The `ballpark://` deep-link scheme (Supabase auth callback) works in Expo Go without any extra configuration.

# Ballpark — Leave Behind

**The operating system for youth sports franchises.**

---

## The Problem

Youth sports facilities run on tools built for yoga studios — MindBody, Square, Excel, Facebook groups. The moment a kid walks out the door, the relationship is gone. Multiply that across a franchise: 5 locations, 15 coaches, 400 families, zero visibility, $300-$500 per churned family per year.

---

## The Product

A mobile app built around the athlete — not the front desk.

- **Home dashboard** — Kid's name, points (847), rank (#3 in 14U), coach video, next booking, pending drill, personal best. All live. A reason to open the app every day.
- **HitTrax auto-import** — Exit velocity, launch angle, distance, session stats. Appears in the app 2 minutes after the kid leaves the cage. No coach data entry. No parent upload.
- **Two-way video messaging** — Coach sends a swing breakdown. Parent replies with a backyard video. Full Mux HLS pipeline. Relationship between sessions, not just during them.
- **Drill assignments** — Coach assigns homework with a video, due date, and point reward. Parent submits. Coach reviews with stars + feedback. Points credited. Loop closed.
- **Gamification engine** — Points for sessions, drills, PRs, achievements. Redeemable for lessons, gear, or store items. Live leaderboard by age group. Kids compete. Kids stay.
- **Booking** — Filter by type, pick a slot, confirm in under 20 seconds. Confirmation email via Resend. 40%+ of bookings shift from phone to app.

---

## Why Not MindBody?

| | MindBody | Ballpark |
|---|---|---|
| Built for | Owner / front desk | The athlete |
| HitTrax / sensor data | None | Automated, 2-min lag |
| Franchise OS | Per-location only | Multi-tenant, one view |
| Kid engagement | Login screen | Daily reason to open |
| Points economy | No | Full gamification loop |

---

## The June Pilot

**Location:** One Infinite Hitting facility — 40-60 families, 4-6 coaches.

| Week | Milestone |
|---|---|
| Week 1 | 10 families, 2 coaches. Invite-only soft launch. |
| Weeks 2-3 | All coaches. 30-40 families. HitTrax live. First redemptions. |
| Week 4 | Full location. Email blast. Front desk QR scanner active. |

**We measure:** ≥3 app opens/kid/week · ≥40% bookings via app · ≥60% drill completion · <24h coach response · ≥10 redemptions · NPS ≥8 · <2% crash rate.

**We own:** Coach onboarding (10 min/coach), family invite emails, week-1 live support, weekly data recaps to IH leadership.

---

## The Ask

**Investors:**
We are raising [X] to [hire / scale / EAS builds + HitTrax partnership]. Anchor customer live. Pilot in June. Technology deployed. The flywheel: more kids → richer leaderboard → more engagement → less churn → more locations.

**Franchise partners (IH):**
Run the June pilot with us. We handle everything. If 3+ opens/kid/week and 40%+ app bookings hold, we expand to your next location in August.

**New franchise tenants:**
Same infrastructure — booking, messaging, gamification, HitTrax or equivalent — under your brand, in your app. Already built. Platform fee on transactions + per-active-family monthly. Live in 30 days.

---

# Ballpark Demo Script

## THEME: "The Operating System for Youth Sports"

**Core narrative:** MindBody runs a gym. Ballpark runs a franchise. The difference is the kid.

Every demo revolves around one athlete — **Marcus Rivera, 14U, #847 points, ranked #3 in his age group at Infinite Hitting**. Every feature is revealed through Marcus's day, not through a feature list.

**Demo runtime:** ~25 minutes for investors / ~40 minutes with a live app walkthrough for franchise partners.

---

## PART 1 — THE PROBLEM (3 minutes)

**[DELIVER WITHOUT SLIDES — conversational, sharp]**

> "Youth sports facilities are running on tools that were designed for yoga studios. MindBody. Square. Excel spreadsheets. Maybe a Facebook group for messages.
>
> Here's what that looks like in practice. A parent calls to book a lesson. A coach texts a kid drill feedback. A 12-year-old hits 88 miles per hour off the tee and nobody records it. The kid goes home and plays on his phone — TikTok, YouTube, whatever — and the facility has zero presence in his life between sessions.
>
> The moment a kid walks out the door, the relationship is gone.
>
> Now multiply that across a franchise. 5 locations. 15 coaches. 400 families. Each location running their own version of chaos, none of it talking to each other. The owner of the franchise has no idea which location is actually performing, which coaches are retaining families, which kids are about to churn.
>
> That's the problem. It's not a booking problem. It's an engagement problem. And it costs these facilities $300 to $500 per lost family per year — in recurring revenue, not one-time transactions.
>
> Ballpark fixes this."

---

## PART 2 — THE PRODUCT: MARCUS'S DAY (12 minutes)

**[LIVE APP WALKTHROUGH — use the seeded Marcus Rivera demo scenario]**

**Setup before demo:** Run `node scripts/seed-demo-scenario.mjs` to load Marcus's full data. Have an iPhone with Expo Go open, logged in as Marcus's parent account.

---

### 2A — HOME TAB (2 min)

> "This is what Marcus sees when he opens the app. Not a booking calendar. Not a payment portal. *His* dashboard."

**Point out:**
- **His name, his points (847), his rank (#3 in 14U)** — gold hero card at the top. His identity is front and center.
- **Stats row:** 7-day streak, rank delta (up 2 this week), exit velocity (88.4 mph from today's HitTrax session).
- **"New from Coach"** — Coach Mike sent him a swing analysis video yesterday. Unread badge. Tap it → full-screen video player opens inline.
- **"Up Next"** — Private lesson this Friday, 4:30 PM, Cage 3, Coach Mike.
- **"Pending Assignment"** — "Hip rotation drill, due Thursday. +25 points."
- **Personal Best card** — 88.4 mph. Set today. The app knows.

> "A kid who sees his name, his rank, and a message from his coach — that kid opens this app every day. That's not a hypothesis. That's what we're building toward. Compare that to a MindBody login screen."

> "This is the HitTrax integration. Every facility that has a HitTrax machine gets automatic data. The coach doesn't touch it. The parent doesn't upload anything. It just appears."

---

### 2C — WORK TAB: MESSAGES (2 min)

> "Coach Mike sent Marcus a swing breakdown."

**Point out:**
- **Messages sub-tab** — thread with Coach Mike at the top.
- Coach's video message: tap → full-screen HLS playback via Mux. Plays beautifully. Marks as viewed automatically.

- Then show a parent-to-coach **video reply** — tap the camera icon, record a 10-second clip of Marcus swinging in the backyard, send. Mux uploads it, processes it, delivers it to Coach Mike's portal in real time.

> "Two-way video. On a phone. Coach sends a breakdown, family sends a response. This is a relationship tool, not just a messaging tool."

> "The drill loop closes the coaching relationship between sessions. It's retention infrastructure."

---

### 2E — BOOK TAB (1 min)

### 2F — EARN TAB (2 min)

- **Ranks sub-tab** — Podium: Marcus at #3. His age group. Live. Tap his row: +2 this week. He's climbing.

**Redeem a reward:**

- Front desk scans it. Done.

### 2G — ME TAB (30 sec)

- **Settings:** update contact info, sign out.
- **Order history:** past redemptions and purchases, all in one place.

---

## PART 3 — THE BACKEND (5 minutes)

**[SWITCH TO VERBAL — no need to show screens unless technical audience]**

> "What you just saw is the surface. Here's what's underneath."

**Infrastructure — describe verbally or show `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` stack diagram:**

```
Mobile App (React Native / Expo)
        ↓
Supabase (Postgres + Auth + Realtime + Edge Functions)
        ↓
HitTrax   |   Mux (video)   |   Stripe Connect   |   Resend (email)
```

**The 5 key backend points:**

**1. Supabase — the data layer.**
Postgres database with row-level security on every table. Every family sees only their data. Every coach sees only their location's data. Every franchise sees only their tenant's data. It's enforced at the database level — not in application code. You cannot query across tenants. Period.

**2. Multi-tenancy — the business model backbone.**
Every record in the system has a `tenant_id`. Infinite Hitting is Tenant #1. The next franchise that signs up becomes Tenant #2. They share zero data. They get a branded build with their own colors, their own coaches, their own store. We flip them on in days, not months.

**3. HitTrax pipeline — the data moat.**
Five Edge Functions handle the full HitTrax integration: association, polling (every 2 minutes via pg_cron), session import, personal best tracking. No competitor has automated this. The data is in the athlete's pocket 2 minutes after they leave the cage.

**4. Mux — video infrastructure.**
Coach uploads a video on the portal. Mux processes it to HLS in under 60 seconds. Parent gets an email (Resend) and an in-app notification. They tap play on their phone. The video streams at full quality. We didn't build a CDN. We didn't build a transcoder. Mux handles it. We just glue the pieces.

**5. Stripe Connect — franchise-ready payments.**
Each location has their own Stripe Connect account. When a family buys a hoodie, the money goes to the location, not to us. We take a platform fee. This is how franchise royalties work in software. It's the same model that powers Shopify and Mindbody — we just built it for youth sports.

---

## PART 4 — KEY DIFFERENTIATORS (3 minutes)

> "Why can't a facility just use MindBody?"

**1. Kid-first, not admin-first.**
MindBody is built for the owner and the front desk. Ballpark is built for the athlete. A 12-year-old can open this app and have a reason to stay for 10 minutes. MindBody's mobile experience is a login screen and a class schedule. We're competing for the kid's attention against TikTok. We designed for that.

**2. Automated performance data.**
No other booking/management platform integrates with HitTrax or similar sensor data. When a kid's exit velocity data appears in their app automatically, that's magic. It creates a feedback loop that no coach can replicate manually. The data is the hook.

**3. Multi-tenant franchise infrastructure.**
MindBody runs one location at a time. Ballpark is a franchise OS. A franchisor logs in and sees all 12 locations — bookings, retention metrics, coach performance — in one view. An owner of 3 locations gets consolidated revenue and engagement data. This is the product that franchise HQs will pay for.

**4. The points economy changes behavior.**
We have a hypothesis: if every session, every drill, every PR translates to points — and points have real-world value — kids will nag their parents to book more sessions. We'll prove this in the June pilot. If the average weekly session count per kid goes up 15% after launch, we have an upsell engine, not just a software product.

---

## PART 5 — THE JUNE PILOT PLAN (5 minutes)

**[DELIVERY: forward-looking, specific, honest about what's a test]**

> "Here's how we're going to stress-test everything we just showed you."

**Location:** One Infinite Hitting facility — [target: highest-volume location, TBD with the IH team]. Target: 40-60 active families, 4-6 coaches.

**Timeline:**
- **Week 1 (early June): Soft launch.** 10 families, 2 coaches. Invite-only via email. We sit with the front desk staff and walk them through coach provisioning, booking setup, and the QR scanner on the portal.
- **Week 2-3: Expanded beta.** All coaches onboarded. 30-40 families invited. HitTrax pipeline active. First real redemptions.
- **Week 4: Full location.** Everyone gets access. Push email blast. Coach Mike demo for families at the front desk.

**What we're measuring:**

| Metric | Target | How We Measure |
|---|---|---|
| Weekly app opens per kid | ≥ 3x | Supabase analytics |
| Bookings via app vs. phone | ≥ 40% via app | `bookings.source` field |
| Drill completion rate | ≥ 60% submitted | Assignment status |
| Coach response time | < 24h on messages | `coach_messages` timestamps |
| Points redemptions | ≥ 10 in 4 weeks | `orders` table |
| Net Promoter Score | ≥ 8 (ask at week 4) | Google Form |
| Crash rate | < 2% sessions | Expo error tracking |

**What the location needs to provide:**
- Wi-Fi for Expo Go testing (QR code onboarding)
- Front desk point of contact (1 person for QR scanner + coach provisioning)
- HitTrax credentials (HITTRAX_PARTNER_ID + API key) — or we run mock data if API isn't ready
- 10 volunteer families for week 1 beta

**What we own:**
- Onboarding all 4-6 coaches (takes 10 minutes per coach)
- Family invite emails via Resend
- Live support during week 1 (Slack channel with location manager)
- Weekly data recap emailed to IH leadership

**Known risks and mitigations:**
- *Expo Go requires a QR scan per device.* Mitigation: we run a TestFlight/Play Store beta build before week 3 to eliminate this friction.
- *HitTrax API may not be live.* Mitigation: seed realistic mock data so the in-app experience is still compelling. The pipeline code is ready to flip live the moment keys are available.
- *Coach adoption.* Mitigation: show coaches the portal first — it's their tool. The parent app is secondary. Coaches who see value in sending swing breakdowns are our distribution channel.

---

## PART 6 — WHAT WE BUILD NEXT (3 minutes)

**[Frame as "the platform getting smarter over time"]**

**Near-term (v0.8-v1.0, 60-90 days post-pilot):**
- **AI daily recap (SMS/push):** Every morning, a parent gets a 2-sentence recap — "Marcus is ranked #3 in 14U exit velo. He has a drill due Thursday. Coach Mike left him a note." Automated. Zero coach time.
- **Coach mobile app:** Coaches shouldn't be tied to a laptop. A lightweight coach app for sending messages, reviewing drills, and marking sessions complete from the cage.
- **Multi-kid families:** One parent account, multiple siblings. Each kid gets their own profile, their own points, their own leaderboard position.
- **Cancellation + rescheduling self-service:** Parents reschedule from the app. No phone calls. No front desk overhead.

**Medium-term (v1.0-v1.5, 3-6 months):**
- **Franchisor portal:** The owner of all 12 locations logs in once. Sees which locations have the highest engagement, which coaches have the best retention, which age groups are at risk of churning. This is the tool that gets a franchise HQ to mandate Ballpark across all locations.
- **White-label builds:** Ballpark powers the "XYZ Baseball Academy" app. Different name, different colors, same infrastructure. Each new franchise is a new revenue line with near-zero marginal cost.
- **Leaderboard cross-location:** Kids competing across multiple Infinite Hitting locations. Top 10 in the state. Regional competitions. This is the flywheel — the more locations on the platform, the more compelling the leaderboard.

**Long-term (the platform play):**
- **Stripe billing integration:** Families manage their memberships in the app. Monthly auto-renew. Pause, cancel, upgrade — all self-service. This eliminates the front desk entirely for billing and puts the subscription business on the platform.
- **Data products for franchisors:** Which drills correlate with exit velocity improvement? Which coaching styles retain kids longest? Aggregate, anonymized insights that a franchisor uses to build their coaching curriculum. This is where the data moat compounds.
- **Other sports:** Same infrastructure, different HitTrax data. Soccer (StatSports). Lacrosse. Swimming. The multi-tenant architecture means we onboard a new sport the same way we onboard a new franchise. This is a 5-year play.

# Design System & Visual Spec

> This document defines the visual design language for the Ballpark athlete app. Every screen, component, and interaction should follow these rules. The authoritative visual reference is `/design/InfiniteHittingApp.jsx` — when in doubt, look there.

---

## 1. Brand Identity

**Tenant:** Infinite Hitting (initial)
**Aesthetic:** Premium athletic, dark luxe, gold accents
**Tone:** Aspirational but accessible. Treats kids as serious athletes, not children.

The visual language is closer to a high-end sports brand (Nike, Adidas, Under Armour) than to typical SaaS apps (MindBody, Mindbody). We're competing for the kid's attention against TikTok and Instagram, not against scheduling software.

---

## 2. Color Tokens

### Primary palette

```typescript
// /src/theme/tokens.ts

export const colors = {
  // Primary darks (backgrounds)
  dark: '#2D2B2A',
  darker: '#1C1B1A',
  darkest: '#0F0E0E',

  // Gold accents (Infinite Hitting signature)
  gold: '#F1E5AD',
  goldBright: '#E8D89A',
  goldDeep: '#B8A268',
  goldHover: '#D9C88F',

  // Cream (light backgrounds when needed)
  cream: '#FAF6E8',
  creamLight: '#FDFBF2',

  // Pure
  white: '#FFFFFF',

  // Text
  text: '#1A1A1A',
  textOnDark: '#FAF6E8',
  textMuted: '#6B6560',
  textLight: '#9B9590',

  // Borders
  border: '#3A3836',
  borderLight: '#E8E3D5',
  borderGold: 'rgba(241, 229, 173, 0.2)',

  // Status colors
  success: '#A8C67F',
  successBg: '#E8F0DC',
  warning: '#E8A747',
  warningBg: '#F9EDD5',
  danger: '#C86B5C',
  dangerBg: '#F5DED8',
  info: '#7BA8C4',
  infoBg: '#D8E6EF',
};
```

### Usage rules

- **Default background** is always one of the dark tones (`darkest`, `darker`, or `dark`)
- **Gold is for attention** — points cards, primary CTAs, highlights, current state
- **Cream is for inverted contexts** — modals, light surfaces, alternative cards
- **Status colors** are for badges, chips, alerts only — never primary surfaces

---

## 3. Typography

```typescript
// /src/theme/tokens.ts

export const fonts = {
  display: 'Oswald',         // headers, big numbers, button labels
  body: 'Inter',             // body text, descriptions, long-form content
  mono: 'JetBrains Mono',    // codes, IDs, redemption codes
};

export const fontSizes = {
  xs: 9,
  sm: 10,
  base: 12,
  md: 13,
  lg: 14,
  xl: 17,
  '2xl': 22,
  '3xl': 28,
  '4xl': 32,
  '5xl': 44,
  '6xl': 48,
};

export const fontWeights = {
  regular: '400',
  medium: '500',
  semibold: '600',
  bold: '700',
  extrabold: '800',
};
```

### Typography rules

- **Display (Oswald)** is for: headlines, big numbers (points, exit velo), button labels, navigation tabs, section labels
- **Body (Inter)** is for: descriptions, paragraphs, list items, secondary text
- **Mono (JetBrains Mono)** is for: redemption codes, transaction IDs, anything that needs to be visually copyable

### Letter spacing

- Display headers (Oswald): `letterSpacing: -0.5` to `-1` for big sizes
- All-caps section labels: `letterSpacing: 1.5` to `2`
- Body text: `letterSpacing: 0` (default)

### Font setup in Expo

```typescript
// In App.tsx, load fonts before app renders:
import { useFonts } from 'expo-font';
import {
  Oswald_400Regular,
  Oswald_500Medium,
  Oswald_600SemiBold,
  Oswald_700Bold,
} from '@expo-google-fonts/oswald';
import {
  Inter_400Regular,
  Inter_500Medium,
  Inter_600SemiBold,
  Inter_700Bold,
  Inter_800ExtraBold,
} from '@expo-google-fonts/inter';
```

## 4. Spacing Scale

```typescript
export const spacing = {
  xxs: 2,
  xs: 4,
  sm: 6,
  base: 8,
  md: 10,
  lg: 12,
  xl: 14,
  '2xl': 16,
  '3xl': 20,
  '4xl': 24,
  '5xl': 32,
  '6xl': 40,
  '7xl': 48,
};
```

**Rule:** Always reference spacing via the scale. Never use arbitrary numbers. If `spacing.lg` (12px) doesn't fit, use the next step up or down — don't introduce 11px or 13px.

## 5. Border Radius

```typescript
export const radius = {
  none: 0,
  sm: 4,
  base: 6,
  md: 8,
  lg: 10,
  xl: 12,
  '2xl': 14,
  '3xl': 16,
  '4xl': 18,
  '5xl': 20,
  full: 9999,
};
```

### Usage
- **Buttons:** `radius.md` (8px) for secondary, `radius.xl` (12px) for primary
- **Cards:** `radius.2xl` (14px) standard, `radius.5xl` (20px) for hero cards
- **Pills/chips:** `radius.full`
- **Phone screen container:** `radius.5xl` (20px) on inner content

## 10. Implementation Notes

### Using design tokens

Every styled component imports from tokens:

```typescript
import { colors, spacing, radius, fonts, fontSizes, fontWeights } from '@/theme/tokens';

const styles = StyleSheet.create({
  card: {
    backgroundColor: colors.darker,
    borderRadius: radius['2xl'],
    padding: spacing['2xl'],
    borderWidth: 1,
    borderColor: colors.border,
  },
  title: {
    fontFamily: fonts.display,
    fontSize: fontSizes['2xl'],
    fontWeight: fontWeights.bold,
    color: colors.textOnDark,
    letterSpacing: -0.5,
  },
});
```

**NEVER hardcode colors, fonts, or spacing values** in component files. Always reference tokens.

### Matching the prototype

When implementing a screen:

1. Open `/design/InfiniteHittingApp.jsx`
2. Find the corresponding component (e.g., `HomeScreen`)
3. Read the JSX structure carefully
4. Note the exact spacing, colors, font sizes used (these will reference inline values like `'#F1E5AD'` — translate them to tokens)
5. Replicate the component hierarchy in React Native
6. Use design tokens (NOT inline values) in the production code
7. Render on Expo Go and visually compare to the prototype

### React Native vs Web differences

The prototype is web React. Key translations for React Native:

| Web (prototype) | React Native (production) |
|---|---|
| `<div>` | `<View>` |
| `<span>`, `<p>` | `<Text>` |
| `onClick` | `onPress` |
| `<img>` | `<Image>` |
| `style={{ ... }}` (inline) | `StyleSheet.create({...})` |
| `cursor: 'pointer'` | omit (RN Pressable handles it) |
| `position: 'sticky'` | not supported, use ScrollView with sticky header |
| CSS gradients | `expo-linear-gradient` |
| `backdrop-filter: blur` | `BlurView` from `expo-blur` |
| SVG inline | `react-native-svg` components |
| Lucide icons | `lucide-react-native` package |

# EAS Build Profiles — Franchise Setup Guide

`eas.json` defines one named build profile per franchise. This document
explains how to add a new profile when onboarding a new franchise location.

## Current profiles

| Profile name               | Tenant slug          | Purpose                              |
|---------------------------|---------------------|--------------------------------------|
| `development`              | (env default)       | Internal dev build (Expo Dev Client) |
| `preview`                  | (env default)       | Internal distribution / QA           |
| `production`               | (env default)       | Generic production (no slug pin)     |
| `production-infinitehitting` | `infinitehitting` | Infinite Hitting production build    |

## Adding a new franchise profile

### 1. Provision the tenant in Supabase

```sql
-- Run in the Supabase SQL editor (or via migration) for the new tenant.
INSERT INTO public.tenants (id, name, slug)
VALUES (gen_random_uuid(), 'My New Gym', 'mynewgym');
```

Record the generated UUID as `<NEW_TENANT_ID>`.

### 2. Add the build profile to `eas.json`

Open `eas.json` and add a new entry under `"build"`:

```json
"production-mynewgym": {
  "autoIncrement": true,
  "env": {
    "EXPO_PUBLIC_TENANT_SLUG": "mynewgym"
  }
}
```

Naming convention: `production-<slug>` in lowercase, matching exactly the
`slug` column in the `tenants` table.

### 3. Set tenant-specific Supabase env vars (optional)

If the new franchise uses its own Supabase project, create a separate
`.env.mynewgym` and pass it via the EAS environment or EAS Secrets:

```bash
eas secret:create --scope project --name EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL_MYNEWGYM \
  --value "https://xxxx.supabase.co"
```

For a single-project multi-tenant setup (current architecture), no extra
Supabase vars are needed — `EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` and
`EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are shared.

### 4. Build and submit

```bash
# Build for the new franchise
eas build --profile production-mynewgym --platform ios
eas build --profile production-mynewgym --platform android

# Submit to stores (uses the default "submit" config in eas.json)
eas submit --platform ios  --latest
eas submit --platform android --latest
```

### 5. Seed initial data for the new tenant

```bash
EXPO_PUBLIC_TENANT_SLUG=mynewgym node scripts/seed-portal-demo-data.mjs
```

Or provision a real owner account via the Supabase dashboard and point the
new app binary at the correct tenant slug.

## Checklist

- [ ] `tenants` row inserted with correct `slug`
- [ ] `tenant_config` row inserted (defaults `allow_cross_location_booking = false`)
- [ ] At least one row in `locations` with `tenant_id = <NEW_TENANT_ID>`
- [ ] Build profile added to `eas.json` with matching `EXPO_PUBLIC_TENANT_SLUG`
- [ ] EAS build + submit completed for both platforms
- [ ] App Store / Play Store listing created for the new franchise (separate app or same with different bundle ID, per your franchise model)

# HitTrax integration runbook

Task #118. Foundation for #119 (Sessions list), #120 (Stats), #121 (Sessions
detail), #122 (PR notifications hardening).

## What we ship

| Path | Role |
|------|------|
| `supabase/migrations/20260508060000_v07_hittrax_capture_pipeline.sql` | `sessions`, `swings`, `personal_bests`, `kid_capture_links` + `detect_swing_pr` trigger |
| `supabase/functions/hittrax-associate` | parent JWT → POST AssociateThirdPartyAccount |
| `supabase/functions/hittrax-registration-complete` | `--no-verify-jwt` HitTrax inbound (Accepted/Declined) |
| `supabase/functions/hittrax-poll` | service-role; pg_cron; pulls GetAvailableThirdPartyData |
| `supabase/functions/hittrax-disconnect` | parent JWT → POST RemoveThirdPartyAssociation |
| `supabase/functions/hittrax-forget` | `--no-verify-jwt` HitTrax inbound (GDPR purge from HitTrax → us) |
| `supabase/functions/_shared/hittrax.ts` | URL builder, response parser, swing-payload mapper, constant-time auth |
| `src/api/hittrax.ts` + `src/hooks/useHitTraxLink.tsx` | client SDK |
| `src/screens/Me/ConnectHitTraxScreen.tsx` | parent connect/disconnect UI |
| `scripts/replay-hittrax-fixture.mjs` | local fixture replay (no HitTrax keys needed) |

### `hittrax-forget` direction (inbound, by design)

HitTrax v1.0 spec defines `ForgetHitTraxUser` as a **HitTrax-initiated**
callback we host: when a HitTrax user requests data deletion through HitTrax,
HitTrax POSTs us, and we purge that user's locally-cached HitTrax data
(swings + HitTrax-sourced personal_bests + the link row). Our endpoint
returns `text/plain` per spec and authenticates with the same constant-time
PartnerID + APIKey check as `hittrax-registration-complete`.

The **parent-initiated outbound disconnect** is the separate
`hittrax-disconnect` Edge Function: it calls HitTrax's
`RemoveThirdPartyAssociation` first and only then flips our local link to
`removed`, so HitTrax stops sending us further data even before our local
purge runs. The two functions cover the two propagation directions:

| Trigger                         | Function                          | Calls                          | Purges local? |
|---------------------------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------|---------------|
| Parent taps Disconnect          | `hittrax-disconnect`              | `RemoveThirdPartyAssociation`  | flips link only — historical swings retained |
| HitTrax-side delete-my-data     | `hittrax-forget` (this endpoint)  | (inbound — no outbound call)   | swings + PBs + link row purged |
| Parent deletes Ballpark account | `account-delete` (parent JWT)     | `RemoveThirdPartyAssociation` + `ForgetHitTraxUser` per active link | family-wide cascade via auth.admin.deleteUser + FKs |

## Polling cadence + backoff

`hittrax-poll` runs every 2 minutes via pg_cron. For each active link the
worker selects rows where `next_poll_at IS NULL OR next_poll_at <= now()`,
so a healthy link is poll-eligible on every tick and a backed-off link
sits out until its delay elapses.

On any transient failure (HitTrax timeout, unreachable, 5xx, "Error …" 200
body, parse drift, partial parse with ANY dropped row, partial swing-upsert
failure) the worker calls `recordFailure(link, retry_count, error)` which:

- increments `retry_count` (capped exponent 30)
- writes `next_poll_at = now() + min(30 * 2^(retry_count-1), 30m)`
- leaves `last_polled_through` untouched so the next eligible poll
  re-fetches the same window (the swings UNIQUE absorbs already-stored
  rows).

Backoff schedule: 30s → 1m → 2m → 4m → 8m → 16m → 30m (capped). On the
next successful poll both columns reset (`retry_count = 0`,
`next_poll_at = null`).

## PR push fan-out (one push per swing)

Personal-best detection inside `hittrax-poll` collapses every metric a
swing topped (`exit_velocity_mph`, `distance_ft`, `pitch_speed_mph`) into
a SINGLE push notification per swing — matching the canonical
`detect_swing_pr` trigger which writes one `points_ledger reason='pr_hit'`
row per qualifying swing. The push title uses a priority order
(exit velo → distance → pitch speed) for the headline metric, and the
push `data.metrics` array carries every metric that PR'd so the client
can render however it likes. Per-metric notifications were a
duplicate-notification bug.

## Secrets (Supabase Edge Function env)

Set via `npx supabase secrets set KEY=...`. **Never** prefix `EXPO_PUBLIC_`.

| Key | Notes |
|-----|-------|
| `HITTRAX_BASE_URL` | per-environment, no trailing slash |
| `HITTRAX_PARTNER_ID` | issued manually by HitTrax per page 2 of spec |
| `HITTRAX_API_KEY` | issued with PartnerID; treat like a database password |
| `HITTRAX_CONTENT_TYPE` | optional; defaults to `Swings`. Override per the contracted ContentType list |

The five Edge Functions all return `503 hittrax_not_configured` until the
three required keys are present, so deploys are safe before keys land.

## Deploy

`scripts/post-merge.sh` runs after every task merge. The two inbound endpoints
(`hittrax-registration-complete`, `hittrax-forget`) deploy with
`--no-verify-jwt` because HitTrax authenticates with PartnerID + APIKey URL
params — there is no JWT.

```
npx supabase functions deploy hittrax-associate
npx supabase functions deploy hittrax-poll
npx supabase functions deploy hittrax-disconnect
npx supabase functions deploy hittrax-registration-complete --no-verify-jwt
npx supabase functions deploy hittrax-forget --no-verify-jwt
```

Give HitTrax these two callback URLs (replace `<project-ref>`):

```
https://<project-ref>.functions.supabase.co/hittrax-registration-complete
https://<project-ref>.functions.supabase.co/hittrax-forget
```

## Cron

`hittrax-poll` is service-role only and intended to run every 2 minutes.
Once the keys are provisioned, install the cron job (one-time, in Supabase
SQL editor as service role):

```sql
SELECT cron.schedule(
  'hittrax-poll-2min',
  '*/2 * * * *',
  $$
    SELECT net.http_post(
      url     := 'https://<project-ref>.functions.supabase.co/hittrax-poll',
      headers := jsonb_build_object(
        'Authorization', 'Bearer ' || current_setting('app.settings.service_role_key'),
        'Content-Type',  'application/json'
      ),
      body    := '{}'::jsonb
    );
  $$
);
```

The function caps each run at 50 active links and sorts by oldest
`last_polled_at` first, so a stalled link can never starve fresh ones.

## Lifecycle

```
parent enters HitTrax UserID
        │
        ▼
hittrax-associate ───▶ HitTrax AssociateThirdPartyAccount
        │                      │
        │                      ▼
        │              email to parent's HitTrax account
        │                      │
        ▼                      ▼ (Accept|Decline)
kid_capture_links     hittrax-registration-complete (← HitTrax)
status='pending'              │
                              ▼
                      status='active' (or 'declined')
                      password persisted, last_polled_through=now
                              │
                              ▼  every 2 min, service role
                      hittrax-poll → GetAvailableThirdPartyData
                              │
                              ▼
                      sessions UPSERT + swings UPSERT
                              │
                              ▼  AFTER INSERT trigger
                      detect_swing_pr → personal_bests + points_ledger +15
                              │
                              ▼  best-effort, Promise.allSettled
                      send-push-notification
```

Disconnect: parent → `hittrax-disconnect` → HitTrax `RemoveThirdPartyAssociation` → flip link to `removed`.

GDPR: HitTrax → `hittrax-forget` → delete swings + sessions + personal_bests for the kid → flip link to `removed`.

## Idempotency contract

| Layer | Key |
|-------|-----|
| Sessions | `UNIQUE (capture_source, capture_session_id)` (partial; manual sessions excluded) |
| Swings | `UNIQUE (capture_source, capture_event_id)` — replays UPSERT, never duplicate |
| PR ledger | partial `UNIQUE (reference_id) WHERE reason='pr_hit' AND reference_type='swing'` |
| Polling cursor | `last_polled_through` advanced **only** after successful UPSERT batch |
| Inbound `registration-complete` | re-delivery against existing `active` row is a graceful no-op |
| Inbound `forget` | re-delivery against already-removed link returns `"true"` |

## Testing without HitTrax keys

```
node scripts/replay-hittrax-fixture.mjs <kid_uuid>
```

Run twice; the second run inserts zero rows (UPSERT idempotent), and
`personal_bests` / `kids.points_balance` remain unchanged. Edit the fixture
to bump `Velo` past the prior best to see a fresh PR + ledger row.

## Open items (deferred / contract-pending)

- **Canonical swing field names.** `_shared/hittrax.ts` `FIELD_MAP` accepts the
  common HitTrax dashboard variants (`Velo`, `LaunchAngle`, `Distance`, …).
  Tighten to the contracted ContentType schema once the keys + sample
  payloads land. Update once and every caller benefits.
- **Backfill on link activation.** `last_polled_through` is seeded to the
  activation timestamp — historical swings before that are NOT pulled in v1.
  Backfill ships as a follow-up if/when product asks.
- **Realtime UI flip.** `useHitTraxLink` subscribes to a postgres_changes
  Realtime channel scoped to the family's `kid_capture_links` rows and
  invalidates the React Query cache on UPDATE — so the Home banner and
  Me → HitTrax screen flip from "pending" → "active" the instant
  `hittrax-registration-complete` writes the row, with no manual refresh.
  A 5-second `refetchInterval` is kept as a defense-in-depth fallback in
  case the websocket is dropped (airplane mode, background → foreground,
  etc.). To disable the fallback once Realtime delivery is fully trusted
  in production, set the `refetchInterval` in `src/hooks/useHitTraxLink.tsx`
  to `false`.
