/**
 * Coach-side inbox API.
 *
 * Fetches all coach_messages where the coach is either the SENDER
 * (coach→parent: sender_user_id = coachUserId) or the RECIPIENT
 * (parent→coach: recipient_coach_user_id = coachUserId), then folds
 * them into one row per family thread — latest message first.
 *
 * Uses the supabaseExt client (same session, extended types) so that
 * the v0.7 columns (label, sender_display, recipient_coach_user_id)
 * are typed correctly until types are regenerated.
 */

import { supabase, supabaseExt } from '@/lib/supabase';
import type { Tables } from '@/types/database';

export type CoachInboxRow = {
  /** The family this thread belongs to. */
  familyId: string;
  familyLastName: string;
  /** The kid in this thread (first kid encountered; one family = one kid in v0.5). */
  kidId: string;
  kidFirstName: string;
  kidLastName: string;
  /** coachUserId — always the caller's own user_id. Carried for convenience. */
  coachUserId: string;
  lastCreatedAt: string;
  lastMessageText: string | null;
  lastHasVideo: boolean;
  /** True when the last message is FROM the parent (i.e., unread by the coach). */
  unread: boolean;
};

type RawMsgRow = {
  id: string;
  created_at: string;
  sender_user_id: string;
  recipient_family_id: string;
  recipient_kid_id: string;
  recipient_coach_user_id: string | null;
  message_text: string | null;
  viewed_at: string | null;
  video_id: string | null;
};

type KidFamilyRow = Pick<
  Tables<'kids'>,
  'id' | 'first_name' | 'last_name' | 'family_id'
> & {
  family: Pick<Tables<'families'>, 'id' | 'parent_last_name'> | null;
};

export async function listCoachInbox(coachUserId: string): Promise<CoachInboxRow[]> {
  // Fetch all messages the coach is involved in (sender OR recipient).
  // PostgREST `or` filter across two columns.
  const { data: msgs, error } = await supabaseExt
    .from('coach_messages')
    .select(
      'id, created_at, sender_user_id, recipient_family_id, recipient_kid_id, recipient_coach_user_id, message_text, viewed_at, video_id',
    )
    .or(
      `sender_user_id.eq.${coachUserId},recipient_coach_user_id.eq.${coachUserId}`,
    )
    .order('created_at', { ascending: false });
  if (error) throw error;

  const rows = (msgs ?? []) as unknown as RawMsgRow[];

  // Build family-keyed map (newest message first = first encounter per family).
  const folder = new Map<
    string,
    { familyId: string; kidId: string; lastMsg: RawMsgRow; isFromParent: boolean }
  >();
  for (const m of rows) {
    const familyId = m.recipient_family_id;
    if (!familyId) continue;
    if (folder.has(familyId)) continue;
    const isFromParent = m.sender_user_id !== coachUserId;
    folder.set(familyId, {
      familyId,
      kidId: m.recipient_kid_id,
      lastMsg: m,
      isFromParent,
    });
  }

  if (folder.size === 0) return [];

  // Batch-fetch kid + family display info.
  const kidIds = Array.from(folder.values()).map((f) => f.kidId);
  const { data: kids, error: kidErr } = await supabase
    .from('kids')
    .select('id, first_name, last_name, family_id, family:families(id, parent_last_name)')
    .in('id', kidIds);
  if (kidErr) throw kidErr;

  const kidMap = new Map<string, KidFamilyRow>();
  for (const k of (kids ?? []) as unknown as KidFamilyRow[]) {
    kidMap.set(k.id, k);
  }

  const result: CoachInboxRow[] = [];
  for (const entry of folder.values()) {
    const kid = kidMap.get(entry.kidId);
    const m = entry.lastMsg;
    result.push({
      familyId: entry.familyId,
      familyLastName: kid?.family?.parent_last_name ?? '',
      kidId: entry.kidId,
      kidFirstName: kid?.first_name ?? 'Athlete',
      kidLastName: kid?.last_name ?? '',
      coachUserId,
      lastCreatedAt: m.created_at,
      lastMessageText: m.message_text,
      lastHasVideo: !!m.video_id,
      unread: entry.isFromParent && !m.viewed_at,
    });
  }

  // Sort by most recent message descending.
  result.sort((a, b) => b.lastCreatedAt.localeCompare(a.lastCreatedAt));
  return result;
}

/**
 * Bidirectional thread for a (kid, coach) pair — coach-side perspective.
 *
 * Unlike the parent-side `listMessageThread` (which uses `selfUserId` to
 * distinguish the parent arm of the `or` filter), this function correctly
 * fetches BOTH directions from the coach's point of view:
 *
 *   - coach→parent:  sender_user_id = coachUserId  (no recipient_coach_user_id)
 *   - parent→coach:  recipient_coach_user_id = coachUserId
 *
 * Both arms are scoped to `recipient_kid_id = kidId`. Sorted ascending so
 * the FlatList renders like a chat (oldest at top).
 *
 * Uses supabaseExt for the v0.7 extended columns.
 */
export type CoachThreadMessage = {
  id: string;
  createdAt: string;
  senderUserId: string;
  recipientFamilyId: string;
  recipientKidId: string;
  recipientCoachUserId: string | null;
  messageText: string | null;
  label: string | null;
  senderDisplay: string | null;
  viewedAt: string | null;
  video: {
    id: string;
    status: string;
    muxPlaybackId: string | null;
    durationSeconds: number | null;
    purpose: string;
  } | null;
};

type CoachThreadJoinRow = {
  id: string;
  created_at: string;
  sender_user_id: string;
  recipient_family_id: string;
  recipient_kid_id: string;
  recipient_coach_user_id: string | null;
  message_text: string | null;
  label: string | null;
  sender_display: string | null;
  viewed_at: string | null;
  video:
    | Pick<
        Tables<'videos'>,
        'id' | 'status' | 'mux_playback_id' | 'duration_seconds' | 'purpose'
      >
    | Pick<
        Tables<'videos'>,
        'id' | 'status' | 'mux_playback_id' | 'duration_seconds' | 'purpose'
      >[]
    | null;
};

function mapCoachThreadRow(r: CoachThreadJoinRow): CoachThreadMessage {
  const v = Array.isArray(r.video) ? r.video[0] ?? null : r.video;
  return {
    id: r.id,
    createdAt: r.created_at,
    senderUserId: r.sender_user_id,
    recipientFamilyId: r.recipient_family_id,
    recipientKidId: r.recipient_kid_id,
    recipientCoachUserId: r.recipient_coach_user_id,
    messageText: r.message_text,
    label: r.label,
    senderDisplay: r.sender_display,
    viewedAt: r.viewed_at,
    video: v
      ? {
          id: v.id,
          status: v.status,
          muxPlaybackId: v.mux_playback_id,
          durationSeconds: v.duration_seconds,
          purpose: v.purpose,
        }
      : null,
  };
}

export async function listCoachMessageThread(opts: {
  kidId: string;
  coachUserId: string;
}): Promise<CoachThreadMessage[]> {
  const { kidId, coachUserId } = opts;
  const { data, error } = await supabaseExt
    .from('coach_messages')
    .select(
      'id, created_at, sender_user_id, recipient_family_id, recipient_kid_id, recipient_coach_user_id, message_text, label, sender_display, viewed_at, video:videos(id, status, mux_playback_id, duration_seconds, purpose)',
    )
    .eq('recipient_kid_id', kidId)
    .or(
      // arm 1: coach sent this message (coach→parent direction)
      // arm 2: parent sent this message TO this coach (parent→coach direction)
      `sender_user_id.eq.${coachUserId},recipient_coach_user_id.eq.${coachUserId}`,
    )
    .order('created_at', { ascending: true });
  if (error) throw error;
  return ((data ?? []) as unknown as CoachThreadJoinRow[]).map(mapCoachThreadRow);
}

/**
 * Coach messages API helpers.
 *
 * v0.4 Step 4.9 added the read-side helper for the recipient picker. Step 4.10
 * adds the write side (`sendCoachMessage`) plus a small `getVideo` lookup so
 * the Send Confirmation screen can poll for the Mux poster as soon as the
 * webhook flips status to `ready`.
 *
 * RLS already lets a coach SELECT every kid + family in their tenant via the
 * `kids_select_coach_stub` / `families_select_coach_stub` policies
 * (see 20260505040800_rename_role_to_app_role_in_jwt.sql), so this file
 * doesn't need to filter by tenant_id client-side on the read paths.
 *
 * For inserts, the coach_messages_insert_own_coach RLS policy
 * (see 20260505080000_v04_videos_coach_messages.sql) requires
 * `tenant_id = (auth.jwt() ->> 'tenant_id')::uuid` AND
 * `sender_user_id = auth.uid()`. The client must therefore pass both —
 * tenant_id is supplied by the caller (read from `public.coaches.tenant_id`
 * via `useCoach`), and sender_user_id is taken from `useAuth().user.id`.
 */

import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';
import type { Tables } from '@/types/database';

/**
 * Flat row returned by `listTenantKids`, denormalised so the recipient
 * picker can render a row + group by family without an N+1 fetch.
 */
export type TenantKid = {
  kidId: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  ageGroup: string | null;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
  familyId: string;
  familyLastName: string;
  parentFirstName: string;
  parentLastName: string;
};

type KidWithFamilyRow = Pick<
  Tables<'kids'>,
  'id' | 'first_name' | 'last_name' | 'age_group' | 'avatar_url' | 'family_id'
> & {
  family:
    | Pick<
        Tables<'families'>,
        'id' | 'parent_first_name' | 'parent_last_name'
      >
    | null;
};

/**
 * Fetch every kid the coach can see (RLS scopes by tenant) along with the
 * family info needed to group + label rows. Sorted by family last name,
 * then kid first name — sorting happens client-side because PostgREST can't
 * `order` by an embedded resource's column.
 */
export async function listTenantKids(): Promise<TenantKid[]> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('kids')
    .select(
      'id, first_name, last_name, age_group, avatar_url, family_id, family:families!inner(id, parent_first_name, parent_last_name)',
    );
  if (error) throw error;

  const rows = (data ?? []) as unknown as KidWithFamilyRow[];

  const mapped: TenantKid[] = rows
    .filter((r): r is KidWithFamilyRow & { family: NonNullable<KidWithFamilyRow['family']> } => !!r.family)
    .map((r) => ({
      kidId: r.id,
      firstName: r.first_name,
      lastName: r.last_name,
      ageGroup: r.age_group,
      avatarUrl: r.avatar_url,
      familyId: r.family.id,
      familyLastName: r.family.parent_last_name,
      parentFirstName: r.family.parent_first_name,
      parentLastName: r.family.parent_last_name,
    }));

  mapped.sort((a, b) => {
    const fam = a.familyLastName.localeCompare(b.familyLastName, undefined, {
      sensitivity: 'base',
    });
    if (fam !== 0) return fam;
    return a.firstName.localeCompare(b.firstName, undefined, {
      sensitivity: 'base',
    });
  });

  return mapped;
}

/**
 * Lightweight projection of `public.videos` used by the Send Confirmation
 * preview. We only need the lifecycle status + playback id (for the Mux
 * poster URL) + duration for an optional caption.
 */
export type VideoPreview = Pick<
  Tables<'videos'>,
  'id' | 'status' | 'mux_playback_id' | 'duration_seconds'
>;

/**
 * Fetch a single video row by id. Returns null when the row is not visible
 * to the caller (RLS) or doesn't exist; callers branch on null to render a
 * generic "couldn't load preview" state.
 */
export async function getVideo(videoId: string): Promise<VideoPreview | null> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('videos')
    .select('id, status, mux_playback_id, duration_seconds')
    .eq('id', videoId)
    .maybeSingle();
  if (error) throw error;
  return data ?? null;
}

/**
 * Input shape for `sendCoachMessage`.
 *
 * `messageText` is normalised by the caller — pass `null` for an empty note
 * so the row's `message_text` column is NULL (not an empty string), which
 * keeps the UI's "video-only" detection trivial. tenant_id and
 * sender_user_id are looked up server-side from the current Supabase
 * session + the caller's `public.coaches` row, so callers can't accidentally
 * pass mismatched values that would trip the
 * coach_messages_insert_own_coach RLS policy.
 */
export type SendCoachMessageInput = {
  videoId: string;
  recipientFamilyId: string;
  recipientKidId: string;
  messageText: string | null;
};

export type SentCoachMessage = Tables<'coach_messages'>;

/**
 * Flat row returned by `listSentCoachMessages()` for the coach "My Videos"
 * list. Denormalised so each row can render without extra fetches.
 */
export type SentCoachMessageRow = {
  id: string;
  createdAt: string;
  viewedAt: string | null;
  messageText: string | null;
  kidFirstName: string;
  kidLastName: string;
  familyLastName: string;
  videoStatus: Tables<'videos'>['status'] | null;
  muxPlaybackId: string | null;
  durationSeconds: number | null;
};

type SentCoachMessageJoinRow = Pick<
  Tables<'coach_messages'>,
  'id' | 'created_at' | 'viewed_at' | 'message_text'
> & {
  kid: Pick<Tables<'kids'>, 'first_name' | 'last_name'> | null;
  family: Pick<Tables<'families'>, 'parent_last_name'> | null;
  video: Pick<
    Tables<'videos'>,
    'status' | 'mux_playback_id' | 'duration_seconds'
  > | null;
};

/**
 * Fetch every coach_messages row sent by `userId`, joined to the recipient
 * kid + family (for display labels) and the attached video (for the Mux
 * poster). Sorted newest first.
 *
 * RLS already restricts SELECT to the caller's own sent messages via
 * `coach_messages_select_own_coach`; the explicit `sender_user_id` filter
 * keeps the planner honest (and matches the index on sender_user_id).
 */
export async function listSentCoachMessages(
  userId: string,
): Promise<SentCoachMessageRow[]> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('coach_messages')
    .select(
      'id, created_at, viewed_at, message_text, kid:kids(first_name, last_name), family:families(parent_last_name), video:videos(status, mux_playback_id, duration_seconds)',
    )
    .eq('sender_user_id', userId)
    .order('created_at', { ascending: false });
  if (error) throw error;

  const rows = (data ?? []) as unknown as SentCoachMessageJoinRow[];
  return rows.map((r) => ({
    id: r.id,
    createdAt: r.created_at,
    viewedAt: r.viewed_at,
    messageText: r.message_text,
    kidFirstName: r.kid?.first_name ?? 'Unknown',
    kidLastName: r.kid?.last_name ?? '',
    familyLastName: r.family?.parent_last_name ?? '',
    videoStatus: r.video?.status ?? null,
    muxPlaybackId: r.video?.mux_playback_id ?? null,
    durationSeconds: r.video?.duration_seconds ?? null,
  }));
}

/**
 * Latest coach message addressed to a kid, denormalised for the Home card.
 * `video` is null when the row hasn't been linked to a video yet (defensive
 * — coach_messages.video_id is nullable in the schema). `coach` is null
 * when the sender isn't found in `public.coaches` (e.g. the row was sent
 * by a deactivated coach whose row was hard-deleted).
 */
export type LatestCoachMessage = {
  id: string;
  createdAt: string;
  viewedAt: string | null;
  messageText: string | null;
  video: {
    status: Tables<'videos'>['status'];
    muxPlaybackId: string | null;
    durationSeconds: number | null;
  } | null;
  coach: { firstName: string; lastName: string } | null;
};

/**
 * Fetch the most recent coach_message addressed to the given kid, with the
 * related video (status + Mux playback id + duration) and the sending
 * coach's name attached. Returns null when no message exists.
 *
 * Two round-trips because there is no FK between
 * `coach_messages.sender_user_id` (-> auth.users) and
 * `coaches.user_id`, so PostgREST can't auto-embed the relation. Doing the
 * coach lookup as a second query keeps the join explicit and lets RLS on
 * `public.coaches` (tenant-scoped) handle visibility.
 *
 * RLS on `coach_messages` already restricts parents to messages addressed
 * to their family, so no extra filter beyond `recipient_kid_id` is needed.
 */
export async function getLatestCoachMessageForKid(
  kidId: string,
): Promise<LatestCoachMessage | null> {
  const { data: msg, error: msgErr } = await supabase
    .from('coach_messages')
    .select(
      'id, created_at, viewed_at, message_text, sender_user_id, video:videos(status, mux_playback_id, duration_seconds)',
    )
    .eq('recipient_kid_id', kidId)
    // Only coach→family messages on the Home card. Parent→coach messages
    // (recipient_coach_user_id IS NOT NULL) are in the Work tab thread and
    // should not surface here as "latest video from coach".
    .is('recipient_coach_user_id', null)
    .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
    .limit(1)
    .maybeSingle();
  if (msgErr) throw msgErr;
  if (!msg) return null;

  // Supabase typings model the embedded video as either array | object | null
  // depending on inferred cardinality; normalise to a single record.
  const videoRaw = msg.video as
    | { status: Tables<'videos'>['status']; mux_playback_id: string | null; duration_seconds: number | null }
    | { status: Tables<'videos'>['status']; mux_playback_id: string | null; duration_seconds: number | null }[]
    | null;
  const v = Array.isArray(videoRaw) ? videoRaw[0] ?? null : videoRaw;

  let coach: LatestCoachMessage['coach'] = null;
  if (msg.sender_user_id) {
    const { data: c, error: coachErr } = await supabase
      .from('coaches')
      .select('first_name, last_name')
      .eq('user_id', msg.sender_user_id)
      .maybeSingle();
    if (coachErr) throw coachErr;
    if (c) coach = { firstName: c.first_name, lastName: c.last_name };
  }

  return {
    id: msg.id,
    createdAt: msg.created_at,
    viewedAt: msg.viewed_at,
    messageText: msg.message_text,
    video: v
      ? {
          status: v.status,
          muxPlaybackId: v.mux_playback_id,
          durationSeconds: v.duration_seconds,
        }
      : null,
    coach,
  };
}

/**
 * List every coach_message addressed to the given kid, newest first. Used
 * by the parent Videos → Messages sub-tab to render the full coach-video
 * rail (latest at the top + history below). RLS already restricts the
 * row set to the parent's own family. Coach-name lookup is batched into
 * a single second round-trip for the union of distinct sender ids so the
 * payload stays O(1) round-trips even for chatty coaches.
 */
export async function listCoachMessagesForKid(
  kidId: string,
  opts: { limit?: number } = {},
): Promise<LatestCoachMessage[]> {
  const limit = opts.limit ?? 100;
  const { data: rows, error } = await supabase
    .from('coach_messages')
    .select(
      'id, created_at, viewed_at, message_text, sender_user_id, video:videos(status, mux_playback_id, duration_seconds)',
    )
    .eq('recipient_kid_id', kidId)
    .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
    .limit(limit);
  if (error) throw error;
  if (!rows || rows.length === 0) return [];

  const senderIds = Array.from(
    new Set(rows.map((r) => r.sender_user_id).filter((x): x is string => !!x)),
  );
  const coachByUserId = new Map<string, { firstName: string; lastName: string }>();
  if (senderIds.length > 0) {
    const { data: coaches, error: cErr } = await supabase
      .from('coaches')
      .select('user_id, first_name, last_name')
      .in('user_id', senderIds);
    if (cErr) throw cErr;
    (coaches ?? []).forEach((c) => {
      if (!c.user_id) return;
      coachByUserId.set(c.user_id, { firstName: c.first_name, lastName: c.last_name });
    });
  }

  return rows.map((r) => {
    const videoRaw = r.video as
      | { status: Tables<'videos'>['status']; mux_playback_id: string | null; duration_seconds: number | null }
      | { status: Tables<'videos'>['status']; mux_playback_id: string | null; duration_seconds: number | null }[]
      | null;
    const v = Array.isArray(videoRaw) ? videoRaw[0] ?? null : videoRaw;
    return {
      id: r.id,
      createdAt: r.created_at,
      viewedAt: r.viewed_at,
      messageText: r.message_text,
      video: v
        ? {
            status: v.status,
            muxPlaybackId: v.mux_playback_id,
            durationSeconds: v.duration_seconds,
          }
        : null,
      coach: r.sender_user_id ? coachByUserId.get(r.sender_user_id) ?? null : null,
    };
  });
}

/**
 * Single coach_message row joined with the attached video — the projection
 * the parent's playback screen needs (Step 4.13). RLS already restricts
 * SELECT to messages addressed to the caller's family, so no extra filter
 * is required.
 */
export type CoachMessageDetail = {
  id: string;
  recipientKidId: string;
  viewedAt: string | null;
  video: {
    id: string;
    status: Tables<'videos'>['status'];
    muxPlaybackId: string | null;
    durationSeconds: number | null;
  } | null;
};

type CoachMessageDetailRow = Pick<
  Tables<'coach_messages'>,
  'id' | 'recipient_kid_id' | 'viewed_at'
> & {
  video: Pick<
    Tables<'videos'>,
    'id' | 'status' | 'mux_playback_id' | 'duration_seconds'
  > | null;
};

/**
 * Fetch a single coach_message row + its attached video by message id.
 * Returns null if the row isn't visible (RLS) or doesn't exist.
 */
export async function getCoachMessageById(
  messageId: string,
): Promise<CoachMessageDetail | null> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('coach_messages')
    .select(
      'id, recipient_kid_id, viewed_at, video:videos(id, status, mux_playback_id, duration_seconds)',
    )
    .eq('id', messageId)
    .maybeSingle();
  if (error) throw error;
  if (!data) return null;

  const row = data as unknown as CoachMessageDetailRow;
  // PostgREST may model the embedded video as object | array | null.
  const videoRaw = row.video as
    | CoachMessageDetailRow['video']
    | NonNullable<CoachMessageDetailRow['video']>[];
  const v = Array.isArray(videoRaw) ? videoRaw[0] ?? null : videoRaw;

  return {
    id: row.id,
    recipientKidId: row.recipient_kid_id,
    viewedAt: row.viewed_at,
    video: v
      ? {
          id: v.id,
          status: v.status,
          muxPlaybackId: v.mux_playback_id,
          durationSeconds: v.duration_seconds,
        }
      : null,
  };
}

/**
 * Idempotently mark a coach_message as viewed. The `viewed_at IS NULL`
 * filter means re-opening an already-viewed message is a no-op (0 rows
 * updated, no error). The column-level GRANT on `coach_messages` from
 * Step 4.1 means an UPDATE that touched any other column would be
 * rejected by Postgres before RLS even runs.
 */
export async function markCoachMessageViewed(messageId: string): Promise<void> {
  // Routed through the `mark_coach_message_viewed` SQL function (see
  // 20260505100000_v04_mark_coach_message_viewed_rpc.sql) so `viewed_at`
  // is stamped with the database's `now()` instead of the client's wall
  // clock. Avoids clock-skew drift between phones and the server. RLS +
  // the column-level UPDATE GRANT still apply (SECURITY INVOKER).
  //
  // Cast to `any` because the generated `Database` types haven't been
  // regenerated to include this RPC yet; the migration is the source of
  // truth and the function signature is fixed.
  const { error } = await (
    supabase.rpc as unknown as (
      fn: string,
      args: Record<string, unknown>,
    ) => Promise<{ error: unknown }>
  )('mark_coach_message_viewed', { p_message_id: messageId });
  if (error) throw error;
}

/**
 * Decode a single string claim from a JWT payload (base64url).
 * Server-side RLS independently validates the same claims, so a plain
 * decode without re-verification is safe for client-side UX use.
 */
function jwtStringClaim(token: string | undefined | null, key: string): string | null {
  if (!token) return null;
  try {
    const parts = token.split('.');
    if (parts.length < 2) return null;
    let b64 = parts[1].replace(/-/g, '+').replace(/_/g, '/');
    const pad = b64.length % 4;
    if (pad) b64 += '='.repeat(4 - pad);
    const payload = JSON.parse(globalThis.atob(b64)) as Record<string, unknown>;
    const val = payload[key];
    return typeof val === 'string' ? val : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

/**
 * Insert a row into `public.coach_messages`. Mirrors `createBooking` in
 * `bookings.ts` — relies on RLS to reject any attempt to smuggle a row
 * into another tenant or impersonate another sender.
 *
 * tenant_id is read from the caller's `public.coaches` row when available.
 * For admin / owner / super_admin callers who have no coaches row by design,
 * falls back to the tenant_id claim in the JWT access token (same value,
 * different source — the server enforces RLS using the JWT claim directly).
 * sender_user_id is taken from `supabase.auth.getUser()` so the value
 * matches what auth.uid() will resolve to inside the RLS policy.
 * We `.select().single()` so callers get the freshly-inserted row
 * (id + created_at) for cache priming on the sent-videos list later.
 */
/**
 * Send a text-only reply from a coach to a family thread.
 * Unlike `sendCoachMessage` (which requires a videoId for the initial
 * video message), this is used for follow-up text replies in an existing thread.
 */
export async function sendCoachTextReply(input: {
  recipientFamilyId: string;
  recipientKidId: string;
  messageText: string;
}): Promise<SentCoachMessage> {
  const {
    data: { user },
    error: userErr,
  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
  if (userErr) throw userErr;
  if (!user) throw new Error('You appear to be signed out. Sign back in and try again.');

  const { data: coach, error: coachErr } = await supabase
    .from('coaches')
    .select('tenant_id')
    .eq('user_id', user.id)
    .maybeSingle();
  if (coachErr) throw coachErr;
  if (!coach) throw new Error('Coach profile not found for the current user.');

  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('coach_messages')
    .insert({
      tenant_id: coach.tenant_id,
      sender_user_id: user.id,
      video_id: null,
      recipient_family_id: input.recipientFamilyId,
      recipient_kid_id: input.recipientKidId,
      message_text: input.messageText,
    })
    .select('*')
    .single();
  if (error) throw error;
  return data;
}

export async function sendCoachMessage(
  input: SendCoachMessageInput,
): Promise<SentCoachMessage> {
  const {
    data: { user },
    error: userErr,
  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
  if (userErr) throw userErr;
  if (!user) throw new Error('You appear to be signed out. Sign back in and try again.');

  const { data: sessionData } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
  const accessToken = sessionData.session?.access_token;
  const appRole = jwtStringClaim(accessToken, 'app_role');
  const staffRoles = ['admin', 'owner', 'super_admin'];

  const { data: coach, error: coachErr } = await supabase
    .from('coaches')
    .select('tenant_id')
    .eq('user_id', user.id)
    .maybeSingle();
  if (coachErr) throw coachErr;

  // Admin / owner / super_admin users have no coaches row by design.
  // Fall back to the JWT tenant_id claim so they can send messages.
  const tenantId =
    coach?.tenant_id ??
    (staffRoles.includes(appRole ?? '') ? jwtStringClaim(accessToken, 'tenant_id') : null);
  if (!tenantId) {
    throw new Error('Could not resolve tenant. Sign out, sign back in, and try again.');
  }

  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('coach_messages')
    .insert({
      tenant_id: tenantId,
      sender_user_id: user.id,
      video_id: input.videoId,
      recipient_family_id: input.recipientFamilyId,
      recipient_kid_id: input.recipientKidId,
      message_text: input.messageText,
    })
    .select('*')
    .single();
  if (error) throw error;
  return data;
}

/**
 * Earn API helpers — products catalogue, orders history, points ledger,
 * leaderboard, and the redeem RPC wrapper.
 *
 * All tenant scoping is enforced by RLS in the v0.5 migration; client just
 * passes the kid/product ids and the database verifies ownership.
 */

import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';
import type { Tables } from '@/types/database';

export type Product = Tables<'products'>;
export type Order = Tables<'orders'>;
export type PointsLedgerEntry = Tables<'points_ledger'>;

export type OrderWithProduct = Order & {
  product: Pick<Product, 'id' | 'name' | 'category' | 'image_url'> | null;
  kid: Pick<Tables<'kids'>, 'id' | 'first_name' | 'last_name'> | null;
};

export type LeaderboardEntry = {
  kidId: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  pointsBalance: number;
  rank: number;
};

/**
 * All active products visible to the caller's tenant. Sorted by sort_order
 * (matches the seed) so the Rewards / Store grids stay deterministic.
 */
export async function listProducts(): Promise<Product[]> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('products')
    .select('*')
    .eq('is_active', true)
    .order('sort_order', { ascending: true })
    .order('name', { ascending: true });
  if (error) throw error;
  return data ?? [];
}

/**
 * Family order history. RLS narrows to the caller's family (or to all
 * tenant orders for coaches, but this hook is parent-only).
 */
export async function listOrders(): Promise<OrderWithProduct[]> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('orders')
    .select(
      'id, tenant_id, family_id, kid_id, product_id, payment_method, amount_paid_points, amount_paid_cents, stripe_payment_intent_id, status, redemption_code, fulfilled_at, created_at, updated_at, product:products(id, name, category, image_url), kid:kids(id, first_name, last_name)',
    )
    .order('created_at', { ascending: false });
  if (error) throw error;
  return (data ?? []) as unknown as OrderWithProduct[];
}

/**
 * Per-kid points history (most-recent first). Includes both grants
 * (sessions, etc.) and spends (redemptions).
 */
export async function listPointsLedger(kidId: string): Promise<PointsLedgerEntry[]> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('points_ledger')
    .select('*')
    .eq('kid_id', kidId)
    .order('created_at', { ascending: false })
    .limit(100);
  if (error) throw error;
  return data ?? [];
}

/**
 * Live tenant leaderboard. Reads the kids table directly (RLS
 * `kids_select_tenant` returns every kid in the caller's tenant) and ranks
 * by points_balance desc. v0.5+ may move this to a nightly snapshot table.
 */
export async function listLeaderboard(): Promise<LeaderboardEntry[]> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('kids')
    .select('id, first_name, last_name, points_balance')
    .order('points_balance', { ascending: false })
    .order('first_name', { ascending: true })
    .limit(50);
  if (error) throw error;
  let rank = 0;
  let prevPoints: number | null = null;
  let stride = 0;
  return (data ?? []).map((row) => {
    stride += 1;
    if (prevPoints === null || row.points_balance !== prevPoints) {
      rank = stride;
      prevPoints = row.points_balance;
    }
    return {
      kidId: row.id,
      firstName: row.first_name,
      lastName: row.last_name,
      pointsBalance: row.points_balance ?? 0,
      rank,
    };
  });
}

export type RedeemResult = {
  orderId: string;
  redemptionCode: string;
  newBalance: number;
};

/**
 * Wraps the `redeem_reward_for_kid` RPC. Server-side it locks the kid +
 * product rows, verifies ownership, decrements the balance, and inserts
 * the order + ledger row atomically. Throws on insufficient points,
 * inactive product, or wrong tenant — the API layer just forwards the
 * Postgres error message up.
 */
/**
 * Look up a single order by its 8-char redemption code (upper-cased before
 * querying). RLS allows coaches and admins to SELECT any order in their
 * tenant, so this works for the coach-side scanner without needing a
 * special RPC.
 */
export async function lookupOrderByRedemptionCode(
  code: string,
): Promise<OrderWithProduct | null> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('orders')
    .select(
      'id, tenant_id, family_id, kid_id, product_id, payment_method, amount_paid_points, amount_paid_cents, stripe_payment_intent_id, status, redemption_code, fulfilled_at, created_at, updated_at, product:products(id, name, category, image_url), kid:kids(id, first_name, last_name)',
    )
    .eq('redemption_code', code.toUpperCase().trim())
    .maybeSingle();
  if (error) throw error;
  return (data ?? null) as unknown as OrderWithProduct | null;
}

/**
 * Calls the `mark_redemption_fulfilled` SECURITY DEFINER RPC. Requires the
 * caller to have app_role = 'admin' or 'coach'. Returns the updated order.
 * Idempotent — calling again on an already-fulfilled order returns it as-is.
 */
export async function fulfillRedemption(code: string): Promise<Order> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc('mark_redemption_fulfilled', {
    p_code: code,
  });
  if (error) throw error;
  const row = Array.isArray(data) ? data[0] : data;
  if (!row) throw new Error('fulfillRedemption returned no row');
  return row as unknown as Order;
}

export async function redeemReward(input: {
  kidId: string;
  productId: string;
}): Promise<RedeemResult> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc('redeem_reward_for_kid', {
    p_kid_id: input.kidId,
    p_product_id: input.productId,
  });
  if (error) throw error;
  const row = Array.isArray(data) ? data[0] : data;
  if (!row) throw new Error('Redemption returned no row');
  return {
    orderId: row.order_id,
    redemptionCode: row.redemption_code,
    newBalance: row.new_balance,
  };
}

/**
 * Swing favorites API helpers (task #119).
 *
 * The toggle goes through the SECURITY DEFINER RPC `toggle_swing_favorite`
 * so the kid_id + tenant_id pinning + ownership check happen in one
 * server round-trip and a malicious client can't favourite a swing from
 * another family. The RPC returns the new state (true = now favorited).
 *
 * Reads can use the table directly because RLS already scopes by
 * parent_user_id = auth.uid().
 */

import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';

/** Set of swing_ids currently favorited by the calling parent. */
export async function listFavoriteSwingIds(): Promise<Set<string>> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('kid_swing_favorites')
    .select('swing_id');
  if (error) throw error;
  return new Set((data ?? []).map((r) => (r as { swing_id: string }).swing_id));
}

/** Toggle. Returns true if the swing is now favorited, false otherwise. */
export async function toggleSwingFavorite(swingId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.rpc('toggle_swing_favorite', {
    p_swing_id: swingId,
  });
  if (error) throw error;
  return Boolean(data);
}

/**
 * HitTrax API helpers — v1.3 flow.
 *
 * Thin wrappers around the HitTrax-related Edge Functions:
 *   - hittrax-associate   POST (three modes — see below)
 *   - hittrax-disconnect  POST { kid_id }
 *
 * Association modes:
 *   Mode 1 – password:    { kid_id, hittrax_username, hittrax_password }
 *   Mode 2 – OTP trigger: { kid_id, hittrax_username, use_otp: true }
 *     → HitTrax texts a code to the user's registered phone.
 *     → Returns { status: 'otp_sent' }. No DB write yet.
 *   Mode 3 – OTP submit:  { kid_id, hittrax_username, otp_code: string }
 *     → Completes association using the SMS code.
 *
 * Modes 1 & 3 return { link_id, association_status: 'active', hittrax_username }.
 * The link goes directly to 'active' — no email confirmation / pending state.
 *
 * getHitTraxLinkForKid excludes `third_party_user_password` so a leaked
 * client log never spills the HitTrax-issued credential.
 */

import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';

import type { Database } from '@/types/database';

type KidCaptureLinkRow = Database['public']['Tables']['kid_capture_links']['Row'];
export type KidCaptureLink = Omit<
  Pick<
    KidCaptureLinkRow,
    | 'id'
    | 'kid_id'
    | 'external_user_id'
    | 'hittrax_registration_status'
    | 'hittrax_release_status'
    | 'associated_at'
    | 'removed_at'
    | 'last_polled_through'
    | 'last_polled_at'
    | 'last_poll_error'
    | 'created_at'
    | 'updated_at'
  >,
  never
> & {
  capture_source: 'hittrax' | 'rapsodo';
  association_status: 'pending' | 'active' | 'declined' | 'removed';
};

const SAFE_COLUMNS =
  'id, kid_id, capture_source, external_user_id, hittrax_registration_status, hittrax_release_status, association_status, associated_at, removed_at, last_polled_through, last_polled_at, last_poll_error, created_at, updated_at';

/** Read the HitTrax link (if any) for a single kid. Excludes the password. */
export async function getHitTraxLinkForKid(
  kidId: string,
): Promise<KidCaptureLink | null> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('kid_capture_links')
    .select(SAFE_COLUMNS)
    .eq('kid_id', kidId)
    .eq('capture_source', 'hittrax')
    .maybeSingle();
  if (error) throw error;
  return (data as KidCaptureLink | null) ?? null;
}

/** v1.3: association is immediate — link goes straight to 'active'. */
export type AssociateResponse = {
  link_id: string;
  association_status: 'active';
  hittrax_username: string;
};

/** Returned by Mode 2 (OTP trigger). No DB write — SMS was sent. */
export type OTPTriggerResponse = {
  status: 'otp_sent';
};

/**
 * Extract a human-readable message from a Supabase FunctionsError.
 * `FunctionsHttpError.context` is the raw Response — read its JSON body to
 * surface the server-side error message. Falls back to the SDK message.
 */
async function extractFunctionError(error: unknown): Promise<string> {
  try {
    const ctx = (error as { context?: unknown }).context;
    if (ctx instanceof Response) {
      const body = await ctx.json().catch(() => null);
      const serverMessage = body?.error?.message;
      if (typeof serverMessage === 'string' && serverMessage.length > 0) {
        return serverMessage;
      }
    }
  } catch {
    // ignore — fall through to error.message
  }
  return (error as { message?: string }).message ?? 'An unexpected error occurred.';
}

/**
 * Mode 1: Associate using HitTrax username + password.
 * The password is used once server-side to authenticate; it is never stored.
 */
export async function associateHitTrax(
  kidId: string,
  hittraxUsername: string,
  hittraxPassword: string,
): Promise<AssociateResponse> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke('hittrax-associate', {
    body: { kid_id: kidId, hittrax_username: hittraxUsername, hittrax_password: hittraxPassword },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(await extractFunctionError(error));
  return data as AssociateResponse;
}

/**
 * Mode 2: Trigger OTP — HitTrax sends an SMS code to the user's registered phone.
 * No association happens yet. Call associateHitTraxWithOTP() after the user
 * enters the code they receive.
 */
export async function triggerHitTraxOTP(
  kidId: string,
  hittraxUsername: string,
): Promise<OTPTriggerResponse> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke('hittrax-associate', {
    body: { kid_id: kidId, hittrax_username: hittraxUsername, use_otp: true },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(await extractFunctionError(error));
  return data as OTPTriggerResponse;
}

/**
 * Mode 3: Complete association using the SMS code the user received.
 * The code is submitted to HitTrax to get a session token, then the account
 * is associated and the link goes straight to 'active'.
 */
export async function associateHitTraxWithOTP(
  kidId: string,
  hittraxUsername: string,
  otpCode: string,
): Promise<AssociateResponse> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke('hittrax-associate', {
    body: { kid_id: kidId, hittrax_username: hittraxUsername, otp_code: otpCode },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(await extractFunctionError(error));
  return data as AssociateResponse;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Create HitTrax account in-app
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export type CreateHitTraxAccountInput = {
  kidId: string;
  hittraxUsername: string;
  password: string;
  sport: 'Baseball' | 'Fastpitch Softball' | 'Slowpitch Softball';
  skillLevel: string;
  gender: 'male' | 'female' | 'other';
  position?: string;
  bats?: 'Right' | 'Left' | 'Switch';
  throws?: 'Right' | 'Left';
  heightInches?: number;
};

/**
 * Create a new HitTrax Cloud account for the kid. The account is
 * pre-linked to Ballpark — the link goes straight to 'active' with no
 * extra association step.
 */
export async function createHitTraxAccount(
  input: CreateHitTraxAccountInput,
): Promise<AssociateResponse> {
  const { kidId, hittraxUsername, password, sport, skillLevel, gender, position, bats, throws: throws_, heightInches } = input;
  const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke('hittrax-create-account', {
    body: {
      kid_id: kidId,
      hittrax_username: hittraxUsername,
      password,
      sport,
      skill_level: skillLevel,
      gender,
      ...(position ? { position } : {}),
      ...(bats ? { bats } : {}),
      ...(throws_ ? { throws: throws_ } : {}),
      ...(heightInches !== undefined ? { height_inches: heightInches } : {}),
    },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(await extractFunctionError(error));
  return data as AssociateResponse;
}

/**
 * Check whether a HitTrax username is available.
 * Returns true if the username can be registered, false if already taken.
 */
export async function checkHitTraxUsernameAvailable(username: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke('hittrax-create-account', {
    body: { check_username: username },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(await extractFunctionError(error));
  return (data as { available: boolean }).available;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Kiosk QR scan
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export type KioskEventResponse = {
  ok: true;
  event_type: string;
  kiosk_response: string;
};

/**
 * Fire a HitTrax kiosk event for the kid by scanning the kiosk QR code.
 * The QR code URL is validated server-side against the configured HitTrax
 * server origin before credentials are appended.
 */
export async function notifyKioskEvent(
  kidId: string,
  qrUrl: string,
): Promise<KioskEventResponse> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke('hittrax-kiosk-event', {
    body: { kid_id: kidId, qr_url: qrUrl },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(await extractFunctionError(error));
  return data as KioskEventResponse;
}

/** Disconnect a kid's HitTrax link (remove association + flip status). */
export async function disconnectHitTrax(kidId: string): Promise<{ link_id: string }> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase.functions.invoke('hittrax-disconnect', {
    body: { kid_id: kidId },
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(await extractFunctionError(error));
  return data as { link_id: string };
}

/**
 * Leaderboard API helpers — HitTrax all-time records and lesson-count board.
 *
 * Both RPCs are SECURITY DEFINER and tenant-pin via JWT; the client only
 * passes the filter params. Tenant_id is derived server-side from the claim.
 */

import type { SupabaseClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';

import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';

// Cast to the un-typed client until next database.ts regen picks up the
// new RPCs from the migration.
const sb: SupabaseClient = supabase as unknown as SupabaseClient;

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Types
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export type HitTraxMetric = 'exit_velocity_mph' | 'distance_ft';
export type LeaderboardScope = 'national' | 'clubhouse';
export type AgeGroupFilter = string | null;  // '8U' | '10U' | '12U' | '14U' | 'HS' | 'College' | null

export type HitTraxLeaderboardEntry = {
  kidId: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  ageGroup: string | null;
  value: number;
  rank: number;
};

export type LessonCountLeaderboardEntry = {
  kidId: string;
  firstName: string;
  lastName: string;
  lessonCount: number;
  rank: number;
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// HitTrax leaderboard
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Returns top-50 all-time personal bests for the given metric, optionally
 * scoped by age group and/or location.
 *
 * p_scope = 'national'  → all kids in the tenant (all locations)
 * p_scope = 'clubhouse' → only kids whose primary_location_id matches
 */
export async function getHitTraxLeaderboard(opts: {
  metric: HitTraxMetric;
  scope?: LeaderboardScope;
  locationId?: string | null;
  ageGroup?: AgeGroupFilter;
}): Promise<HitTraxLeaderboardEntry[]> {
  const { metric, scope = 'national', locationId = null, ageGroup = null } = opts;

  const { data, error } = await sb.rpc('get_hittrax_leaderboard', {
    p_metric:      metric,
    p_scope:       scope,
    p_location_id: locationId,
    p_age_group:   ageGroup,
  });

  if (error) throw error;

  return ((data as unknown[]) ?? []).map((row: unknown) => {
    const r = row as {
      kid_id: string;
      first_name: string;
      last_name: string;
      age_group: string | null;
      value: number;
      rank: number;
    };
    return {
      kidId:     r.kid_id,
      firstName: r.first_name,
      lastName:  r.last_name,
      ageGroup:  r.age_group,
      value:     Number(r.value),
      rank:      Number(r.rank),
    };
  });
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Lesson-count leaderboard
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * Returns top-50 active members ranked by total completed bookings at the
 * given location. Pass null to see all locations in the tenant.
 */
export async function getLessonCountLeaderboard(opts: {
  locationId?: string | null;
}): Promise<LessonCountLeaderboardEntry[]> {
  const { locationId = null } = opts;

  const { data, error } = await sb.rpc('get_lesson_count_leaderboard', {
    p_location_id: locationId,
  });

  if (error) throw error;

  return ((data as unknown[]) ?? []).map((row: unknown) => {
    const r = row as {
      kid_id: string;
      first_name: string;
      last_name: string;
      lesson_count: number;
      rank: number;
    };
    return {
      kidId:       r.kid_id,
      firstName:   r.first_name,
      lastName:    r.last_name,
      lessonCount: Number(r.lesson_count),
      rank:        Number(r.rank),
    };
  });
}

/**
 * Memberships API helpers.
 *
 * Thin wrappers around the memberships table and session-credit RPCs.
 * RLS restricts parents to their own family's memberships via the
 * `memberships_parent_select` policy added in migration
 * 20260602000010_session_packs_credit_tracking.sql.
 *
 * The session-credit RPCs are called via the untyped client because they are
 * not yet in the generated database.ts types. This is the established project
 * pattern for post-regen RPCs — see replit.md "Generated types caveat".
 */

import type { SupabaseClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';

export type ActiveMembership = {
  id: string;
  plan_name: string;
  plan_type: 'eft' | 'otc';
  status: string;
  /** OTC pack: total sessions in the pack. Null for EFT. */
  sessions_total: number | null;
  /** OTC pack: sessions remaining. Null for EFT. */
  sessions_remaining: number | null;
  /**
   * EFT limited: max sessions allowed per week.
   * Null = unlimited EFT (no enforcement).
   */
  sessions_per_week: number | null;
  /** EFT: sessions already used in the current weekly period. */
  weekly_sessions_used: number;
  /** EFT: ISO date string of Monday that starts the current period. */
  weekly_period_start: string | null;
  started_at: string;
};

const untypedClient = supabase as unknown as SupabaseClient;

/**
 * Fetch the most-recent active membership for the given kid + tenant.
 * Returns null if the kid has no active membership.
 *
 * Includes EFT weekly-credit fields added in migration
 * 20260610000000_eft_weekly_credits.sql — accessed via untyped client
 * until the next generated-types regen.
 */
export async function getActiveMembership(
  kidId: string,
  tenantId: string,
): Promise<ActiveMembership | null> {
  const { data, error } = await untypedClient
    .from('memberships')
    .select(
      'id, plan_name, plan_type, status, sessions_total, sessions_remaining, sessions_per_week, weekly_sessions_used, weekly_period_start, started_at',
    )
    .eq('kid_id', kidId)
    .eq('tenant_id', tenantId)
    .eq('status', 'active')
    .order('started_at', { ascending: false })
    .limit(1)
    .maybeSingle();
  if (error) throw error;
  if (!data) return null;
  const row = data as Record<string, unknown>;
  return {
    id:                   row.id as string,
    plan_name:            row.plan_name as string,
    plan_type:            row.plan_type as 'eft' | 'otc',
    status:               row.status as string,
    sessions_total:       (row.sessions_total as number | null) ?? null,
    sessions_remaining:   (row.sessions_remaining as number | null) ?? null,
    sessions_per_week:    (row.sessions_per_week as number | null) ?? null,
    weekly_sessions_used: (row.weekly_sessions_used as number) ?? 0,
    weekly_period_start:  (row.weekly_period_start as string | null) ?? null,
    started_at:           row.started_at as string,
  };
}

/**
 * Pre-booking check: returns the number of sessions remaining for the kid's
 * active OTC pack, or EFT weekly allowance, or -1 if unlimited.
 *
 * Call this BEFORE inserting the booking to give the user a clear
 * error before hitting the DB.  The real race-condition guard lives in
 * `deduct_session_credit` (uses FOR UPDATE).
 */
export async function checkSessionCredits(
  kidId: string,
  tenantId: string,
): Promise<number> {
  const { data, error } = await untypedClient.rpc('check_session_credits', {
    p_kid_id: kidId,
    p_tenant_id: tenantId,
  });
  if (error) throw error;
  return typeof data === 'number' ? data : -1;
}

/**
 * Atomically decrement the kid's session credit by 1.
 * Returns the new (post-decrement) balance, or -1 for unlimited.
 * Throws if sessions are already exhausted.
 */
export async function deductSessionCredit(bookingId: string): Promise<number> {
  const { data, error } = await untypedClient.rpc('deduct_session_credit', {
    p_booking_id: bookingId,
  });
  if (error) throw error;
  return typeof data === 'number' ? data : -1;
}

/**
 * Atomically decrement the kid's session credits by N (for Bring-a-Friend).
 * Returns the new (post-decrement) balance, or -1 for unlimited/untracked.
 * Throws 'no_session_credits' if remaining < n.
 */
export async function deductSessionCredits(kidId: string, n: number): Promise<number> {
  const { data, error } = await untypedClient.rpc('deduct_session_credits', {
    p_kid_id: kidId,
    p_n: n,
  });
  if (error) throw error;
  return typeof data === 'number' ? data : -1;
}

/**
 * Restore one session credit when a future-dated booking is cancelled.
 * Returns the new balance, or -1 for unlimited/untracked memberships,
 * or -2 if the credit was already restored (idempotent no-op).
 */
export async function restoreSessionCredit(bookingId: string): Promise<number> {
  const { data, error } = await untypedClient.rpc('restore_session_credit', {
    p_booking_id: bookingId,
  });
  if (error) throw error;
  return typeof data === 'number' ? data : -1;
}

/**
 * Atomically book a primary session + a guest (Bring-a-Friend) in one
 * database transaction:
 *   1. Deduct 2 credits (OTC or EFT weekly, FOR UPDATE lock)
 *   2. Insert primary booking row (is_guest = false)
 *   3. Insert guest booking row  (is_guest = true)
 *   4. Insert points_ledger +100, reason = 'bring_a_friend'
 *
 * Returns { primary_booking_id, guest_booking_id, sessions_remaining,
 *           weekly_sessions_remaining }.
 * Throws 'no_session_credits' if balance < 2.
 */
export type BookWithFriendResult = {
  primary_booking_id: string;
  guest_booking_id: string;
  sessions_remaining: number;
  weekly_sessions_remaining: number;
};

export async function bookSessionWithFriend(params: {
  tenant_id: string;
  location_id: string;
  kid_id: string;
  coach_id: string;
  session_type_id: string;
  scheduled_start: string;
  scheduled_end: string;
  guest_name: string;
  guest_phone?: string | null;
  guest_email?: string | null;
}): Promise<BookWithFriendResult> {
  const { data, error } = await untypedClient.rpc('book_session_with_friend', {
    p_tenant_id:        params.tenant_id,
    p_location_id:      params.location_id,
    p_kid_id:           params.kid_id,
    p_coach_id:         params.coach_id,
    p_session_type_id:  params.session_type_id,
    p_scheduled_start:  params.scheduled_start,
    p_scheduled_end:    params.scheduled_end,
    p_guest_name:       params.guest_name,
    p_guest_phone:      params.guest_phone ?? null,
    p_guest_email:      params.guest_email ?? null,
  });
  if (error) throw error;
  const row = data as {
    primary_booking_id: string;
    guest_booking_id: string;
    sessions_remaining: number;
    weekly_sessions_remaining?: number;
  };
  return {
    primary_booking_id:        row.primary_booking_id,
    guest_booking_id:          row.guest_booking_id,
    sessions_remaining:        typeof row.sessions_remaining === 'number' ? row.sessions_remaining : -1,
    weekly_sessions_remaining: typeof row.weekly_sessions_remaining === 'number' ? row.weekly_sessions_remaining : -1,
  };
}

/**
 * Award 100 bonus points to the kid for using Bring-a-Friend.
 * Writes a points_ledger row with reason 'bring_a_friend'.
 */
export async function addBringAFriendPoints(
  kidId: string,
  tenantId: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const { error } = await (supabase as unknown as SupabaseClient)
    .from('points_ledger')
    .insert({
      kid_id: kidId,
      tenant_id: tenantId,
      delta: 100,
      reason: 'bring_a_friend',
    });
  if (error) throw error;
}

import type { SupabaseClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';

    .select('id, plan_name, plan_type, status, amount_cents, billing_anchor_day, stripe_subscription_id, pause_start, pause_end, contract_url, payment_failed_at')

  tenantId: string,
  currentAmountCents: number,

    .from('membership_plans')
    .select('id, name, plan_type, amount_cents, description, sort_order')
    .eq('tenant_id', tenantId)
    .eq('is_active', true)
    .gt('amount_cents', currentAmountCents)
    .order('sort_order', { ascending: true });

  if (error) throw new Error(errorMessage(error));

export async function requestUpgrade(
  membershipId: string,
  requestedPlanId: string,
): Promise<void> {
  const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
  if (!session) throw new Error('Not authenticated');

  const supabaseUrl = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
  if (!supabaseUrl) throw new Error('EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL not configured');

  const res = await fetch(`${supabaseUrl}/functions/v1/request-membership-upgrade`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: {
      'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      Authorization: `Bearer ${session.access_token}`,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ membership_id: membershipId, requested_plan_id: requestedPlanId }),
  });

  const body = await res.json() as { ok?: boolean; error?: { message?: string; code?: string } };
  if (!res.ok || !body.ok) {
    const msg = typeof body.error === 'object'
      ? body.error?.message ?? `Error ${res.status}`
      : String(body.error ?? `Error ${res.status}`);
    throw new Error(msg);
  }
}

FILE: src/api/mux.ts

/**
 * Mux API helpers (client side).
 *
 * `createMuxUpload` calls our `mux-create-upload` Edge Function (Step 4.4),
 * which mints a Mux Direct Upload URL and inserts the corresponding
 * `public.videos` row. The function authorizes the caller from the JWT and
 * pins `tenant_id` / `uploaded_by_user_id` server-side, so the client must
 * NOT send those fields — only an `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` header and an
 * `Idempotency-Key` so a flaky retry returns the SAME upload row instead of
 * creating a duplicate.
 *
 * Errors from the function come back as `{ error: { code, message } }`; we
 * surface them through the same `errorMessage()` shape the rest of the app
 * uses, so `catch (err) { Alert.alert(..., errorMessage(err)); }` Just Works.
 */

import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';

const SUPABASE_URL = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;

if (!SUPABASE_URL) {
  // Mirrors src/lib/supabase.ts — fail loudly instead of silently calling
  // `undefined/functions/...`.
  throw new Error('EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL is not set');
}

const FUNCTION_URL = `${SUPABASE_URL.replace(/\/$/, '')}/functions/v1/mux-create-upload`;

export type MuxUpload = {
  upload_url: string;
  video_id: string;
};

type MuxFunctionErrorBody = {
  error?: { code?: string; message?: string };
};

/**
 * Thrown when the Edge Function returns a structured error. Carries the
 * server `code` so callers can branch (e.g. show a special message on
 * `forbidden`) and `errorMessage()` formats it as `"<msg> [<code>]"` to
 * match how `bookings.ts` surfaces PostgrestError shapes.
 */
export class MuxFunctionError extends Error {
  code: string;
  status: number;
  details?: string;
  constructor(opts: { code: string; message: string; status: number; details?: string }) {
    super(opts.message);
    this.name = 'MuxFunctionError';
    this.code = opts.code;
    this.status = opts.status;
    this.details = opts.details;
  }
}

/**
 * Mint a fresh Mux Direct Upload. Returns `{ upload_url, video_id }` on
 * success. Pass the SAME `idempotencyKey` for any retries of the same
 * user-initiated attempt so we don't create duplicate `videos` rows; only
 * generate a new key when the coach picks a different video.
 */
export type MuxUploadPurpose = 'coach_message' | 'drill' | 'parent_to_coach';

export async function createMuxUpload(
  idempotencyKey: string,
  purpose: MuxUploadPurpose = 'coach_message',
): Promise<MuxUpload> {
  const { data: sessionData, error: sessionErr } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
  if (sessionErr) throw sessionErr;
  const accessToken = sessionData.session?.access_token;
  if (!accessToken) {
    throw new MuxFunctionError({
      code: 'no_session',
      message: 'You are signed out. Sign back in and try again.',
      status: 401,
    });
  }

  let res: Response;
  try {
    res = await fetch(FUNCTION_URL, {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        Authorization: `Bearer ${accessToken}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
        'Idempotency-Key': idempotencyKey,
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({ purpose }),
    });
  } catch (err) {
    throw new MuxFunctionError({
      code: 'network_error',
      message: 'Could not reach the upload service. Check your connection and try again.',
      status: 0,
      details: err instanceof Error ? err.message : undefined,
    });
  }

  // Try to parse the JSON body whether the call succeeded or failed; the
  // function returns JSON in both cases.
  let body: (MuxUpload & MuxFunctionErrorBody) | null = null;
  try {
    body = (await res.json()) as MuxUpload & MuxFunctionErrorBody;
  } catch {
    body = null;
  }

  if (!res.ok) {
    const code = body?.error?.code ?? 'function_error';
    const message =
      body?.error?.message ?? `Upload service returned status ${res.status}`;
    throw new MuxFunctionError({ code, message, status: res.status });
  }

  if (!body?.upload_url || !body?.video_id) {
    throw new MuxFunctionError({
      code: 'bad_response',
      message: 'Upload service returned an unexpected response.',
      status: res.status,
    });
  }

  return { upload_url: body.upload_url, video_id: body.video_id };
}

/**
 * Parent-side messaging API (v0.7 task #120).
 *
 * Mirrors src/api/coachMessages.ts but flips the direction: the parent is
 * the SENDER, the addressed coach is pinned in
 * `coach_messages.recipient_coach_user_id` (added by migration
 * 20260509000000). Coach access to those rows is granted by RLS policy
 * `coach_messages_select_recipient_coach` — i.e. only the addressed coach
 * (and the parent sender, via `coach_messages_select_parent_sender`) can
 * read the row.
 *
 * Tables touched:
 *   coach_messages    insert with sender_user_id = parent.user_id,
 *                     recipient_coach_user_id = picked coach, label,
 *                     sender_display, optional video_id (parent_to_coach).
 *   coaches           list tenant coaches so the composer / inbox can show
 *                     a "to: <coach>" affordance.
 *
 * RLS is enforced server-side. The client passes tenant_id explicitly
 * because the policy WITH CHECK requires it on the row itself.
 */

import { supabase, supabaseExt } from '@/lib/supabase';
import type { Tables } from '@/types/database';
import type { DatabaseExt } from '@/types/databaseExt';

// `supabaseExt` is the same connection / session as `supabase` but typed
// against `DatabaseExt`, which augments the generated types with the
// columns added by 20260509000000 (`label`, `sender_display`,
// `recipient_coach_user_id`). When the types are regenerated, swap
// `supabaseExt` -> `supabase` and delete `src/types/databaseExt.ts`.
type CoachMessageRowExt =
  DatabaseExt['public']['Tables']['coach_messages']['Row'];
type CoachMessageInsertExt =
  DatabaseExt['public']['Tables']['coach_messages']['Insert'];

export type ComposerLabel =
  | 'game_footage'
  | 'home_practice'
  | 'swing_check'
  | 'question'
  | 'other';

export const COMPOSER_LABELS: { value: ComposerLabel; label: string }[] = [
  { value: 'game_footage', label: 'Game footage' },
  { value: 'home_practice', label: 'Home practice' },
  { value: 'swing_check', label: 'Swing check' },
  { value: 'question', label: 'Question' },
  { value: 'other', label: 'Other' },
];

/** Lightweight coach projection for the composer + inbox. */
export type TenantCoach = {
  userId: string;
  firstName: string | null;
  lastName: string | null;
  avatarUrl: string | null;
};

/**
 * List every coach in the parent's tenant. Parents have a SELECT policy on
 * `public.coaches` introduced in v0.5 (`coaches_select_same_tenant`). We
 * return the lot — there's typically a handful per facility — and let the
 * UI pick a default (most-recent contacted, then alphabetical).
 */
export async function listTenantCoachesForParent(): Promise<TenantCoach[]> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('coaches')
    .select('user_id, first_name, last_name, avatar_url');
  if (error) throw error;
  return (data ?? [])
    .filter((c): c is typeof c & { user_id: string } => !!c.user_id)
    .map((c) => ({
      userId: c.user_id,
      firstName: c.first_name,
      lastName: c.last_name,
      avatarUrl: c.avatar_url,
    }));
}

/**
 * Input shape for `sendParentMessage`. Mirrors `SendCoachMessageInput`
 * with parent-side additions (`label`, `senderDisplay`).
 */
export type SendParentMessageInput = {
  videoId: string | null;
  recipientFamilyId: string;
  recipientKidId: string;
  recipientCoachUserId: string;
  label: ComposerLabel | null;
  senderDisplay: string | null;
  messageText: string | null;
};

export type SentParentMessage = CoachMessageRowExt;

/**
 * Insert a parent->coach row. Tenant + sender are looked up from the
 * caller's session/family so the client can't smuggle either.
 */
export async function sendParentMessage(
  input: SendParentMessageInput,
): Promise<SentParentMessage> {
  const {
    data: { user },
    error: userErr,
  } = await supabase.auth.getUser();
  if (userErr) throw userErr;
  if (!user) throw new Error('You appear to be signed out. Sign back in and try again.');

  const { data: family, error: famErr } = await supabase
    .from('families')
    .select('tenant_id')
    .eq('parent_user_id', user.id)
    .maybeSingle();
  if (famErr) throw famErr;
  if (!family) throw new Error('Family profile not found for the current user.');

  const insertRow: CoachMessageInsertExt = {
    tenant_id: family.tenant_id,
    sender_user_id: user.id,
    video_id: input.videoId,
    recipient_family_id: input.recipientFamilyId,
    recipient_kid_id: input.recipientKidId,
    recipient_coach_user_id: input.recipientCoachUserId,
    message_text: input.messageText,
    label: input.label,
    sender_display: input.senderDisplay,
  };
  const { data, error } = await supabaseExt
    .from('coach_messages')
    .insert(insertRow)
    .select('*')
    .single();
  if (error) throw error;
  return data;
}

/**
 * Row in the bidirectional message thread. Sender side is decided by the
 * caller comparing `senderUserId` to their own `auth.uid()`.
 */
export type ThreadMessage = {
  id: string;
  createdAt: string;
  senderUserId: string;
  recipientFamilyId: string;
  recipientKidId: string;
  recipientCoachUserId: string | null;
  messageText: string | null;
  label: string | null;
  senderDisplay: string | null;
  viewedAt: string | null;
  video: {
    id: string;
    status: string;
    muxPlaybackId: string | null;
    durationSeconds: number | null;
    purpose: string;
  } | null;
};

type ThreadJoinRow = {
  id: string;
  created_at: string;
  sender_user_id: string;
  recipient_family_id: string;
  recipient_kid_id: string;
  recipient_coach_user_id: string | null;
  message_text: string | null;
  label: string | null;
  sender_display: string | null;
  viewed_at: string | null;
  video:
    | Pick<
        Tables<'videos'>,
        'id' | 'status' | 'mux_playback_id' | 'duration_seconds' | 'purpose'
      >
    | Pick<
        Tables<'videos'>,
        'id' | 'status' | 'mux_playback_id' | 'duration_seconds' | 'purpose'
      >[]
    | null;
};

function mapThreadRow(r: ThreadJoinRow): ThreadMessage {
  const v = Array.isArray(r.video) ? r.video[0] ?? null : r.video;
  return {
    id: r.id,
    createdAt: r.created_at,
    senderUserId: r.sender_user_id,
    recipientFamilyId: r.recipient_family_id,
    recipientKidId: r.recipient_kid_id,
    recipientCoachUserId: r.recipient_coach_user_id,
    messageText: r.message_text,
    label: r.label,
    senderDisplay: r.sender_display,
    viewedAt: r.viewed_at,
    video: v
      ? {
          id: v.id,
          status: v.status,
          muxPlaybackId: v.mux_playback_id,
          durationSeconds: v.duration_seconds,
          purpose: v.purpose,
        }
      : null,
  };
}

/**
 * Bidirectional thread for a (kid, coach) pair. Returns every message
 * for this kid that is either:
 *   - sent BY the coach (coach -> parent), OR
 *   - sent BY the parent AND addressed TO this coach via
 *     `recipient_coach_user_id`.
 *
 * Both arms are unioned with PostgREST's `or` syntax. Sorted ascending so
 * the FlatList renders bottom-up like a chat.
 */
export async function listMessageThread(opts: {
  kidId: string;
  coachUserId: string;
  selfUserId: string;
}): Promise<ThreadMessage[]> {
  const { kidId, coachUserId, selfUserId } = opts;
  const { data, error } = await supabaseExt
    .from('coach_messages')
    .select(
      'id, created_at, sender_user_id, recipient_family_id, recipient_kid_id, recipient_coach_user_id, message_text, label, sender_display, viewed_at, video:videos(id, status, mux_playback_id, duration_seconds, purpose)',
    )
    .eq('recipient_kid_id', kidId)
    .or(
      `sender_user_id.eq.${coachUserId},and(sender_user_id.eq.${selfUserId},recipient_coach_user_id.eq.${coachUserId})`,
    )
    .order('created_at', { ascending: true });
  if (error) throw error;
  return ((data ?? []) as unknown as ThreadJoinRow[]).map(mapThreadRow);
}

/**
 * Inbox row for the parent — one row per coach who has been part of any
 * thread for this kid (either direction). Folded client-side from the
 * full message list (typical inbox is < 10 coaches).
 */
export type InboxRow = {
  coachUserId: string;
  coachFirstName: string | null;
  coachLastName: string | null;
  coachAvatarUrl: string | null;
  lastCreatedAt: string;
  lastMessageText: string | null;
  lastHasVideo: boolean;
  lastSenderIsSelf: boolean;
  unread: boolean;
};

export async function listParentInbox(opts: {
  kidId: string;
  selfUserId: string;
}): Promise<InboxRow[]> {
  const { kidId, selfUserId } = opts;

  const { data: msgs, error } = await supabaseExt
    .from('coach_messages')
    .select(
      'id, created_at, sender_user_id, recipient_coach_user_id, message_text, viewed_at, video_id',
    )
    .eq('recipient_kid_id', kidId)
    .order('created_at', { ascending: false });
  if (error) throw error;

  // No messages yet — surface every coach in the tenant so the parent can
  // start a thread from a cold inbox.
  const coachRows: TenantCoach[] = await listTenantCoachesForParent();
  const coachById = new Map(coachRows.map((c) => [c.userId, c]));

  // Build per-coach last-message folder. The conversation-partner coach is
  // deterministic now: for inbound rows it's `sender_user_id`; for
  // parent-sent rows it's `recipient_coach_user_id` (set by the composer).
  // Walk newest-first so the first time we encounter a coach is the
  // last-message timestamp.
  type RawMsg = {
    id: string;
    created_at: string;
    sender_user_id: string;
    recipient_coach_user_id: string | null;
    message_text: string | null;
    viewed_at: string | null;
    video_id: string | null;
  };
  const folder = new Map<string, InboxRow>();
  for (const m of (msgs ?? []) as RawMsg[]) {
    const isSelf = m.sender_user_id === selfUserId;
    const coachId = isSelf ? m.recipient_coach_user_id : m.sender_user_id;
    if (!coachId) continue;
    if (folder.has(coachId)) continue;
    const c = coachById.get(coachId);
    folder.set(coachId, {
      coachUserId: coachId,
      coachFirstName: c?.firstName ?? null,
      coachLastName: c?.lastName ?? null,
      coachAvatarUrl: c?.avatarUrl ?? null,
      lastCreatedAt: m.created_at,
      lastMessageText: m.message_text,
      lastHasVideo: !!m.video_id,
      lastSenderIsSelf: isSelf,
      unread: !isSelf && !m.viewed_at,
    });
  }

  // Fill in any tenant coach with no messages so the cold inbox isn't blank.
  for (const c of coachRows) {
    if (!folder.has(c.userId)) {
      folder.set(c.userId, {
        coachUserId: c.userId,
        coachFirstName: c.firstName,
        coachLastName: c.lastName,
        coachAvatarUrl: c.avatarUrl,
        lastCreatedAt: '',
        lastMessageText: null,
        lastHasVideo: false,
        lastSenderIsSelf: false,
        unread: false,
      });
    }
  }

  return Array.from(folder.values()).sort((a, b) =>
    b.lastCreatedAt.localeCompare(a.lastCreatedAt),
  );
}

/**
 * Sessions API helpers (task #119).
 *
 * One row in `public.sessions` = one cage session (a contiguous batch of
 * swings). `swing_count`, `best_exit_velocity_mph`, etc. are pre-aggregated
 * by the polling worker so the Videos → Swings (BY SESSION) grouping
 * renders without re-aggregating swings client-side.
 */

import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';
import type { Database } from '@/types/database';

export type Session = Database['public']['Tables']['sessions']['Row'];

const SESSION_COLUMNS =
  'id, tenant_id, kid_id, capture_source, capture_session_id, facility_id, started_at, ended_at, swing_count, best_exit_velocity_mph, avg_exit_velocity_mph, max_distance_ft, notes, created_at, updated_at';

/**
 * List every session for a kid, newest first. Default cap of 200 covers
 * roughly 8 months of weekly cage time — well past the spec's smoke-test
 * target. The FlatList in Videos still virtualizes, so a higher cap is
 * cheap if a tenant ever needs it.

export async function listSessionsForKid(
  kidId: string,

): Promise<Session[]> {

    .from('sessions')

/**
 * Stripe card payment API helpers.
 *
 * Calls the `stripe-create-payment-intent` Edge Function to obtain
 * a client secret, Stripe Customer context, and ephemeral key for
 * the Stripe payment sheet, then surfaces the response to
 * StoreCheckoutScreen for presentation.
 *
 * Also calls `stripe-setup-intent` to save a payment method for
 * recurring membership subscription billing (Phase 3).
 *
 * `savePaymentMethod` / `getCardOnFile` added in Task #233 for
 * in-app payment method management.
 */

import { supabase } from '@/lib/supabase';

export type CardPaymentIntentResult = {
  clientSecret: string;
  customerId: string;
  ephemeralKeySecret: string;
  orderId: string;
  redemptionCode: string;
  amountCents: number;
};

/**
 * Creates a Stripe PaymentIntent for a store item purchase and returns
 * the data needed to present the Stripe payment sheet.
 */
export async function createCardPaymentIntent(input: {
  productId: string;
  kidId: string;
}): Promise<CardPaymentIntentResult> {
  const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
  if (!session) throw new Error('Not authenticated');

  const supabaseUrl = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
  if (!supabaseUrl) throw new Error('Supabase URL not configured');

  const res = await fetch(
    `${supabaseUrl}/functions/v1/stripe-create-payment-intent`,
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${session.access_token}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      },
      body: JSON.stringify({
        product_id: input.productId,
        kid_id: input.kidId,
      }),
    },
  );

  const json = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok) {
    const msg = json?.error?.message ?? `Request failed (${res.status})`;
    const err = new Error(msg) as Error & { code?: string };
    err.code = json?.error?.code ?? 'unknown';
    throw err;
  }

  return {
    clientSecret: json.client_secret,
    customerId: json.customer_id,
    ephemeralKeySecret: json.ephemeral_key_secret,
    orderId: json.order_id,
    redemptionCode: json.redemption_code,
    amountCents: json.amount_cents,
  };
}

export type SetupIntentResult = {
  setupIntentClientSecret: string;
  customerId: string;
  ephemeralKeySecret: string;
  stripeAccountId: string;
};

/**
 * Creates a Stripe SetupIntent for saving a payment method for recurring
 * membership billing. The returned secrets are passed to initPaymentSheet
 * in SetupIntent mode to save the card without charging it.
 */
export async function createSetupIntent(): Promise<SetupIntentResult> {
  const { data: { session } } = await supabase.auth.getSession();
  if (!session) throw new Error('Not authenticated');

  const supabaseUrl = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
  if (!supabaseUrl) throw new Error('Supabase URL not configured');

  const res = await fetch(
    `${supabaseUrl}/functions/v1/stripe-setup-intent`,
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${session.access_token}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      },
      body: '{}',
    },
  );

  const json = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok) {
    const msg = json?.error?.message ?? `Request failed (${res.status})`;
    const err = new Error(msg) as Error & { code?: string };
    err.code = json?.error?.code ?? 'unknown';
    throw err;
  }

  return {
    setupIntentClientSecret: json.setup_intent_client_secret,
    customerId: json.customer_id,
    ephemeralKeySecret: json.ephemeral_key_secret,
    stripeAccountId: json.stripe_account_id,
  };
}

// ── Card-on-file (Task #233) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────

export type CardOnFile = {
  brand: string;
  last4: string;
  expMonth: number;
  expYear: number;
};

/**
 * Reads the card shadow columns from the calling parent's `families` row.
 * Returns null when no card has been saved yet.
 */
export async function getCardOnFile(): Promise<CardOnFile | null> {
  const { data, error } = await supabase
    .from('families')
    .select('card_brand, card_last4, card_exp_month, card_exp_year')
    .single();

  if (error || !data) return null;

  const { card_brand, card_last4, card_exp_month, card_exp_year } = data as unknown as {
    card_brand: string | null;
    card_last4: string | null;
    card_exp_month: number | null;
    card_exp_year: number | null;
  };

  if (!card_last4) return null;

  return {
    brand: card_brand ?? '',
    last4: card_last4,
    expMonth: card_exp_month ?? 0,
    expYear: card_exp_year ?? 0,
  };
}

/**
 * Calls the `save-payment-method` Edge Function after a successful
 * Stripe PaymentSheet confirmation. The function retrieves the newly
 * attached card from Stripe, sets it as default, and writes the four
 * shadow display columns back to `families`.
 *
 * Returns the saved card details for immediate UI update.
 */
export async function savePaymentMethod(): Promise<CardOnFile> {

  if (!session) throw new Error('Not authenticated');

  const supabaseUrl = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
  if (!supabaseUrl) throw new Error('Supabase URL not configured');

  const res = await fetch(
    `${supabaseUrl}/functions/v1/save-payment-method`,
    {
      method: 'POST',
      headers: {
        'Authorization': `Bearer ${session.access_token}`,
        'Content-Type': 'application/json',
      },
      body: '{}',
    },
  );

  const json = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok) {
    const msg = json?.error?.message ?? `Request failed (${res.status})`;
    const err = new Error(msg) as Error & { code?: string };
    err.code = json?.error?.code ?? 'unknown';
    throw err;
  }

  return {
    brand: json.card_brand ?? '',
    last4: json.card_last4 ?? '',
    expMonth: json.card_exp_month ?? 0,
    expYear: json.card_exp_year ?? 0,
  };
}
