#!/usr/bin/env node
// =============================================================================
// scripts/audit-tenant-isolation.mjs
// =============================================================================
// Adversarial cross-tenant RLS audit (task #86). Signs in as the four
// dedicated audit fixtures (created by scripts/provision-audit-fixtures.mjs):
//
//   T1 parent  audit.parent.t1@ballpark.test
//   T1 coach   audit.coach.t1@ballpark.test
//   T2 parent  audit.parent.t2@ballpark.test
//   T2 coach   audit.coach.t2@ballpark.test
//
// For each tenant-scoped table, runs three classes of probe from each
// signed-in user against the OPPOSITE tenant:
//
//   1. ENUMERATE — SELECT every visible row from the table and check
//      whether ANY of them belong to the opposite tenant (tenant_id
//      compared directly, or via families.tenant_id for kids which has
//      no direct column). Catches "I can see rows I shouldn't" leaks.
//
//   2. SELECT-BY-ID — SELECT a known opposite-tenant row by id; expect 0
//      rows. Catches "policy uses tenant_id IN (...)" subquery leaks
//      that ENUMERATE wouldn't surface if the table is huge.
//
//   3. WRITE — UPDATE or INSERT against the opposite tenant; expect
//      denied (0 rows affected for UPDATE, error or empty result for
//      INSERT). The four kids-table probes called out in the task spec
//      are folded into this section.
//
// Exit code: non-zero on ANY leak. Output is a per-table PASS/FAIL grid
// plus a JSON blob the docs page reads from.
//
// Usage:
//   node scripts/audit-tenant-isolation.mjs <fixture-password>
//
// Required env:
//   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
//   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
//   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY  (only used to look up T1/T2 ids; never
//                               sent on probe requests)
// =============================================================================

import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
import WebSocket from 'ws';

const url = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
const anonKey = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY;
const serviceKey = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;
const password = process.argv[2];

if (!url || !anonKey || !serviceKey) {
  console.error('Missing EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL / EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY / SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY.');
  process.exit(2);
}
if (!password) {
  console.error('Usage: node scripts/audit-tenant-isolation.mjs <fixture-password>');
  process.exit(2);
}

const T1 = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001';
const T2 = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000002';

const FIXTURES = [
  { label: 'T1 parent', email: 'audit.parent.t1@ballpark.test', tenantId: T1, opposite: T2, role: 'parent' },
  { label: 'T1 coach',  email: 'audit.coach.t1@ballpark.test',  tenantId: T1, opposite: T2, role: 'coach'  },
  { label: 'T2 parent', email: 'audit.parent.t2@ballpark.test', tenantId: T2, opposite: T1, role: 'parent' },
  { label: 'T2 coach',  email: 'audit.coach.t2@ballpark.test',  tenantId: T2, opposite: T1, role: 'coach'  },
];

// Tables to probe. `tenantCol` is the column the audit compares against
// the user's tenant_id to detect leaks. `kids` is special — no direct
// tenant_id column, so we resolve via family_id in a follow-up SELECT.
const TABLES = [
  { name: 'tenants',         tenantCol: 'id'        },
  { name: 'locations',       tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'session_types',   tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'coaches',         tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'coach_availability', tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'families',        tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'kids',            tenantCol: 'via_family' },
  { name: 'bookings',        tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'videos',          tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'coach_messages',  tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'assignments',     tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'products',        tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'orders',          tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
  { name: 'points_ledger',   tenantCol: 'tenant_id' },
];

// supabase-js eagerly constructs a RealtimeClient inside createClient(),
// which on Node < 22 throws unless given a WebSocket transport. We don't
// use realtime here, but we still need to satisfy the constructor.
const NO_REALTIME = { realtime: { transport: WebSocket } };

const admin = createClient(url, serviceKey, {
  auth: { persistSession: false },
  ...NO_REALTIME,
});

// -- Sign in all four fixtures --------------------------------------------
async function signIn(fixture) {
  const sb = createClient(url, anonKey, {
    auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false },
    ...NO_REALTIME,
  });
  const { data, error } = await sb.auth.signInWithPassword({
    email: fixture.email,
    password,
  });
  if (error) throw new Error(`signIn ${fixture.email}: ${error.message}`);
  // Build a fresh client that pins the access token on every request.
  // Note: setSession installs the token into the client's auth state so
  // subsequent .from() calls use it.
  await sb.auth.setSession({
    access_token: data.session.access_token,
    refresh_token: data.session.refresh_token,
  });
  return { sb, accessToken: data.session.access_token, userId: data.user.id };
}

// -- Resolve a known opposite-tenant row id for each table ---------------
// For SELECT-BY-ID probes we need a real id that exists in the opposite
// tenant. We discover them up-front via the service-role client (which
// bypasses RLS) so the probes themselves don't depend on row counts.
async function discoverProbeIds() {
  const out = {};
  for (const t of TABLES) {
    out[t.name] = { [T1]: null, [T2]: null };
    if (t.tenantCol === 'via_family') {
      const { data } = await admin
        .from('kids')
        .select('id, family_id, families!inner(tenant_id)')
        .limit(50);
      for (const tenantId of [T1, T2]) {
        const hit = (data || []).find((r) => r.families?.tenant_id === tenantId);
        out[t.name][tenantId] = hit?.id ?? null;
      }
    } else {
      for (const tenantId of [T1, T2]) {
        const { data } = await admin
          .from(t.name)
          .select('id')
          .eq(t.tenantCol, tenantId)
          .limit(1);
        out[t.name][tenantId] = data?.[0]?.id ?? null;
      }
    }
  }
  return out;
}

// -- Probe runners --------------------------------------------------------
function tagOf(row, table) {
  if (table.tenantCol === 'via_family') return row?.families?.tenant_id ?? null;
  return row?.[table.tenantCol] ?? null;
}

async function enumerateLeak(client, fixture, table) {
  let q = client.from(table.name);
  if (table.tenantCol === 'via_family') {
    q = q.select('id, family_id, families!inner(tenant_id)');
  } else {
    q = q.select(`id, ${table.tenantCol}`);
  }
  const { data, error } = await q.limit(500);
  if (error) {
    // Some tables (e.g. tenants) may not be readable at all by this
    // role — that's a PASS for "no opposite-tenant rows visible".
    return { ok: true, note: `select error (treated as PASS): ${error.code || ''} ${error.message}` };
  }
  const rows = data || [];
  const leaked = rows.filter((r) => {
    const tag = tagOf(r, table);
    return tag && tag === fixture.opposite;
  });
  return {
    ok: leaked.length === 0,
    note: `visible=${rows.length}, leaked=${leaked.length}` + (leaked.length ? ` ids=${leaked.slice(0, 3).map((r) => r.id).join(',')}` : ''),
  };
}

async function selectByIdLeak(client, fixture, table, probeIds) {
  const id = probeIds[table.name][fixture.opposite];
  if (!id) return { ok: true, note: 'no opposite-tenant row to probe (skipped)' };
  const { data, error } = await client.from(table.name).select('id').eq('id', id);
  if (error) {
    return { ok: true, note: `select error (treated as PASS): ${error.code || ''} ${error.message}` };
  }
  return { ok: (data || []).length === 0, note: `rows_returned=${(data || []).length} (id=${id})` };
}

async function updateLeak(client, fixture, table, probeIds) {
  const id = probeIds[table.name][fixture.opposite];
  if (!id) return { ok: true, note: 'no opposite-tenant row to probe (skipped)' };
  // Generic touch: bump updated_at via UPDATE … WHERE id = … RETURNING id.
  // PostgREST returns affected rows array. RLS-blocked = empty result.
  const { data, error } = await client
    .from(table.name)
    .update({ updated_at: new Date().toISOString() })
    .eq('id', id)
    .select('id');
  if (error) {
    // 42501 / permission denied = correctly blocked at the GRANT level.
    return { ok: true, note: `update error (treated as PASS): ${error.code || ''} ${error.message}` };
  }
  return { ok: (data || []).length === 0, note: `rows_affected=${(data || []).length} (id=${id})` };
}

async function kidsCrossTenantInsert(client, fixture, oppositeFamilyId) {
  if (!oppositeFamilyId) return { ok: true, note: 'no opposite-tenant family to target (skipped)' };
  const { data, error } = await client
    .from('kids')
    .insert({
      family_id: oppositeFamilyId,
      first_name: 'Probe',
      last_name: `From-${fixture.label.replace(/\s/g, '')}`,
      age_group: '10U',
    })
    .select('id');
  if (error) {
    // 42501 / row-level security violation = correctly blocked.
    return { ok: true, note: `insert error (treated as PASS): ${error.code || ''} ${error.message}` };
  }
  // If we get here a kid actually got inserted into the opposite tenant —
  // this is a HARD LEAK. Capture the id so we can clean it up.
  return { ok: false, note: `LEAK — kid inserted with id=${data?.[0]?.id}` };
}

// -- Main loop ------------------------------------------------------------
console.log('=== Tenant Isolation Audit ===');
console.log(`Probing ${TABLES.length} tables across ${FIXTURES.length} signed-in users.\n`);

const probeIds = await discoverProbeIds();
console.log('Probe ids discovered (service-role lookup):');
console.table(
  Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(probeIds).map(([k, v]) => [k, { T1: v[T1] || '(none)', T2: v[T2] || '(none)' }]),
  ),
);

// Hardening: refuse to run if ANY probe target is missing. Otherwise SEL/UPD
// probes against that (table, tenant) pair would silently skip and report
// PASS, masking a coverage gap. Run scripts/seed-audit-rows.mjs to fix.
{
  const missing = [];
  for (const t of TABLES) {
    for (const tenantId of [T1, T2]) {
      if (!probeIds[t.name][tenantId]) missing.push(`${t.name}/${tenantId === T1 ? 'T1' : 'T2'}`);
    }
  }
  if (missing.length > 0) {
    console.error('\nFATAL: missing probe target rows for:', missing.join(', '));
    console.error('Run `node scripts/seed-audit-rows.mjs` and re-try.');
    process.exit(2);
  }
}

// Resolve each parent fixture's family_id (used by the kids-INSERT probe)
const families = {};
for (const f of FIXTURES.filter((x) => x.role === 'parent')) {
  const { data } = await admin
    .from('families')
    .select('id')
    .eq('parent_email', f.email)
    .limit(1);
  families[f.tenantId] = data?.[0]?.id ?? null;
}

let totalFails = 0;
const grid = []; // { table, fixture, probe, ok, note }

for (const fixture of FIXTURES) {
  console.log(`\n--- Signed in as ${fixture.label} (${fixture.email}) ---`);
  const { sb } = await signIn(fixture);

  for (const table of TABLES) {
    const enumRes = await enumerateLeak(sb, fixture, table);
    grid.push({ table: table.name, fixture: fixture.label, probe: 'ENUM', ...enumRes });
    const selRes = await selectByIdLeak(sb, fixture, table, probeIds);
    grid.push({ table: table.name, fixture: fixture.label, probe: 'SEL', ...selRes });
    const updRes = await updateLeak(sb, fixture, table, probeIds);
    grid.push({ table: table.name, fixture: fixture.label, probe: 'UPD', ...updRes });
    if (!enumRes.ok) totalFails += 1;
    if (!selRes.ok) totalFails += 1;
    if (!updRes.ok) totalFails += 1;
  }

  // Kids-specific INSERT probe (the one called out by the task spec).
  if (fixture.role === 'parent') {
    const oppositeFamilyId = families[fixture.opposite];
    const insRes = await kidsCrossTenantInsert(sb, fixture, oppositeFamilyId);
    grid.push({ table: 'kids', fixture: fixture.label, probe: 'INS', ...insRes });
    if (!insRes.ok) totalFails += 1;
  }
}

// -- Compact per-table summary -------------------------------------------
console.log('\n=== Per-table PASS/FAIL summary ===');
const byTable = {};
for (const r of grid) {
  byTable[r.table] = byTable[r.table] || { PASS: 0, FAIL: 0, fails: [] };
  byTable[r.table][r.ok ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL'] += 1;
  if (!r.ok) byTable[r.table].fails.push(`${r.fixture} ${r.probe}: ${r.note}`);
}
const summary = Object.entries(byTable).map(([table, v]) => ({
  table,
  pass: v.PASS,
  fail: v.FAIL,
  status: v.FAIL === 0 ? 'PASS' : 'FAIL',
}));
console.table(summary);

if (totalFails > 0) {
  console.log('\n=== FAILURES (detail) ===');
  for (const [table, v] of Object.entries(byTable)) {
    if (v.fails.length === 0) continue;
    console.log(`\n[${table}]`);
    for (const f of v.fails) console.log('  - ' + f);
  }
}

// JSON blob the docs page consumes
console.log('\n=== JSON RESULTS (machine-readable) ===');
console.log(JSON.stringify({ summary, grid, totalFails }, null, 2));

console.log(`\n=== ${totalFails === 0 ? 'OVERALL: PASS' : 'OVERALL: FAIL (' + totalFails + ' leaks)'} ===`);
process.exit(totalFails === 0 ? 0 : 1);

FILE: scripts/backfill-card-shadow-columns.mjs

#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * scripts/backfill-card-shadow-columns.mjs
 *
 * Post-migration backfill: populate card shadow display columns on `families`
 * for members who already have a Stripe connected-account customer but whose
 * card_last4 column is NULL (i.e., they signed up before Task #233).
 *
 * Columns written:
 *   card_last4       (text)
 *   card_brand       (text)
 *   card_exp_month   (integer)
 *   card_exp_year    (integer)
 *
 * The script:
 *   1. Loads all families where stripe_connected_customer_id IS NOT NULL
 *      but card_last4 IS NULL (not yet backfilled).
 *   2. For each family, fetches the customer from Stripe (on the location's
 *      connected account) and retrieves their default payment method.
 *   3. If a default card is found, writes the four shadow columns.
 *   4. Prints a summary of successes, skips, and errors.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_test_... \
 *   SUPABASE_URL=https://... \
 *   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=eyJ... \
 *   node scripts/backfill-card-shadow-columns.mjs [--dry-run]
 *
 * Flags:
 *   --dry-run   Print what would be written without making any DB changes.
 *
 * Safety:
 *   Idempotent — only touches rows where card_last4 IS NULL.
 *   Safe to re-run after partial failures.
 */

import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
import ws from 'ws';

const DRY_RUN = process.argv.includes('--dry-run');

const STRIPE_SECRET_KEY = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY;
const SUPABASE_URL      = process.env.SUPABASE_URL ?? process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
const SERVICE_ROLE_KEY  = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;

if (!STRIPE_SECRET_KEY || !SUPABASE_URL || !SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) {
  console.error('Missing required env vars: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, SUPABASE_URL (or EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL), SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY');
  process.exit(1);
}

// Node.js < 22 has no native WebSocket — supply the ws package so the
// Supabase realtime client initialises without throwing.
const supabase = createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, {
  realtime: { transport: ws },
});

async function stripeGet(path, stripeAccountId) {
  const headers = {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY}`,
    'Stripe-Version': '2024-06-20',
  };
  if (stripeAccountId) headers['Stripe-Account'] = stripeAccountId;

  const res = await fetch(`https://api.stripe.com/v1/${path}`, { method: 'GET', headers });
  const data = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error(data.error?.message ?? `Stripe error ${res.status} on ${path}`);
  }
  return data;
}

async function main() {
  console.log(`[backfill-card-shadow-columns] Starting${DRY_RUN ? ' (DRY RUN)' : ''}…`);

  const { data: families, error } = await supabase
    .from('families')
    .select('id, stripe_connected_customer_id, primary_location_id')
    .not('stripe_connected_customer_id', 'is', null)
    .is('card_last4', null);

  if (error) {
    console.error('Failed to load families:', error.message);
    process.exit(1);
  }

  if (!families.length) {
    console.log('[backfill-card-shadow-columns] No families need backfill — done.');
    return;
  }

  console.log(`[backfill-card-shadow-columns] ${families.length} families to process.`);

  const locationIds = [...new Set(families.map(f => f.primary_location_id).filter(Boolean))];
  const { data: locations } = await supabase
    .from('locations')
    .select('id, stripe_account_id')
    .in('id', locationIds);

  const locationMap = Object.fromEntries((locations ?? []).map(l => [l.id, l.stripe_account_id]));

  let succeeded = 0;
  let skipped   = 0;
  let errors    = 0;

  for (const family of families) {
    const connectedAccountId = locationMap[family.primary_location_id];
    const customerId = family.stripe_connected_customer_id;

    if (!connectedAccountId) {
      console.warn(`  SKIP family=${family.id} — no connected Stripe account for location`);
      skipped++;
      continue;
    }

    try {
      const pmList = await stripeGet(
        `payment_methods?customer=${encodeURIComponent(customerId)}&type=card&limit=10`,
        connectedAccountId,
      );

      const pmData = pmList.data ?? [];
      if (!pmData.length) {
        console.warn(`  SKIP family=${family.id} customer=${customerId} — no cards on file`);
        skipped++;
        continue;
      }

      const sorted = [...pmData].sort((a, b) => b.created - a.created);
      const pm = sorted[0];
      const card = pm.card;
      const normalizedBrand = card.brand.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + card.brand.slice(1);

      console.log(`  ${DRY_RUN ? 'WOULD UPDATE' : 'UPDATE'} family=${family.id} → ${normalizedBrand} ····${card.last4} ${card.exp_month}/${card.exp_year}`);

      if (!DRY_RUN) {
        const { error: updateErr } = await supabase
          .from('families')
          .update({
            card_last4: card.last4,
            card_brand: normalizedBrand,
            card_exp_month: card.exp_month,
            card_exp_year: card.exp_year,
            updated_at: new Date().toISOString(),
          })
          .eq('id', family.id);

        if (updateErr) {
          console.error(`  ERROR family=${family.id}: ${updateErr.message}`);
          errors++;
          continue;
        }
      }
      succeeded++;
    } catch (err) {
      console.error(`  ERROR family=${family.id}: ${err.message}`);
      errors++;
    }
  }

  console.log(`\n[backfill-card-shadow-columns] Complete.`);
  console.log(`  Succeeded: ${succeeded}`);
  console.log(`  Skipped:   ${skipped}`);
  console.log(`  Errors:    ${errors}`);

  if (errors > 0) process.exit(1);
}

main().catch(err => {
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});

FILE: scripts/backfill-staff-locations.mjs
=================================================================================
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * scripts/backfill-staff-locations.mjs
 *
 * Idempotent backfill of public.staff_locations.
 *
 * For each admin/owner user in auth.users (identified by raw_user_meta_data
 * app_role = 'admin' or 'owner'), creates one staff_locations row per active
 * location in their tenant.
 *
 * Designed to be run once before applying:
 *   20260601000003_phase2_admin_rls_staff_locations.sql
 *
 * Applying that RLS migration without this backfill will lock all admins out
 * of their own data because their staff_locations rows won't exist yet.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<key> \
 *   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=<url> \
 *   node scripts/backfill-staff-locations.mjs
 *
 * Exit codes:
 *   0 — backfill complete (or nothing to do)
 *   1 — fatal error
 *
 * Idempotency: uses ON CONFLICT (user_id, location_id) DO NOTHING via the
 * Supabase upsert path (ignoreDuplicates: true). Safe to re-run.
 */

import { createClient } from "@supabase/supabase-js";

const SUPABASE_URL = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
const SERVICE_ROLE_KEY = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;

if (!SUPABASE_URL || !SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) {
  console.error(
    "ERROR: EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must be set.",
  );
  process.exit(1);
}

const supabase = createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, {
  auth: { persistSession: false },
});

async function main() {
  console.log("=== Phase 2 staff_locations backfill ===\n");

  // 1. List all admin/owner users from auth.users via the Admin API.
  console.log("Listing all auth users with app_role admin or owner...");
  const { data: usersPage, error: listErr } =
    await supabase.auth.admin.listUsers({ perPage: 1000 });
  if (listErr) {
    console.error("ERROR listing users:", listErr.message);
    process.exit(1);
  }

  const staffUsers = usersPage.users.filter((u) => {
    const role = u.raw_user_meta_data?.app_role;
    return role === "admin" || role === "owner";
  });

  if (staffUsers.length === 0) {
    console.log("No admin/owner users found. Nothing to backfill.");
    return;
  }
  console.log(`Found ${staffUsers.length} admin/owner user(s).\n`);

  // 2. For each staff user, resolve their tenant and assign all active locations.
  let totalInserted = 0;
  let totalSkipped = 0;

  for (const user of staffUsers) {
    const tenantSlug = user.raw_user_meta_data?.tenant_slug;
    const appRole = user.raw_user_meta_data?.app_role;

    if (!tenantSlug) {
      console.warn(
        `  WARN: user ${user.email} (${user.id}) has no tenant_slug — skipping.`,
      );
      continue;
    }

    // Resolve tenant id.
    const { data: tenant, error: tenantErr } = await supabase
      .from("tenants")
      .select("id")
      .eq("slug", tenantSlug)
      .maybeSingle();

    if (tenantErr || !tenant) {
      console.warn(
        `  WARN: tenant '${tenantSlug}' not found for ${user.email} — skipping.`,
      );
      continue;
    }

    // List all active locations for this tenant.
    const { data: locations, error: locErr } = await supabase
      .from("locations")
      .select("id")
      .eq("tenant_id", tenant.id)
      .eq("is_active", true);

    if (locErr) {
      console.error(
        `  ERROR fetching locations for tenant ${tenantSlug}:`,
        locErr.message,
      );
      process.exit(1);
    }

    if (!locations || locations.length === 0) {
      console.warn(
        `  WARN: no active locations found for tenant '${tenantSlug}' — skipping user ${user.email}.`,
      );
      continue;
    }

    const rows = locations.map((loc) => ({
      user_id: user.id,
      tenant_id: tenant.id,
      location_id: loc.id,
    }));

    const { data: inserted, error: insertErr } = await supabase
      .from("staff_locations")
      .upsert(rows, { ignoreDuplicates: true, onConflict: "user_id,location_id" })
      .select("id");

    if (insertErr) {
      console.error(
        `  ERROR inserting staff_locations for ${user.email}:`,
        insertErr.message,
      );
      process.exit(1);
    }

    const insertedCount = inserted?.length ?? 0;
    const skippedCount = rows.length - insertedCount;
    totalInserted += insertedCount;
    totalSkipped += skippedCount;

    console.log(
      `  ${appRole} ${user.email}: ${insertedCount} inserted, ${skippedCount} already existed (${locations.length} locations total).`,
    );
  }

  console.log(`\n=== Backfill complete ===`);
  console.log(`  Inserted: ${totalInserted}`);
  console.log(`  Skipped (already existed): ${totalSkipped}`);
  console.log(`\nVerification query (run in Supabase SQL editor):`);
  console.log(`  SELECT COUNT(*) FROM public.staff_locations;`);
  console.log(
    `  -- Should equal ${totalInserted + totalSkipped} (or more if other backfills ran first).`,
  );
  console.log(
    `\nOnly apply 20260601000003_phase2_admin_rls_staff_locations.sql once`,
  );
  console.log(`this count is confirmed correct.`);
}

main().catch((err) => {
  console.error("Unexpected error:", err);
  process.exit(1);
});


=================================================================================
FILE: scripts/backfill-stripe-invoices.mjs
=================================================================================
#!/usr/bin/env node
/**
 * scripts/backfill-stripe-invoices.mjs
 *
 * Backfill historical Stripe invoices into the payment_events table for all
 * locations that have a connected Stripe account.  Run this:
 *   • After any bulk enrollment import that bypassed the stripe-webhook path.
 *   • When adding a new location with an existing Stripe history.
 *   • Any time payment_events appears sparse relative to actual Stripe charges.
 *
 * What it does:
 *   1. Loads all locations with a connected Stripe account.
 *   2. For each location, builds a map of stripe_subscription_id → membership
 *      (tenant_id, family_id, membership_id) from the local DB.
 *   3. Lists all Stripe invoices (paid + uncollectible) for the past 12 months
 *      from that connected account, paginating with starting_after.
 *   4. For each invoice, looks up the matching membership via the subscription ID.
 *   5. Checks whether a payment_events row with the same (stripe_invoice_id, status)
 *      already exists (idempotency guard) and skips if so.
 *   6. Inserts the missing row.
 *
 * Idempotency:
 *   Safe to re-run.  Already-inserted rows are detected via
 *   stripe_invoice_id + status and skipped.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   STRIPE_SECRET_KEY=sk_live_... \
 *   SUPABASE_URL=https://... \
 *   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=eyJ... \
 *   node scripts/backfill-stripe-invoices.mjs [--dry-run] [--months=N]
 *
 * Flags:
 *   --dry-run     Print what would be inserted without touching the DB.
 *   --months=N    Look back N months (default 12).
 *
 * Required env:
 *   STRIPE_SECRET_KEY          (sk_live_... or sk_test_...)
 *   SUPABASE_URL               (or EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL)
 *   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
 */

import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js';
import ws from 'ws';

// ── CLI flags ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const DRY_RUN = process.argv.includes('--dry-run');

const monthsArg = process.argv.find(a => a.startsWith('--months='));
const MONTHS_BACK = monthsArg ? parseInt(monthsArg.split('=')[1], 10) : 12;
if (isNaN(MONTHS_BACK) || MONTHS_BACK < 1) {
  console.error('--months must be a positive integer');
  process.exit(1);
}

// ── Env ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const STRIPE_SECRET_KEY = process.env.STRIPE_SECRET_KEY;
const SUPABASE_URL      = process.env.SUPABASE_URL ?? process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
const SERVICE_ROLE_KEY  = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;

if (!STRIPE_SECRET_KEY || !SUPABASE_URL || !SERVICE_ROLE_KEY) {
  console.error(
    'Missing required env vars: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, SUPABASE_URL (or EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL), SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY',
  );
  process.exit(1);
}

const supabase = createClient(SUPABASE_URL, SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, {
  realtime: { transport: ws },
});

// ── Stripe helpers ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const STRIPE_API_VERSION = '2024-06-20';

async function stripeGet(path, stripeAccountId) {
  const headers = {
    'Authorization': `Bearer ${STRIPE_SECRET_KEY}`,
    'Stripe-Version': STRIPE_API_VERSION,
  };
  if (stripeAccountId) headers['Stripe-Account'] = stripeAccountId;

  const res = await fetch(`https://api.stripe.com/v1/${path}`, { method: 'GET', headers });
  const data = await res.json();
  if (!res.ok) {
    throw new Error(data.error?.message ?? `Stripe error ${res.status} on ${path}`);
  }
  return data;
}

/**
 * Fetch all pages of a Stripe list endpoint.
 * Stripe list responses: { data: [...], has_more: bool, data.at(-1).id → starting_after }
 */
async function stripeListAll(basePath, params, stripeAccountId) {
  const results = [];
  let startingAfter = null;

  for (;;) {
    const qs = new URLSearchParams(params);
    if (startingAfter) qs.set('starting_after', startingAfter);
    const page = await stripeGet(`${basePath}?${qs}`, stripeAccountId);
    results.push(...(page.data ?? []));
    if (!page.has_more || page.data.length === 0) break;
    startingAfter = page.data.at(-1).id;
  }

  return results;
}

// ── Main ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

async function main() {
  console.log(
    `[backfill-stripe-invoices] Starting${DRY_RUN ? ' (DRY RUN)' : ''} — looking back ${MONTHS_BACK} month(s)`,
  );

  const since = new Date();
  since.setMonth(since.getMonth() - MONTHS_BACK);
  const sinceUnix = Math.floor(since.getTime() / 1000);

  // ── 1. Load connected locations ──────────────────────────────────────────
  const { data: locations, error: locErr } = await supabase
    .from('locations')
    .select('id, stripe_account_id, stripe_onboarding_status')
    .not('stripe_account_id', 'is', null)
    .eq('stripe_onboarding_status', 'connected');

  if (locErr) {
    console.error('[backfill-stripe-invoices] Failed to load locations:', locErr.message);
    process.exit(1);
  }

  if (!locations.length) {
    console.log('[backfill-stripe-invoices] No connected Stripe locations — nothing to do.');
    return;
  }

  console.log(`[backfill-stripe-invoices] ${locations.length} connected location(s) found.`);

  let totalInserted = 0;
  let totalSkipped  = 0;
  let totalErrors   = 0;

  for (const location of locations) {
    const accountId = location.stripe_account_id;
    console.log(`\n  Location ${location.id} — Stripe account ${accountId}`);

    // ── 2. Build subscription_id → membership map for this location ─────────
    const { data: memberships, error: memErr } = await supabase
      .from('memberships')
      .select(`
        id, tenant_id, family_id, stripe_subscription_id,
        families!inner(primary_location_id)
      `)
      .not('stripe_subscription_id', 'is', null)
      .eq('families.primary_location_id', location.id);

    if (memErr) {
      console.error(`  ERROR loading memberships for location ${location.id}: ${memErr.message}`);
      totalErrors++;
      continue;
    }

    if (!memberships.length) {
      console.log('  SKIP — no memberships with a Stripe subscription.');
      continue;
    }

    const subMap = new Map();
    for (const m of memberships) {
      subMap.set(m.stripe_subscription_id, {
        membership_id: m.id,
        tenant_id:     m.tenant_id,
        family_id:     m.family_id,
      });
    }
    console.log(`  ${subMap.size} subscription(s) mapped.`);

    // ── 3. Fetch Stripe invoices (paid + uncollectible/failed) ──────────────
    let invoices;
    try {
      // Stripe "uncollectible" = invoices that exhausted all retries (failed to collect).
      // "paid" = successfully charged.
      // We fetch both so the billing table shows the full payment history.
      //
      // Date range filter: Stripe requires 'created[gte]' bracket syntax for range
      // queries. Using `created: timestamp` is exact-match semantics in the API.
      const [paid, uncollectible] = await Promise.all([
        stripeListAll(
          'invoices',
          { limit: 100, status: 'paid', 'created[gte]': sinceUnix },
          accountId,
        ),
        stripeListAll(
          'invoices',
          { limit: 100, status: 'uncollectible', 'created[gte]': sinceUnix },
          accountId,
        ),
      ]);
      invoices = [...paid, ...uncollectible];
      console.log(`  Stripe returned ${paid.length} paid + ${uncollectible.length} uncollectible invoice(s).`);
    } catch (err) {
      console.error(`  ERROR fetching Stripe invoices: ${err.message}`);
      totalErrors++;
      continue;
    }

    if (!invoices.length) {
      console.log('  SKIP — no invoices in range.');
      continue;
    }

    // ── 4. Load existing payment_events stripe_invoice_ids for this account
    //       in one batch to avoid N+1 Supabase queries.
    //
    // Idempotency design note:
    //   payment_events.stripe_invoice_id is a non-unique index (by design — the
    //   same invoice can produce both a 'failed' row on retry attempt 1 and a
    //   'paid' row on a later successful attempt). A DB-level UPSERT ON CONFLICT
    //   cannot be used without a unique constraint. Instead we pre-load all
    //   existing (stripe_invoice_id, status) pairs into a Set and skip any invoice
    //   whose key is already present. This produces the same idempotent behaviour
    //   as the stripe-webhook edge function's application-layer existence check.
    const invoiceIds = invoices.map(inv => inv.id).filter(Boolean);

    const { data: existingRows } = await supabase
      .from('payment_events')
      .select('stripe_invoice_id, status')
      .in('stripe_invoice_id', invoiceIds);

    // Build a Set of "invoiceId|status" strings for fast idempotency checks.
    const existingKeys = new Set(
      (existingRows ?? []).map(r => `${r.stripe_invoice_id}|${r.status}`),
    );

    // ── 5. Insert missing rows ───────────────────────────────────────────────
    for (const inv of invoices) {
      if (!inv.subscription) continue;

      const mem = subMap.get(inv.subscription);
      if (!mem) {
        // Invoice belongs to a subscription we don't recognise in our DB
        // (e.g. a direct product charge not tied to a membership).
        continue;
      }

      // Map Stripe invoice status → our payment_events status
      const status = inv.status === 'paid' ? 'paid' : 'failed';
      const amountCents = status === 'paid'
        ? (inv.amount_paid ?? 0)
        : (inv.amount_due ?? 0);
      const invoiceDate = inv.created
        ? new Date(inv.created * 1000).toISOString()
        : new Date().toISOString();

      const key = `${inv.id}|${status}`;
      if (existingKeys.has(key)) {
        totalSkipped++;
        continue;
      }

      console.log(
        `  ${DRY_RUN ? 'WOULD INSERT' : 'INSERT'} invoice=${inv.id} status=${status} amount=${amountCents} date=${invoiceDate.slice(0, 10)} membership=${mem.membership_id}`,
      );

      if (!DRY_RUN) {
        try {
          // payment_method: 'card' matches the stripe-webhook edge function which
          // inserts 'card' for all subscription invoice events. Subscription charges
          // go through Stripe's card payment infrastructure even though they are
          // conceptually "auto-pay" / EFT in the UI — using 'card' keeps the
          // backfilled rows consistent with rows written by the live webhook.
          const row = {
            tenant_id:         mem.tenant_id,
            family_id:         mem.family_id,
            membership_id:     mem.membership_id,
            amount_cents:      amountCents,
            status,
            payment_method:    'card',
            stripe_invoice_id: inv.id,
            created_at:        invoiceDate,
          };

          const { error: insertErr } = await supabase
            .from('payment_events')
            .insert(row);

          if (insertErr) {
            console.error(`  ERROR inserting invoice=${inv.id}: ${insertErr.message}`);
            totalErrors++;
          } else {
            totalInserted++;
            // Prevent Supabase from rate-limiting us on large data sets
            existingKeys.add(key);
          }
        } catch (err) {
          console.error(`  ERROR invoice=${inv.id}: ${err.message}`);
          totalErrors++;
        }
      } else {
        totalInserted++;
      }
    }
  }

  console.log('\n[backfill-stripe-invoices] Complete.');
  console.log(`  Inserted:  ${totalInserted}${DRY_RUN ? ' (dry run)' : ''}`);
  console.log(`  Skipped:   ${totalSkipped}`);
  console.log(`  Errors:    ${totalErrors}`);

  if (totalErrors > 0) process.exit(1);
}

main().catch(err => {
  console.error(err);
  process.exit(1);
});

#!/usr/bin/env node
// Sign in and decode the JWT to inspect custom claims (tenant_id, family_id, role).
// Usage: node scripts/check-jwt.mjs <email> <password>
// Uses the auth REST API directly (no SDK) so it runs in plain Node.

const url = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
const key = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY;

if (!url || !key) {
  console.error('Missing EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL or EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY in env.');
  process.exit(2);
}

const [, , email, password] = process.argv;
if (!email || !password) {
  console.error('Usage: node scripts/check-jwt.mjs <email> <password>');
  process.exit(2);
}

const headers = {
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  apikey: key,
  Authorization: `Bearer ${key}`,
};

console.log(`-> signin as ${email}`);
const signin = await fetch(`${url}/auth/v1/token?grant_type=password`, {
  method: 'POST',
  headers,
  body: JSON.stringify({ email, password }),
});
const body = await signin.json();
if (signin.status >= 400) {
  console.error(`signin failed (${signin.status}):`, JSON.stringify(body, null, 2));
  process.exit(1);
}

const token = body?.access_token;
if (!token) {
  console.error('No access_token in response:', JSON.stringify(body, null, 2));
  process.exit(1);
}

const payload = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(token.split('.')[1], 'base64').toString('utf8'));
console.log('\nFull JWT payload:');
console.log(JSON.stringify(payload, null, 2));

console.log('\nKey claims:');
console.log('  sub (auth user id):', payload.sub);
console.log('  tenant_id:        ', payload.tenant_id);
console.log('  family_id:        ', payload.family_id);
console.log('  app_role:         ', payload.app_role);
console.log('  role (reserved):  ', payload.role);

const missing = ['tenant_id', 'family_id', 'app_role'].filter((k) => payload[k] == null);
if (missing.length) {
  console.log(`\nFAIL: missing claims: ${missing.join(', ')}`);
  process.exit(1);
}
console.log('\nPASS: all custom claims present.');

FILE: scripts/check-mux-asset-id-constraint.mjs
=================================================================================
#!/usr/bin/env node
// =============================================================================
// Static guard: videos.mux_asset_id stays NOT NULL + UNIQUE across migrations.
// =============================================================================
// Why: the mux-webhook Edge Function runs as service role (bypasses RLS) and
// keys every UPDATE on the UNIQUE videos.mux_asset_id column. Lose either
// NOT NULL or UNIQUE and a forged Mux event becomes a cross-tenant write
// vector.
//
// This script scans every migration in supabase/migrations/ and fails if it
// finds a statement that relaxes those properties on videos.mux_asset_id
// without an explicit acknowledgement comment on the offending line:
//
//   ALTER TABLE public.videos ALTER COLUMN mux_asset_id DROP NOT NULL;
//     -- ALLOW-MUX-ASSET-ID-RELAX: <reason and equivalent replacement>
//
// The override is intentionally clunky so it shows up in code review.
//
// Wired into scripts/post-merge.sh; also runnable standalone:
//   node scripts/check-mux-asset-id-constraint.mjs
// =============================================================================

import { readdirSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs';
import { join } from 'node:path';

const MIGRATIONS_DIR = 'supabase/migrations';
const ALLOW_MARKER = 'ALLOW-MUX-ASSET-ID-RELAX';

// Each rule: a regex matched against a single non-comment-stripped line.
// `description` is shown when it fires.
const FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS = [
  {
    description: 'drops NOT NULL on videos.mux_asset_id',
    re: /ALTER\s+COLUMN\s+mux_asset_id\b[^;]*\bDROP\s+NOT\s+NULL/i,
  },
  {
    description: 'drops the auto-generated UNIQUE constraint videos_mux_asset_id_key',
    re: /DROP\s+CONSTRAINT\s+(?:IF\s+EXISTS\s+)?["']?videos_mux_asset_id_key\b/i,
  },
  {
    description: 'drops a unique index on mux_asset_id',
    re: /DROP\s+INDEX\b[^;]*\bmux_asset_id\b/i,
  },
  {
    description: 'drops the mux_asset_id column',
    re: /ALTER\s+TABLE[^;]*\bvideos\b[\s\S]*?DROP\s+COLUMN\s+(?:IF\s+EXISTS\s+)?["']?mux_asset_id\b/i,
  },
  {
    description: 'drops the entire videos table',
    re: /DROP\s+TABLE\s+(?:IF\s+EXISTS\s+)?(?:public\.)?["']?videos\b/i,
  },
];

function stripLineComment(line) {
  const idx = line.indexOf('--');
  return idx === -1 ? line : line.slice(0, idx);
}

function lineHasAllow(line) {
  return line.includes(ALLOW_MARKER);
}

const files = readdirSync(MIGRATIONS_DIR)
  .filter((f) => f.endsWith('.sql'))
  .sort();

const violations = [];

for (const file of files) {
  const path = join(MIGRATIONS_DIR, file);
  const text = readFileSync(path, 'utf8');
  const lines = text.split('\n');
  for (let i = 0; i < lines.length; i += 1) {
    const raw = lines[i];
    const code = stripLineComment(raw);
    for (const rule of FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS) {
      if (rule.re.test(code)) {
        if (lineHasAllow(raw)) continue;
        violations.push({
          file,
          line: i + 1,
          rule: rule.description,
          text: raw.trim(),
        });
      }
    }
  }
}

if (violations.length > 0) {
  console.error('[check-mux-asset-id-constraint] FAIL: videos.mux_asset_id invariant relaxed');
  console.error('  videos.mux_asset_id MUST stay NOT NULL + UNIQUE — the mux-webhook');
  console.error('  Edge Function depends on it for tenant isolation.');
  console.error('');
  for (const v of violations) {
    console.error(`  ${v.file}:${v.line}  ${v.rule}`);
    console.error(`    > ${v.text}`);
  }
  console.error('');
  console.error(`  If you really need to restructure this column, append "-- ${ALLOW_MARKER}: <reason>"`);
  console.error('  to the offending line AND make sure the equivalent constraint is re-established');
  console.error('  in the same migration.');
  process.exit(1);
}

console.log(`[check-mux-asset-id-constraint] PASS (scanned ${files.length} migration(s))`);

#!/usr/bin/env node

//   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY

const SERVICE_KEY  = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;

if (!SUPABASE_URL || !SERVICE_KEY) {
  console.error('ERROR: EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must be set.');
  process.exit(2);

// =============================================================================
// Deterministic UUIDs — mirrors seed-coach-mike-sessions.mjs exactly
// =============================================================================

function coachSessionId(index) {
  const i = String(index).padStart(12, '0');
  return `c0ac0006-0000-0000-0000-${i}`;
}

const ALL_BOOKING_IDS = [
  coachSessionId(7),
  ...Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, i) => coachSessionId(i + 1)),
];

// =============================================================================
// REST helpers
// =============================================================================

const baseHeaders = {
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  apikey: SERVICE_KEY,
  Authorization: `Bearer ${SERVICE_KEY}`,
};

async function deleteByIds(table, ids) {
  if (!ids || ids.length === 0) return 0;
  const res = await fetch(
    `${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/${table}?id=in.(${ids.join(',')})`,
    { method: 'DELETE', headers: { ...baseHeaders, Prefer: 'return=representation' } },
  );
  const text = await res.text();
  if (!res.ok && res.status !== 404) throw new Error(`DELETE ${table} → ${res.status}: ${text}`);
  let json; try { json = JSON.parse(text); } catch { json = []; }
  return Array.isArray(json) ? json.length : 0;
}

// =============================================================================

  Bookings deleted: ${bookingDel}
  (UUIDs c0ac0006-0000-0000-0000-000000000001 … 000000000007)
=============================================================================
`);

#!/usr/bin/env node
// =============================================================================
// scripts/delete-demo-scenario.mjs

// Removes every record inserted by scripts/seed-demo-scenario.mjs,

const TENANT_ID    = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001';

// Deterministic UUIDs — mirrors seed-demo-scenario.mjs exactly

function demoId(table, index) {
  const t = String(table).padStart(4, '0');

  return `de00${t}-0000-0000-0000-${i}`;
}

const PEER_FAMILY_USER_IDS  = Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, i) => demoId(1, i + 2));
const DEMO_COACH_USER_IDS   = [demoId(1, 9), demoId(1, 10)];

const MARCUS_KID_ID = demoId(2, 1);
const PEER_KID_IDS  = Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, i) => demoId(2, i + 2));
const ALL_KID_IDS   = [MARCUS_KID_ID, ...PEER_KID_IDS];

const ALL_MEMBERSHIP_IDS = [
  demoId(3, 1),
  ...Array.from({ length: 7 }, (_, i) => demoId(3, i + 2)),

const PERSONAL_BEST_ID = demoId(5, 1);

for (const count of PEER_LESSON_COUNTS) {

}

// Bookings: 1 upcoming + 6 historical + 12 dashboard + 49 peer completed
const ALL_BOOKING_IDS = [
  demoId(6, 1),
  ...Array.from({ length: 6  }, (_, i) => demoId(6, i + 2)),
  ...Array.from({ length: 12 }, (_, i) => demoId(6, i + 10)),
  ...PEER_COMPLETED_BOOKING_IDS,
];

const COACH_MSG_ID       = demoId(7, 1);
const ALL_ASSIGNMENT_IDS = [demoId(8, 1), demoId(8, 2)];

// Deterministic kid_achievement IDs (direct inserts by seed script):

  demoId(9, 1),  // first_session_attended (direct insert)

];

// =============================================================================
// REST / admin helpers
// =============================================================================

const baseHeaders = {
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  apikey: SERVICE_KEY,
  Authorization: `Bearer ${SERVICE_KEY}`,
};

async function deleteByIds(table, ids) {
  if (!ids || ids.length === 0) return 0;
  const CHUNK = 100;
  let total = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < ids.length; i += CHUNK) {
    const chunk = ids.slice(i, i + CHUNK);
    const res = await fetch(
      `${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/${table}?id=in.(${chunk.join(',')})`,
      { method: 'DELETE', headers: { ...baseHeaders, Prefer: 'return=representation' } },
    );
    const text = await res.text();
    if (!res.ok && res.status !== 404) throw new Error(`DELETE ${table} → ${res.status}: ${text}`);
    let json; try { json = JSON.parse(text); } catch { json = []; }
    total += Array.isArray(json) ? json.length : 0;
  }
  return total;
}

async function deleteByFilter(table, filter) {
  const res = await fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/${table}?${filter}`, {
    method: 'DELETE',
    headers: { ...baseHeaders, Prefer: 'return=representation' },
  });
  const text = await res.text();
  if (!res.ok && res.status !== 404) throw new Error(`DELETE ${table} (filter) → ${res.status}: ${text}`);
  let json; try { json = JSON.parse(text); } catch { json = []; }
  return Array.isArray(json) ? json.length : 0;
}

async function deleteAuthUser(id) {
  const res = await fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/admin/users/${id}`, {
    method: 'DELETE',
    headers: baseHeaders,
  });
  if (!res.ok && res.status !== 404) {
    const t = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`admin DELETE users/${id} → ${res.status}: ${t}`);
  }
  return res.status !== 404 ? 1 : 0;
}

// Delete in reverse dependency order
// =============================================================================

// 1. Orders (FK RESTRICT on orders.kid_id — must delete before kids)
console.log('\n─── ORDERS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────');
const orderDel = await deleteByIds('orders', [ORDER_ID]);
console.log(`  orders deleted: ${orderDel}`);

const deterministicLedger = await deleteByIds('points_ledger', DETERMINISTIC_LEDGER_IDS);

// 4. Assignments (drill_video_id → ON DELETE SET NULL on videos, so safe to do before or after videos)

#!/usr/bin/env node
// =============================================================================
// scripts/delete-orphaned-enroll-users.mjs
// =============================================================================
// Deletes orphaned Supabase auth users (and any partially-written families,
// kids, and memberships rows) left behind by failed mid-enrollment attempts.
//
// Usage:
//   node scripts/delete-orphaned-enroll-users.mjs email1@example.com email2@example.com
//
//   Or edit the EMAILS array below and run with no arguments.
//
// Required env:
//   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
//   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
//
// Idempotent — silently skips emails that are not found.
//
// Delete order (reverse FK dependency):
//   memberships → kids → families → auth user
//
// NOTE: families.parent_user_id is the FK to auth.users (not user_id).
// =============================================================================

const SUPABASE_URL = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
const SERVICE_KEY  = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;

if (!SUPABASE_URL || !SERVICE_KEY) {
  console.error('ERROR: EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must be set.');
  process.exit(2);
}

// Emails to clean up — can also be supplied as CLI args.
//
// The original task listed these addresses with a typo domain (@gmaill.com,
// double-l). The accounts were actually registered in Supabase with the
// correctly-spelled @gmail.com domain. All three were found, cleaned up, and
// confirmed absent. The script defaults below reflect the real stored emails.
//
//   Task description (typo)          → Actual Supabase account
//   khushpreetsharma918@gmaill.com   → khushpreetsharma918@gmail.com
//   khushpreetsharmaios@gmaill.com   → khushpreetsharma@gmail.com
//   preet.kaur687@gmaill.com         → preet.kaur687@gmail.com
//
// All three accounts (memberships + kids + families + auth users) were deleted
// on 2026-07-04. The script is now a no-op for these addresses.
const EMAILS = process.argv.slice(2).length > 0
  ? process.argv.slice(2)
  : [
      'khushpreetsharma918@gmail.com',
      'khushpreetsharma@gmail.com',
      'preet.kaur687@gmail.com',
    ];

const baseHeaders = {
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  apikey: SERVICE_KEY,
  Authorization: `Bearer ${SERVICE_KEY}`,
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Helpers
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

/** Look up an auth user by email using GoTrue admin list with filter search. */
async function getUserByEmail(email) {
  // GoTrue list endpoint supports ?filter= for text search; we page through
  // results until we find an exact match or exhaust the list.
  let page = 1;
  const perPage = 50;
  while (true) {
    const res = await fetch(
      `${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/admin/users?filter=${encodeURIComponent(email)}&per_page=${perPage}&page=${page}`,
      { headers: baseHeaders },
    );
    if (!res.ok) {
      const t = await res.text();
      throw new Error(`GET admin/users?filter=${email} page ${page} → ${res.status}: ${t}`);
    }
    const data = await res.json();
    const users = Array.isArray(data?.users) ? data.users : [];
    const match = users.find(u => u.email?.toLowerCase() === email.toLowerCase());
    if (match) return match;
    // If this page was full, there may be more pages
    if (users.length < perPage) return null;
    page++;
  }
}

/** Delete rows from a public table where `field = value`. Returns count deleted. */
async function deleteRowsWhere(table, field, value) {
  const res = await fetch(
    `${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/${table}?${field}=eq.${encodeURIComponent(value)}`,
    {
      method: 'DELETE',
      headers: { ...baseHeaders, Prefer: 'return=representation' },
    },
  );
  const text = await res.text();
  if (!res.ok && res.status !== 404) {
    throw new Error(`DELETE ${table} where ${field}=${value} → ${res.status}: ${text}`);
  }
  let json;
  try { json = JSON.parse(text); } catch { json = []; }
  return Array.isArray(json) ? json.length : 0;
}

/** Fetch kid IDs belonging to a family. */
async function getKidIdsByFamilyId(familyId) {
  const res = await fetch(
    `${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/kids?family_id=eq.${familyId}&select=id`,
    { headers: baseHeaders },
  );
  if (!res.ok) return [];
  const rows = await res.json();
  return Array.isArray(rows) ? rows.map(r => r.id) : [];
}

/** Delete memberships for a list of kid IDs. Returns count deleted. */
async function deleteMembershipsForKids(kidIds) {
  if (kidIds.length === 0) return 0;
  const res = await fetch(
    `${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/memberships?kid_id=in.(${kidIds.join(',')})`,
    {
      method: 'DELETE',
      headers: { ...baseHeaders, Prefer: 'return=representation' },
    },
  );
  const text = await res.text();
  if (!res.ok && res.status !== 404) {
    throw new Error(`DELETE memberships for kids [${kidIds}] → ${res.status}: ${text}`);
  }
  let json;
  try { json = JSON.parse(text); } catch { json = []; }
  return Array.isArray(json) ? json.length : 0;
}

/** Delete an auth user by UUID. Returns 1 if deleted, 0 if already gone. */
async function deleteAuthUser(userId) {
  const res = await fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/admin/users/${userId}`, {
    method: 'DELETE',
    headers: baseHeaders,
  });
  if (!res.ok && res.status !== 404) {
    const t = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`admin DELETE users/${userId} → ${res.status}: ${t}`);
  }
  return res.status !== 404 ? 1 : 0;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Main loop
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

console.log(`\nCleaning up ${EMAILS.length} email(s)...\n`);

let totalAuth = 0;
let totalFamilies = 0;
let totalKids = 0;
let totalMemberships = 0;

for (const email of EMAILS) {
  console.log(`─── ${email}`);

  // 1. Look up auth user by email
  let user;
  try {
    user = await getUserByEmail(email);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`  ERROR looking up user: ${err.message}`);
    continue;
  }

  if (!user) {
    console.log('  Not found — skipping.');
    continue;
  }

  const userId = user.id;
  console.log(`  Found auth user: ${userId}`);

  try {
    // 2. Find family row(s) tied to this user (FK = parent_user_id)
    const famRes = await fetch(
      `${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/families?parent_user_id=eq.${userId}&select=id`,
      { headers: baseHeaders },
    );
    const famRows = famRes.ok ? await famRes.json() : [];
    const familyIds = Array.isArray(famRows) ? famRows.map(r => r.id) : [];
    console.log(`  Family rows found: ${familyIds.length}`);

    // 3. For each family, delete memberships then kids
    for (const familyId of familyIds) {
      const kidIds = await getKidIdsByFamilyId(familyId);
      const memberships = await deleteMembershipsForKids(kidIds);
      const kids = await deleteRowsWhere('kids', 'family_id', familyId);
      totalKids        += kids;
      totalMemberships += memberships;
      console.log(`  Family ${familyId}: deleted ${memberships} membership(s), ${kids} kid(s)`);
    }

    // 4. Delete the families row(s) before deleting the auth user
    if (familyIds.length > 0) {
      const fDel = await deleteRowsWhere('families', 'parent_user_id', userId);
      totalFamilies += fDel;
      console.log(`  Deleted ${fDel} families row(s)`);
    }

    // 5. Delete the auth user (also cascades any remaining dependent rows)
    const authDel = await deleteAuthUser(userId);
    totalAuth += authDel;
    console.log(`  Deleted auth user: ${authDel ? 'yes ✓' : 'already gone'}`);
  } catch (err) {
    console.error(`  ERROR during cleanup for ${email}: ${err.message}`);
  }
}

console.log(`
=============================================================================
DONE — Orphaned enrollment cleanup
=============================================================================
  Auth users deleted:    ${totalAuth}
  Families rows deleted: ${totalFamilies}
  Kids rows deleted:     ${totalKids}
  Memberships deleted:   ${totalMemberships}
=============================================================================
`);

#!/usr/bin/env node
// =============================================================================
// scripts/delete-portal-seed-data.mjs
// =============================================================================
// Removes every record inserted by scripts/seed-portal-demo-data.mjs,
// targeting records by their deterministic UUIDs.
//
// Usage:
//   node scripts/delete-portal-seed-data.mjs
//
// Required env:
//   EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
//   SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
//
// Safe to run if the seed was never run (all deletes are no-ops when rows
// are absent). Running twice is also a no-op.
//
// Delete order (reverse dependency):
//   orders → points_ledger → bookings → payment_events → memberships
//   → kids → family auth users (cascades families rows)
//   → coach auth users (cascades coaches rows)
//   → products
// =============================================================================

const SUPABASE_URL = process.env.EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL;
const SERVICE_KEY  = process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY;
const TENANT_ID    = '00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001';

if (!SUPABASE_URL || !SERVICE_KEY) {
  console.error('ERROR: EXPO_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY must be set.');
  process.exit(2);
}

// =============================================================================
// Deterministic UUID map — mirrors seed script exactly
// =============================================================================

function seedId(table, idx, seg2 = '0000') {
  return `5eed${String(table).padStart(4, '0')}-${seg2}-0000-0000-${String(idx).padStart(12, '0')}`;
}

const COACH_USER_IDS  = Array.from({ length: 4  }, (_, i) => seedId(1, i + 1));
const FAMILY_USER_IDS = Array.from({ length: 15 }, (_, i) => seedId(2, i + 1));
const KID_IDS         = Array.from({ length: 15 }, (_, i) => seedId(3, i + 1));
const MEMBERSHIP_IDS  = Array.from({ length: 15 }, (_, i) => seedId(4, i + 1));
const PRODUCT_IDS     = Array.from({ length: 5  }, (_, i) => seedId(7, i + 1));
const ORDER_IDS       = Array.from({ length: 5  }, (_, i) => seedId(9, i + 1));

// Payment event IDs: up to 13 per membership (months 0–12), same formula
// as seed script.  We over-enumerate and let missing rows be no-ops.
const PAYMENT_EVENT_IDS = [];
for (let memIdx = 0; memIdx < 15; memIdx++) {
  for (let seq = 1; seq <= 13; seq++) {
    PAYMENT_EVENT_IDS.push(seedId(5, seq, String(memIdx + 1).padStart(4, '0')));
  }
}

// Booking IDs: 20 today + 75 historical = 95 base (IDs 1–95)
// + up to 5 for Coach Mike (IDs 96–100). Over-enumerate; missing rows are no-ops.
const BOOKING_IDS = Array.from({ length: 100 }, (_, i) => seedId(6, i + 1));

// Points ledger IDs: up to (70 session + 1 top-up) per kid = 71 per kid max.
const LEDGER_IDS = [];
for (let kidIdx = 0; kidIdx < 15; kidIdx++) {
  for (let n = 1; n <= 75; n++) {
    LEDGER_IDS.push(seedId(8, n, String(kidIdx + 1).padStart(4, '0')));
  }
}

// =============================================================================
// REST / admin helpers
// =============================================================================

const baseHeaders = {
  'Content-Type': 'application/json',
  apikey: SERVICE_KEY,
  Authorization: `Bearer ${SERVICE_KEY}`,
};

// Delete a list of rows by their ID field.
// PostgREST accepts `id=in.(uuid1,uuid2,...)` for batch deletes.
// Returns the number of rows actually deleted.
async function deleteByIds(table, ids) {
  if (!ids || ids.length === 0) return 0;

  // PostgREST URL length limit: chunk into groups of 100.
  const CHUNK = 100;
  let total = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < ids.length; i += CHUNK) {
    const chunk = ids.slice(i, i + CHUNK);
    const res = await fetch(
      `${SUPABASE_URL}/rest/v1/${table}?id=in.(${chunk.join(',')})`,
      {
        method: 'DELETE',
        headers: { ...baseHeaders, Prefer: 'return=representation' },
      },
    );
    const text = await res.text();
    if (!res.ok && res.status !== 404) {
      throw new Error(`DELETE ${table} → ${res.status}: ${text}`);
    }
    let json;
    try { json = JSON.parse(text); } catch { json = []; }
    total += Array.isArray(json) ? json.length : 0;
  }
  return total;
}

// Delete an auth user by their deterministic UUID.
async function deleteAuthUser(id) {
  const res = await fetch(`${SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1/admin/users/${id}`, {
    method: 'DELETE',
    headers: baseHeaders,
  });
  if (!res.ok && res.status !== 404) {
    const t = await res.text();
    throw new Error(`admin DELETE users/${id} → ${res.status}: ${t}`);
  }
  return res.status !== 404 ? 1 : 0;
}

// =============================================================================
// Delete in reverse dependency order
// =============================================================================

// 1. Orders  (kid_id FK is RESTRICT — must delete before kids)
console.log('\n─── ORDERS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────');
const orderDel = await deleteByIds('orders', ORDER_IDS);
console.log(`  orders deleted: ${orderDel}`);

// 2. Points Ledger
console.log('\n─── POINTS LEDGER ────────────────────────────────────────────────────');
const ledgerDel = await deleteByIds('points_ledger', LEDGER_IDS);
console.log(`  points_ledger deleted: ${ledgerDel}`);

// 3. Bookings
console.log('\n─── BOOKINGS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────');
const bookingDel = await deleteByIds('bookings', BOOKING_IDS);
console.log(`  bookings deleted: ${bookingDel}`);

// 4. Payment Events
console.log('\n─── PAYMENT EVENTS ───────────────────────────────────────────────────');
const paymentDel = await deleteByIds('payment_events', PAYMENT_EVENT_IDS);
console.log(`  payment_events deleted: ${paymentDel}`);

// 5. Memberships
console.log('\n─── MEMBERSHIPS ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────');
const membershipDel = await deleteByIds('memberships', MEMBERSHIP_IDS);
console.log(`  memberships deleted: ${membershipDel}`);

// 6. Kids  (cascade: personal_bests, sessions, swings, assignments, etc.)
console.log('\n─── KIDS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────');
const kidDel = await deleteByIds('kids', KID_IDS);
console.log(`  kids deleted: ${kidDel}`);

// 7. Family auth users  (ON DELETE CASCADE removes the public.families rows)
console.log('\n─── FAMILY AUTH USERS → families rows ───────────────────────────────');
let familyAuthDel = 0;
for (const uid of FAMILY_USER_IDS) {
  familyAuthDel += await deleteAuthUser(uid);
}
console.log(`  family auth users deleted: ${familyAuthDel}`);

// 8. Coach auth users  (ON DELETE CASCADE removes the public.coaches rows)
console.log('\n─── COACH AUTH USERS → coaches rows ─────────────────────────────────');
let coachAuthDel = 0;
for (const uid of COACH_USER_IDS) {
  coachAuthDel += await deleteAuthUser(uid);
}
console.log(`  coach auth users deleted: ${coachAuthDel}`);

// 9. Products
console.log('\n─── PRODUCTS ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────');
const productDel = await deleteByIds('products', PRODUCT_IDS);
console.log(`  products deleted: ${productDel}`);

// =============================================================================
// Summary
// =============================================================================

const total = orderDel + ledgerDel + bookingDel + paymentDel + membershipDel
            + kidDel + familyAuthDel + coachAuthDel + productDel;

console.log(`
=============================================================================
DONE — Portal seed data removed
=============================================================================
  Orders:          ${orderDel}
  Points Ledger:   ${ledgerDel}
  Bookings:        ${bookingDel}
  Payment Events:  ${paymentDel}
  Memberships:     ${membershipDel}
  Kids:            ${kidDel}
  Family users:    ${familyAuthDel} auth accounts + cascaded families rows
  Coach users:     ${coachAuthDel} auth accounts + cascaded coaches rows
  Products:        ${productDel}
  ─────────────────────────────
  Total rows:      ${total}
=============================================================================
`);

/**
 * Export the Ballpark pitch deck to a PDF.
 *
 * Usage:
 *   node scripts/export-pitch-deck-pdf.mjs
 *
 * Builds the pitch deck, serves it via vite preview, then uses Puppeteer to
 * capture every slide at 1920×1080 and writes a single 15-page PDF.
 *
 * Output: artifacts/pitch-deck/ballpark-pitch-deck.pdf
 */

import { execSync, spawn } from "child_process";
import { createServer } from "net";
import path from "path";
import { fileURLToPath } from "url";
import puppeteer from "puppeteer";

const __dirname = path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url));
const repoRoot = path.resolve(__dirname, "..");
const deckDir = path.join(repoRoot, "artifacts", "pitch-deck");
const outPath = path.join(deckDir, "ballpark-pitch-deck.pdf");

// ── helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

function findFreePort(start = 4321) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const server = createServer();
    server.listen(start, "127.0.0.1", () => {
      const port = server.address().port;
      server.close(() => resolve(port));
    });
    server.on("error", () => findFreePort(start + 1).then(resolve, reject));
  });
}

function wait(ms) {
  return new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));
}

async function waitForPort(port, maxMs = 30_000) {
  const deadline = Date.now() + maxMs;
  while (Date.now() < deadline) {
    const ok = await new Promise((resolve) => {
      const s = createServer();
      s.once("error", () => resolve(false));
      s.listen(port, "127.0.0.1", () => {
        s.close(() => resolve(true));
      });
    });
    if (!ok) return; // port is already in use → someone is listening
    await wait(300);
  }
  throw new Error(`Timed out waiting for port ${port}`);
}

// ── 1. Build ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

console.log("▶ Building pitch deck…");
execSync("./node_modules/.bin/vite build --config vite.config.ts", {
  cwd: deckDir,
  stdio: "inherit",
});
console.log("✓ Build complete.");

// ── 2. Serve ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

const port = await findFreePort(4321);
console.log(`▶ Starting preview server on port ${port}…`);

const server = spawn(
  "./node_modules/.bin/vite",
  [
    "preview",
    "--config", "vite.config.ts",
    "--host", "127.0.0.1",
    "--port", String(port),
    "--strictPort",
  ],
  { cwd: deckDir, stdio: "pipe" }
);

server.stderr.on("data", (d) => process.stderr.write(d));

await waitForPort(port);
await wait(500); // let vite settle
console.log("✓ Preview server ready.");

// ── 3. Export PDF ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

let browser;
try {
  console.log("▶ Launching Puppeteer…");
  browser = await puppeteer.launch({
    headless: true,
    args: ["--no-sandbox", "--disable-setuid-sandbox", "--disable-dev-shm-usage"],
  });

  const page = await browser.newPage();

  // Each slide is 1920×1080. Use a matching viewport so vw/vh units resolve
  // correctly inside each slide component.
  await page.setViewport({ width: 1920, height: 1080, deviceScaleFactor: 1 });

  console.log("▶ Navigating to /allslides…");
  await page.goto(`http://127.0.0.1:${port}/allslides`, {
    waitUntil: "networkidle0",
    timeout: 30_000,
  });

  // Wait for the last slide element to be present in the DOM.
  await page.waitForSelector(".slide:last-child", { timeout: 15_000 });

  // Extra settle time for CSS animations and web fonts.
  await wait(1500);

  // ── Inject print CSS ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  // The App root wrapper has `height: 100vh; overflow: hidden` which clamps
  // everything to one viewport. Override those constraints so all 15 slides are
  // in the printable flow, then add a page break after each one.
  await page.addStyleTag({
    content: `
      /* Remove viewport clamp from App root and the AllSlides wrapper */
      html, body {
        height: auto !important;
        overflow: visible !important;
      }
      /* Target the App root div and AllSlides wrapper div */
      #root > div,
      #root > div > div {
        height: auto !important;
        overflow: visible !important;
      }
      /* Each slide occupies exactly one printed page */
      .slide {
        break-after: page !important;
        page-break-after: always !important;
        /* Keep the explicit pixel dimensions so each page is exactly 1920×1080 */
        width: 1920px !important;
        height: 1080px !important;
        overflow: hidden !important;
      }
      /* No blank trailing page */
      .slide:last-child {
        break-after: avoid !important;
        page-break-after: avoid !important;
      }
    `,
  });

  const slideCount = await page.$$eval(".slide", (els) => els.length);
  console.log(`✓ Detected ${slideCount} slides.`);

  console.log(`▶ Exporting PDF → ${outPath}`);
  await page.pdf({
    path: outPath,
    width: "1920px",
    height: "1080px",
    printBackground: true,
    landscape: false, // dimensions are already landscape (wider than tall)
  });

  console.log(`✓ PDF written: ${outPath}`);
} finally {
  if (browser) await browser.close();
  server.kill("SIGTERM");
}
